Show who created, changed, moved, linked or removed which node, and when (administrators only) administrators only · reads only audit [--user=<string>] [--id=<string>] [--record=<string>] [--cause=<string>] [--op=<string>] [--since=<string>] [--until=<string>] [--type=<string>] [--after=<string>] [-n <string>] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> only writes to this path or below it (moves match on either side) Option What it does --user=<string> only writes by this user (name or uid) --id=<string> only writes to this node id. --record=<string> only the record with this id. --cause=<string> only writes set off by the write with this record id: what its pipeline runs wrote. --op=<string> only this operation: create, update, move, link, unlink, delete. --since=<string> from this time on (ISO date/time or epoch ms) --until=<string> before this time (ISO date/time or epoch ms) --type=<string> only writes to nodes of this type (repeatable) --after=<string> only the records after this record id, oldest first: pass the last id read to follow the trail. -n <string> at most this many records, the latest, or with --after the first (default: 100) -v show each record's id, session or pipeline run, cause, and the values it changed.

Pattern scanning and text processing language (fields, patterns, arrays, printf) reads only awk [-F <string>] [-v <string>] [-f <string>] <PROGRAM> <FILE>... Argument What it is <PROGRAM> awk program, e.g. '{ print $1 }' or 'BEGIN { FS=":" } $3 > 10 { n++ } END { print n }'; omit when using -f. <FILE>... files to process, or var=value assignments (reads stdin if no files) Option What it does -F <string> field separator (a character, "t" for tab, or a regex) -v <string> assign var=value before the program starts (repeatable) -f <string> read the program from this file (repeatable)

Strip directory and suffix from filenames. reads only basename [-s <string>] [-a] [-z] <NAME> <SUFFIX> Argument What it is <NAME> the path to extract basename from. <SUFFIX> optional suffix to remove. Option What it does -s <string> remove a trailing SUFFIX. -a support multiple arguments. -z end each output line with NUL, not newline.

Print nodes' contents, one after the other: a text file, a log (one JSON entry a line), a position or an embedding (JSON) reads only cat [-s] [-l] [-t] [--timestamps] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... nodes to output, one after the other; without one, or for -, stdin is copied. Option What it does -s small media preview (mediaLines / 2) -l large media preview (mediaLines * 2) -t log: each entry's time (ISO 8601, UTC) first, a tab, then the entry. --timestamps log: each entry's time (ISO 8601, UTC) first, a tab, then the entry. cat /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/notes.txt cat -t /archive/people/Anna_Exempel/measurements/weight With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the node's contents; with -t on a log, lines like 2016-09-04T16:13:27.739Z {"value":83.4}.

Change file mode bits. changes things chmod [-L] [-r] <mode> <path> Argument What it is <mode> mode to set. <path> node(s) to change. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links. -r apply to the whole subtree, skipping nodes that hold their own access.

Change file owner and group. changes things chown [-L] [-r] <usergroup> <path> Argument What it is <usergroup> user or group to set. <path> node(s) to change. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links. -r apply to the whole subtree, skipping nodes that hold their own access.
Clear the terminal screen. reads only clear

Manage comments on a node (list, add, remove) reads only comment [--body=<string>] [--body-base64=<string>] <subcommand> <path> <slug> Argument What it is <subcommand> list | add | remove. <path> node the comment belongs to. <slug> comment slug (remove) Option What it does --body=<string> comment body (add) --body-base64=<string> base64-encoded comment body (add)
Spec-driven completion helpers. completion <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Autocomplete a command argument. reads only completion-arg [--word=<string>] Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.
Autocomplete a command name, without the subcommands of groups. reads only completion-commands [--word=<string>] Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.

Complete a person, location, album, device or track by name. reads only completion-entity [--kind=<string>] [--limit=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> the partial name typed so far. Option What it does --kind=<string> restrict to these kinds, comma-separated: whichever the installed modules declare (person, location, album, device, track) --limit=<string> maximum suggestions (default 8)
Autocomplete a group. reads only completion-group [--word=<string>] Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.
Autocomplete a path. reads only completion-path [--word=<string>] Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.

Autocomplete a command. reads only completion-subcommand [--word=<string>] <command> Argument What it is <command> Command to which the subcommand belongs. Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.
Autocomplete a user. reads only completion-user [--word=<string>] Option What it does --word=<string> Word to autocomplete.
Read and change system and personal settings. visitors too config <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Print the effective value of one setting; for a key, only whether it is set. reads only config-get <key> Argument What it is <key> setting name.
List settings with their effective values. visitors too · reads only config-list [--scope=<string>] Option What it does --scope=<string> limit to 'system' or 'user' settings.
Copy settings from this process's environment into /etc/environment. changes things config-publish
Change a setting and restart the services that read it only at start. changes things config-set <key> <value> Argument What it is <key> setting name. <value> new value.
Reset a setting to its default. changes things config-unset <key> Argument What it is <key> setting name.

Copy files and directories. changes things cp [-r] [-f] <source> <dest> Argument What it is <source> source file(s) or directories to copy. <dest> destination: an existing directory (or other node that is not a file) to copy into, or the path of a single source, replacing a file there. Option What it does -r copy directories recursively. -f replace a node of the same name in the destination directory; a file named as DEST is replaced without it. cp /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007_copy.jpg cp -r /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_A /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_B With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Remove sections from each line of files. reads only cut [-d <string>] [-f <string>] [-c <string>] [-s] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to cut, one after the other (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -d <string> use DELIM instead of TAB for field delimiter. -f <string> select only these fields (e.g., -f1, -f1-3, -f1,3) -c <string> select only these characters (e.g., -c1-5) -s do not print lines not containing delimiters.

Print or set the system date and time. reads only date [-d <string>] [-u] [-I <string>] [-R] <+FORMAT> Argument What it is <+FORMAT> output format (strftime-style) Option What it does -d <string> display time described by STRING, not now. -u print or set UTC time. -I <string> output in ISO 8601 format (date, hours, minutes, seconds, ns) -R output in RFC 5322 format.

detach a job so it keeps running after the shell closes. changes things detach [--list] <job> Argument What it is <job> job spec (%n), job number, or pid; defaults to the most recent job. Option What it does --list list detached jobs system-wide instead, from their records under /var/logs/jobs.
Free space per storage tier, its growth per day and when it fills, and the database size. reads only df
Strip last component from file name. reads only dirname [-z] <NAME> Argument What it is <NAME> the path to extract directory from. Option What it does -z end each output line with NUL, not newline.

Print system log. reads only dmesg [-n <string>] [--level=<string>] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] log node path (default: /var/logs/system) Option What it does -n <string> show last N lines. --level=<string> only lines at this level or above: debug, info, warn, error.
Describe what this installation is made of: its commands, node types and environment variables. docs <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

List every command on your PATH with its full spec and the module it comes from. reads only docs-commands docs commands With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One entry per command: name, module (core or the module whose bin it is) and its whole spec.

List the environment variables EiN and its modules read, with their values in this shell. reads only docs-env docs env docs env | grep PATH With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One entry per variable: key, kind, description, default, owner module, and its value in this shell where it has one.

Commands by what they do, best first: by the command CFG_COMMAND_FINDER names, else by their words. reads only docs-find [--limit=<number>] <words>... Argument What it is <words>... What the command should do. Option What it does --limit=<number> How many commands.

List every node type, described or in use, with what it is for and how many exist. reads only docs-node-types docs node-types With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One entry per type: type, count, and label, description, category and owner module where it is described.

Estimate file usage in node structures. reads only du [-c] [-h] [-s] <path> Argument What it is <path> one or more structures to measure (default: .) Option What it does -c print a grand total. -h print sizes in units of 1024 (e.g. 1.5 KB) -s print only a total for each argument. du -sh /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the size of each path, and a total with -c.
Edit a text file, with syntax highlighting and checks for JSON, YAML, bash and Markdown. changes things edit <path> Argument What it is <path> path to file to edit.
Print environment variables. reads only env

What falls on the days around a date, from every events-* command on PATH. reads only events [--today=<string>] [--days-ahead=<number>] [--days-past=<number>] [--limit=<number>] Option What it does --today=<string> the date to look around, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, UTC) --days-ahead=<number> how far forward to look (default 30) --days-past=<number> how far back to look (default 7) --limit=<number> entries returned across all providers; milestones, then the nearest, survive the cut (default 16) events events --days-ahead 0 --days-past 0 events --today 2026-12-24 --days-ahead 7 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the entries of every events-* provider in the window, in date order: the day, what, whether it is a milestone, the node it is about, which provider, and the route that draws it.

Bucket counts (per year, per kind) for sizing search filters. reads only facets [--kind=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] Option What it does --kind=<string> restrict to content kinds: photo, video, audio, document, or node types. --from=<string> only count media taken at/after this date. --to=<string> only count media taken before this date, exclusive. facets --kind photo --from 2015 --to 2020 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : per-year and per-kind counts for the filters given.

Stat for on disk file. reads only file-stat [-f] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -f return full information, including mimetype, sha256, much slower. file-stat /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the file's size, mode and times as they are on disk.

Sync for on disk file. changes things file-sync <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. file-sync /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the node's size and checksum are brought in line with the bytes on disk.

Search for nodes under a path, as GNU find does: starting points, then an expression of tests (-name -iname -path -ipath GLOB, -regex -iregex RE on the whole path, -type f|d|l| , -empty, -size [+-]N[cwbkMG], -user -group NAME, -uid -gid N, -newer PATH, -mmin and -mtime [+-]N), operators (! -not -a -o and parentheses), options (-maxdepth -mindepth N, -depth) and actions (-print -print0 -printf FORMAT -prune -quit -delete, -exec CMD {} ';' and -exec CMD {} +); -printf knows %p %f %h %P %d %s %y %m %u %g %U %G %t %c and %Tk %Ck %Bk for k in @YymdHMSFTDab+; the flags below are the same tests. reads only find [--name=<string>] [--iname=<string>] [--type=<string>] [--maxdepth=<string>] [--mindepth=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> starting point, printed itself at depth 0; several may be given (default: .) Option What it does --name=<string> match the name by glob pattern (-name) --iname=<string> match the name by glob pattern, ignoring case (-iname) --type=<string> node type: f, d, l or one such as person; several comma-separated (-type) --maxdepth=<string> descend at most this many levels: 0 is the starting point alone (-maxdepth) --mindepth=<string> match nothing shallower than this level: 1 leaves out the starting point (-mindepth) find /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 -name '*.jpg' - type f find /archive/people -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 - type person find /home/anna/staging -name '.tmp*' -prune -o - type f -mmin -60 - print find /home/anna/staging - type f -size +10M - printf '%s %p\n' find /home/anna/staging -name '*.tmp' - exec rm {} + With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every path -print selects; in JSON each with its type, name and number of children. With -printf, -print0 or -exec the output is text.

Find positions whose shape contains a point. reads only find-containing [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--limit=<string>] <lat> <lng> Argument What it is <lat> latitude of the point. <lng> longitude of the point. Option What it does --lat=<string> latitude, as --lat= — required form for a negative coordinate. --lng=<string> longitude, as --lng= — required form for a negative coordinate. --limit=<string> max results (default: 10)

Find positions near a position node, by distance. reads only find-nearby [--radius=<string>] [--limit=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> path of a position node. Option What it does --radius=<string> search radius in meters (default: 10000) --limit=<string> max results (default: 10)

Find similar nodes by embedding. reads only find-similar [--limit=<number>] <path> Argument What it is <path> path of embedding node. Option What it does --limit=<number> at most this many matches. With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the nearest embeddings with their similarity and paths, as JSON (SimilarAnswer).

Wrap each input line to fit a width (fold -w1: one character per line) reads only fold [-w <number>] [-s] [-b] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to fold (reads from stdin if omitted) Option What it does -w <number> width in columns (default 80) -s break at the last blank that fits. -b count characters, not columns (tabs count one)
List the gauges running services draw beside the host's (a card's memory, say) reads only gauges

Search for patterns in input. reads only grep [-i] [-v] [-c] [-n] [-o] [-E] [-F] [-q] <PATTERN> <FILE>... Argument What it is <PATTERN> the pattern to search for. <FILE>... files to search (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -i ignore case distinctions. -v select non-matching lines. -c print only a count of matching lines. -n prefix each line with line number. -o show only the matching part of lines. -E interpret pattern as extended regexp. -F interpret pattern as fixed string. -q quiet mode, exit with 0 on match, 1 otherwise. grep -n exempelord /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/notes.txt With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the matching lines.
Manage groups. group <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Add a user to a group. administrators only · changes things group-add-member <group> <user> Argument What it is <group> group to add the user to. <user> user to add to the group.

Create a new group. administrators only · changes things group-create [--gid=<string>] [--title=<string>] [--description=<string>] <groupname> Argument What it is <groupname> name of the group to create: letters, digits and . _ - @, starting with a letter or _. Option What it does --gid=<string> numeric group ID. --title=<string> display title for the group. --description=<string> description of the group.

Delete a group: what it owned goes to another group, and ACL entries naming it are dropped. administrators only · changes things group-delete [--to=<group>] [--force] <groupname> Argument What it is <groupname> name of the group to delete. Option What it does --to=<group> group that takes over the nodes it owned (default admin) --force delete it even if it is a primary group; those users go back to their own group.
Check if a group exists. reads only group-exists <groupname> Argument What it is <groupname> group name to check.
Display group information. reads only group-info <groupname> Argument What it is <groupname> group name to look up.
Check if a user is a member of a group. reads only group-is-member <group> <user> Argument What it is <group> group to check if the user is member of. <user> user to check.

List the groups; as JSON with each one's description and built-in role. reads only group-list [--members] Option What it does --members also list the usernames linked into each group, where the caller may see them (a primary group's users are not linked)

List members of a group. administrators only · reads only group-members [--limit=<string>] <group> Argument What it is <group> group to list members of. Option What it does --limit=<string> maximum members to return (1-50)
Remove a user from a group. administrators only · changes things group-remove-member <group> <user> Argument What it is <group> group to remove the user from. <user> user to remove from the group.
Resolve group name to GID or vice versa. reads only group-resolve <gid_or_groupname> Argument What it is <gid_or_groupname> gid (numeric) or group name to resolve.

Update a group's title or description; its gid is fixed when it is created. administrators only · changes things group-update [--title=<string>] [--description=<string>] <groupname> Argument What it is <groupname> name of the group to update. Option What it does --title=<string> set display title. --description=<string> set description.

Output the first part of files, logs, or stdin; on a queue, the next entries without consuming them. reads only head [-n <string>] [-c <string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> file, log or queue node to read (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -n <string> print the first NUM lines instead of the first 10 (-NUM works too) -c <string> print the first NUM bytes. head -n 20 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/notes.txt With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the first lines of the file.
Say whether the system is healthy, catching up, stuck or needs a person, and the checks that decide it. reads only health

The machine's CPU, this container's memory and event-loop lag now, with their recent history from metrics-sampler. reads only host-metrics [--window=<string>] Option What it does --window=<string> Minutes of history (default: 360)

Start an HTTP server. administrators only · changes things http-server [--port=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to serve as root, "default" in root will be used as the default host. Option What it does --port=<string> port to use.
Display node ID and type. reads only info [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links.

Lightweight JSON processor. reads only jq [-r] [-e] [-c] [-C] [-M] [-S] <filter> <FILE>... Argument What it is <filter> jq filter expression (e.g., .field, .field.nested, .[] | .name, startswith("x")); . if omitted. <FILE>... files of JSON texts (one, or JSON Lines), each text filtered in turn (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -r output raw strings, not JSON texts. -e exit with status 1 if output is null or false. -c compact instead of pretty-printed output. -C colorize JSON output even when not on a terminal. -M do not colorize JSON output. -S Output the fields of each object with the keys in sorted order.

Manage labels/tags (add, remove, list, prune) reads only label <subcommand> <path> <label> Argument What it is <subcommand> add | remove | list | prune. <path> node path. <label> label name(s) label add /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg exempeletikett label list /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : for list , the labels on the node; for add and remove , nothing.

List labels (all, or of a node); search --tag finds what carries one. reads only labels <path> Argument What it is <path> node path (optional) labels labels /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : without a path, every label in use with how many nodes carry it ({ label, count }); with one, the labels on that node.

Create links between files. changes things ln [-s] [-f] <target> <link_name> Argument What it is <target> target of the link. <link_name> name of the link to create. Option What it does -s make symbolic links instead of hard links. -f remove existing destination files. ln -s /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg /home/anna/favourite.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Append a JSON entry to a log, optionally at an explicit (backdated) timestamp. changes things log-append [--data=<string>] [--at=<string>] <log> <data> Argument What it is <log> VFS path to the log node. <data> JSON entry (alternative to --data) Option What it does --data=<string> JSON payload for the entry. --at=<string> ISO timestamp to backdate the entry to.

Authenticate as a user. visitors too · changes things login [--session] <username> <password> Argument What it is <username> user to login: a username, or the e-mail address of an account. <password> password (optional, prompts if not provided) Option What it does --session login session not just shell.
Log out of the current session. visitors too · changes things logout [--session] Option What it does --session logout session not just shell.

List directory contents. reads only ls [-l] [-a] [-A] [-r] [-L] [-C] [-1] [-h] [--limit=<string>] [--after=<string>] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... paths to list, each under its own header when there are several. Option What it does -l use a long listing format. -a do not ignore entries starting with . -A do not ignore entries starting with . except for . and .. -r reverse order while sorting. -L do not follow symbolic links. -C include each entry's own child names (extra lookup, JSON output only) -1 list one entry per line, also on a terminal. -h with -l, print file sizes in units of 1024 (e.g. 1.5 KB) --limit=<string> list one page of this many entries, in the store's name order. --after=<string> with --limit, the page after this name: the last one of the page before. ls -l /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files ls /archive/people ls -l -- limit 200 --after IMG_0412.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the directory's entries; for several paths, an object of each path's entries.

Who is in a container: an album's members by its rules, or a directory's media. reads only members <path> Argument What it is <path> The container. members /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 members /archive/tags/segling With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every member's path, node id and, for a member held by a link, the link; with a type's own command (members- ), also which member stands for a folded group.

Sample host, storage and workload metrics into /var/logs/metrics (long-running) administrators only · changes things metrics-sampler [--interval=<string>] Option What it does --interval=<string> Seconds between ticks (default: shortest series cadence)
Show stored, extension-based and content-sniffed mimetype of a node. reads only mime <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node.
Create a buffer node. changes things mkbuf mkbuf /tmp/exempelbuffert With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the buffer node is created.
Create a directory node (-p to create parents) changes things mkdir mkdir -p /archive/albums/Nytt_Exempelalbum/files With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the directory is created.

Create an empty text file node (what touch does elsewhere) changes things mkfile <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the new file. mkfile /home/exempel/anteckning.txt With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; an empty text file node is created.

Create a log node. changes things mklog [--routing-keys=<string>] [--retention=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the log node. Option What it does --routing-keys=<string> , -k Comma-separated routing keys to bind to. --retention=<string> , -r Retention policy (default: forever, e.g. 7 day, 100 entries)

Create new or ensure node. changes things mknode [-p] [-t <string>] [--under=<string>] [--tier=<string>] [--as=<string>] [--an=<number>] [--aj=<string>] [--al=<string>] [-m <string>] [-o <string>] [-g <string>] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... node path to create; repeatable. Option What it does -p if the path already exists, do nothing. -t <string> type of node to make, required. --under=<string> existing node the path must sit under; bounds what -p may create. --tier=<string> storage tier for a file's bytes: disk, volatile or db; fixed once created. --as=<string> set attribute as string. --an=<number> set attribute as number. --aj=<string> set attribute as JSON. --al=<string> set attribute as comma-separated list. -m <string> mode to set. -o <string> owner as uid or user name. -g <string> group as gid or group name.

Create a pool node. changes things mkpool [--aging-seconds=<string>] [--aging-boost=<string>] [--aging-max=<string>] [--lease-ms=<string>] [--max-attempts=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the pool node. Option What it does --aging-seconds=<string> , -a Queue age per aging step (0 disables aging) --aging-boost=<string> , -b Effective-priority points per aging step. --aging-max=<string> , -m Total aging cap; keep below the gap between priority lanes. --lease-ms=<string> , -l Default lease duration in ms. --max-attempts=<string> , -n Default attempts before a job fails.

Create a queue node. changes things mkqueue [--routing-keys=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the queue node. Option What it does --routing-keys=<string> , -k Comma-separated routing keys to bind to.

Create a router node. changes things mkrouter [--routing-key=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the router node. Option What it does --routing-key=<string> , -k Routing key for fan-out broadcasting (required)
Module management. mod <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Pre-fetch a module's TypeScript command dependencies. administrators only · changes things mod-cache <name> Argument What it is <name> Module name (directory name under /modules)

Say which groups a module is kept to, or keep it to some groups, or make it everyone's again. administrators only · reads only mod-groups [--everyone] <name> <group>... Argument What it is <name> The module. <group>... Keep it to these groups: on their PATH and in their navigation alone, its commands refused to anyone else. Option What it does --everyone Make it everyone's again. mod groups archive mod groups archive family friends mod groups archive --everyone With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : The module and the groups it is kept to, none when it is everyone's.
Show module information. reads only mod-info <name> Argument What it is <name> Module name.

Install modules from their repositories, or update them, with the dependencies they lack, and set them up. administrators only · changes things mod-install [--force] [--missing] [--groups=<string>] [--no-setup] <module>... Argument What it is <module>... A published module by name (archive), or its repository ( https://github.com/einhq/module-archive ), either with @branch, @tag or @commit (its id whole, or its first seven characters or more) Option What it does --force Fetch again what is installed at the same commit, and update even when an installed module does not accept the new version. --missing Install only modules not installed at all, leaving an installed one as it is without asking its forge. --groups=<string> Keep the modules named to these groups, comma-separated, as mod groups does; the dependencies it installs with them are everyone's. --no-setup Put the modules in place without setting them up or starting their services, as boot does before its own mod setup --all.
List installed modules, those kept to groups only for their members and administrators. reads only mod-list [--long] Option What it does --long Show detailed information.
Uninstall a module. administrators only · changes things mod-remove [--force] <name> Argument What it is <name> Module name. Option What it does --force Skip confirmation prompt.

The published modules: each module-* repository of the module sources (CFG_MODULE_SOURCES), with its version and whether it is installed. reads only mod-search <words>... Argument What it is <words>... Words the name or description must hold.

Set up a module already in the modules directory. administrators only · changes things mod-setup <name> Argument What it is <name> Module name (directory name under /modules), or --all for every module in dependency order.

Mount a filesystem. changes things mount [--save] [-a] <path> <type> <options> Argument What it is <path> mount point. <type> type: memory, pg, filesystem, command, sftp. <options> k=v,... — any: readonly, noaudit (paths, separated by : , whose writes the audit trail skips); sftp: host, port, user, path, key (identity file), hostkey (SHA256:… to pin), uid, gid. Option What it does --save also record the mount in /etc/fstab, so boot mounts it again. -a mount every /etc/fstab entry not mounted yet. mount mount --save /mnt/nas sftp "host=nas.local,user=anna,path=/srv/photos" mount /mnt/backup sftp "host=backup.example.com,port=2222,key=/home/admin/.ssh/backup,readonly" mount -a

Move or rename files and directories, re-pointing the softlinks at each moved path or anywhere under it (and a relation link’s peerLink with them) changes things mv [--no-clobber] [--no-relink] <source> <dest> Argument What it is <source> the files or directories to move; several go into DEST, which must exist. <dest> destination: an existing node that is not a file to move into, or the new path of a single source, replacing a file there. Option What it does --no-clobber Do not overwrite an existing file - fails if destination already exists (-n) --no-relink Leave the softlinks that point at or under each moved source on its old path. mv /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/nytt_namn.jpg mv /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-16 /home/anna/staging/files/scans/ With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : in JSON mode, MvAnswer: how many sources moved, how many softlinks were re-pointed, and each source that did not move with why. Exits non-zero only when no source moved.

What has been added lately, newest first, from every news-* command on PATH. reads only news [--limit=<number>] Option What it does --limit=<number> entries returned, across all providers (default 8) news news -- limit 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the newest entries of every news-* provider together: when, what, who did it, the node it is about, which provider, and the route that draws it.
run a command detached, immune to shell hang-up, logging to /var/logs/jobs. changes things nohup <command> Argument What it is <command> the command (and args) to run detached.

What the archive has from a calendar day (MM-DD, default today) in earlier years, from every onthisday-* command on PATH. reads only onthisday [--limit=<number>] <day> Argument What it is <day> day as MM-DD (default today, UTC) Option What it does --limit=<number> entries returned across all providers (default 8) onthisday onthisday 06-21 -- limit 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the entries of every onthisday-* provider, newest year first: the year, what, the node it is about, which provider, and the route that draws it.

A search's words read as filters — subjects, an area, years, kinds — by the command CFG_SEARCH_PARSER names, or as words when it names none. reads only parse-search [--rules] <words>... Argument What it is <words>... What was typed into the search box. Option What it does --rules The parser's fast pass only, without its model.
Manage pipelines. pipeline <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Cancel a running pipeline. administrators only · changes things pipeline-cancel <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID.
Register a pipeline definition from a YAML file. administrators only · changes things pipeline-define <path> Argument What it is <path> Path to pipeline YAML file.
Run the pipeline engine (long-running) administrators only · changes things pipeline-engine

Rerun failed instances after a growing wait, and mark those that keep failing for a person. administrators only · reads only pipeline-heal [--apply] [--now] [--limit=<number>] Option What it does --apply Rerun and mark (default is a dry run) --now Skip the waits: the cause is known to have passed. --limit=<number> Failed instances to look at, oldest first (default 500)

List pipeline instances — running, failed or completed — newest first. reads only pipeline-instances [-s <string>] [--limit=<string>] [--after=<string>] <name> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name (optional, repeatable) Option What it does -s <string> Filter by status. --limit=<string> Page size (default 100) --after=<string> Keyset cursor from a previous page ( : )
List pipeline definitions. reads only pipeline-list
Pipeline workload summary: instance counts (running, failed, completed), queue depths, active instances, completion rate. reads only pipeline-overview

Remove terminal pipeline instances (completed/failed/cancelled) administrators only · changes things pipeline-prune [-s <string>] [--all] [--keep=<string>] [--max=<string>] [--older-than=<string>] [--budget=<string>] <name> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name (optional; all if omitted) Option What it does -s <string> Only remove instances with this status. --all Remove all instances, including running (cancels first) --keep=<string> Retention cap: keep this many newest per pipeline, remove the rest. --max=<string> Stop after removing this many per pipeline (with --keep or --older-than) --older-than=<string> Retention by age: remove those completed longer ago than this, e.g. 30d. --budget=<string> Stop starting new pages after this long, e.g. 15m (with --keep or --older-than)

Remove pipeline instances (cancels running ones first) administrators only · changes things pipeline-remove [-f] <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID(s) Option What it does -f Ignore instances that are not found.

Return instances marked terminal while still holding unfinished steps to running. administrators only · reads only pipeline-repair [--apply] Option What it does --apply Perform the repair (default is a dry run)
Rerun pipeline(s) from the current definition, replacing the old instance. administrators only · changes things pipeline-rerun <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID(s)
Restart a failed pipeline (re-queue failed steps) administrators only · changes things pipeline-restart <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID.

Manually start a pipeline. administrators only · changes things pipeline-start [--var=<string>] <name> <path> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name. <path> Target path to process. Option What it does --var=<string> Override a declared variable for this run: NAME=VALUE (repeatable)
Show pipeline instance status. reads only pipeline-status <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID.
Restart a single pipeline step. administrators only · changes things pipeline-step-restart <id> <step> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID. <step> Step name.
Remove a pipeline definition, and cancel its running instances. administrators only · changes things pipeline-undefine <name> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name to undefine.

Run a pool worker (long-running) administrators only · changes things pipeline-worker [--pool=<path>] [--capacity=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--reserve-kind=<string>] [--reserve-capacity=<string>] [--kind-quantum=<number>] [--lease=<number>] [--concurrency=<number>] Option What it does --pool=<path> Pool node path to claim from. --capacity=<string> Capacity offered to the pool, key=number (repeatable) --kind=<string> Only claim these job kinds (repeatable) --reserve-kind=<string> Prefer these kinds within reserved capacity (repeatable) --reserve-capacity=<string> Soft capacity reservation, key=number (repeatable) --kind-quantum=<number> Batch by kind: drain one kind for this many ms before rotating (default 0, off) --lease=<number> Lease duration in ms (default 60000) --concurrency=<number> Upper bound on concurrent jobs (default 1)
Manage work pools. pool <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Add a job to a pool. administrators only · changes things pool-add [--kind=<string>] [--priority=<string>] [--requires=<string>] [--params=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--exclusive=<string>] [--attempts=<string>] [--delay=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --kind=<string> Capability class the job needs (required) --priority=<string> Higher runs first (default 0) --requires=<string> Resource vector, key=number (repeatable or comma-separated) --params=<string> JSON payload handed to the worker. --key=<string> Dedup key; re-adding a live one updates it instead of duplicating. --exclusive=<string> Mutex class; one claimed job per class at a time. --attempts=<string> Attempts before the job fails. --delay=<string> Hold the job back this long (e.g. 30s, 5m)

Cancel pending or claimed jobs. administrators only · changes things pool-cancel [--job=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--prefix=<string>] [--kind=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --job=<string> Cancel one job by id. --key=<string> Cancel the job with this dedup key. --prefix=<string> Cancel every job whose dedup key starts with this. --kind=<string> Cancel every job of this kind.

Claim the best matching job from a pool under a lease. administrators only · changes things pool-claim [--owner=<string>] [--offer=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--lease=<string>] [--wait] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --owner=<string> Lease owner (default derives from the session) --offer=<string> Available capacity, key=number (repeatable or comma-separated) --kind=<string> Only consider these kinds (repeatable) --lease=<string> Lease duration (default 30s) --wait Block until a job is claimable.

List jobs in a pool. reads only pool-list [--state=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--after=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --state=<string> Filter by state (comma-separated) --kind=<string> Filter by kind. --limit=<string> Page size (default 100) --after=<string> Keyset cursor from a previous page (job id)

Delete finished jobs so a pool does not grow without bound. administrators only · changes things pool-purge [--state=<string>] [--older-than=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --state=<string> States to drop (default done,failed,cancelled) --older-than=<string> Only drop jobs finished longer ago than this (e.g. 7d)

Return failed or cancelled jobs to the pool with a clean attempt count. administrators only · changes things pool-retry [--job=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--prefix=<string>] [--kind=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --job=<string> Retry one job by id. --key=<string> Retry the job with this dedup key. --prefix=<string> Retry every job whose dedup key starts with this. --kind=<string> Retry every job of this kind.
Show a pool backlog, job counts, policy and throughput per job kind; every pool without a path. reads only pool-stat [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] Pool node path (default: every pool)
Try resting job kinds again now, every resting kind without a name. administrators only · changes things pool-wake [<kind>...] Argument What it is [<kind>...] Job kind to wake (repeatable)

Where nodes are: each path's name, type and the shape of its position (a location's, a picture's GPS) reads only position-get <path>... Argument What it is <path>... the nodes, or position nodes themselves. position-get /archive/locations/Exempelviken /archive/albums/Sommar/files/IMG_0001.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nodes: one per path, in order — path, name, type and position (lat, lng, and radius or polygon) when it has one; error for a path that cannot be read.

Set the shape of a position node (point, circle or polygon), making the node when it is missing. changes things position-set [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--radius=<string>] [--polygon=<string>] [--clear] <path> Argument What it is <path> path of the position node, such as /position. Option What it does --lat=<string> latitude of the center point. --lng=<string> longitude of the center point. --radius=<string> circle radius in meters. --polygon=<string> polygon ring as JSON: [{"lat":..,"lng":..},...]. --clear clear the stored shape.
Display node properties. reads only props [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links.

List the commands running now: pid, user, shell, how long, and the command line. Admin sees everyone's, anyone else their own. reads only ps [--user=<user>] Option What it does --user=<user> Only this user's commands (-u) ps ps --user anna With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One row per running command, oldest first.

List the entries a queue set aside after their delivery attempts, or retry or drop them. reads only queue-dead [--retry] [--drop] [--id=<string>] [-n <string>] [--limit=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Queue node path. Option What it does --retry put them back in line with no attempts spent. --drop delete them. --id=<string> only this entry, with --retry or --drop (repeatable) -n <string> how many entries to list (default 10) --limit=<string> how many entries to list (default 10) queue-dead /var/queues/archive-bridge queue-dead --retry /var/queues/archive-bridge queue-dead --drop -- id 42 /var/queues/archive-bridge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the dead-lettered entries: id, attempts, created, dead, routing key and data; in JSON mode { items }. With --retry or --drop, how many were settled; in JSON mode { ok, settled }.

List the next entries of a queue without consuming them. reads only queue-peek [-n <string>] [--limit=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Queue node path. Option What it does -n <string> how many entries, from the front (default 10) --limit=<string> how many entries, from the front (default 10) queue-peek -n 20 /var/queues/pipeline-engine With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the next entries in delivery order: id, state (ready or in-flight), attempts, created, routing key and data; in JSON mode { items }.

Check stored reach against a walk of each path, for a sample of nodes and every account. reads only reach-check [--sample=<string>] Option What it does --sample=<string> how many nodes to judge (default 2000)

Create a bidirectional relation between two nodes. changes things relate [--reverse=<string>] <a> <b> <label> Argument What it is <a> first node. <b> second node. <label> relation label (both sides unless --reverse) Option What it does --reverse=<string> label for the b -> a side (default: same as label)
Remove reciprocal relation links when one side is deleted (long-running) administrators only · changes things relations-guard
Resolve node ID to path. reads only resolve-id <id> Argument What it is <id> id of node.
Reverse lines character-wise. reads only rev <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to reverse, one after the other (stdin if omitted, or for -)

Remove (delete) files or directories. changes things rm [-r] [-f] [-d] <path> Argument What it is <path> node(s) to remove. Option What it does -r remove nodes and their contents recursively. -f ignore nonexistent nodes and arguments. -d remove empty directories (what rm without -r already does) rm /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg rm -r /archive/albums/Tomt_Exempelalbum With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Remove empty directories. changes things rmdir [-p] <path> Argument What it is <path> empty directory node(s) to remove. Option What it does -p also remove each parent the path names, as each becomes empty. rmdir /home/exempel/tomt rmdir -p /home/exempel/utkast/2019/juni With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Copy files between EiN and another machine over SSH (members of group ssh) changes things scp [-r] [-p] [-q] [-B] [-P <number>] [-i <path>] [-F <path>] [-o <string>] <source>... <target> Argument What it is <source>... files to copy: EiN paths, or [user@]host:path. <target> where to: an EiN path, or [user@]host:path. Option What it does -r copy directories recursively. -p keep modes and modification times. -q no progress meter. -B batch mode: never ask for passwords or passphrases. -P <number> port (default 22) -i <path> identity file. -F <path> config file (default ~/.ssh/config; none: no file) -o <string> ssh option, e.g. StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new. scp anna@nas.local:photos/sailboat.jpg "/archive/albums/Summer 2020/" scp "anna@nas.local:photos/*.jpg" "/archive/albums/Summer 2020/" scp -r "/archive/albums/Summer 2020" anna@nas.local:backup/ With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; 1 when any file failed.

Faceted search over content: text, time, region, kind, tags, subjects (people, locations, devices) and containers. reads only search [-l <number>] [--limit=<number>] [--kind=<string>] [--tag=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--after=<string>] [--before=<string>] [--creator=<string>] [--subject=<string>] [--subject-name=<string>] [--under=<path>] [--include-stacked] [--within=<path>] [--undated] [--missing=<string>] [--like=<path>] [--bbox=<string>] [--circle=<string>] [--polygon=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--at=<string>] [--facets] [--group-by=<string>] [--layout] [--cursor=<string>] [--above=<string>] [--max-scan=<number>] [--fields=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> search query text (optional) Option What it does -l <number> page size (default 60, max 200) --limit=<number> page size (default 60, max 200) --kind=<string> content kind, comma-separated: photo, video, audio, document, or a node type (album, person, location, …) --tag=<string> filter by label (repeatable, intersected) --from=<string> taken at/after this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01) --to=<string> taken before this date, exclusive (--to 2000 includes all of 2000) --after=<string> alias for --from. --before=<string> alias for --to. --creator=<string> media created (uploaded or imported) by a user, by name or uid. --subject=<string> media a subject has, as : (person:anna-exempel, location:…, device:…) or a path; any kind a subject- command answers for (repeatable, intersected). For a town or country use --bbox from location-region. --subject-name=<string> media of any subject of a kind whose name matches, as : (person:anna); repeatable groups intersect. --under=<path> media held by one album or directory (its own level; softlink members followed) --include-stacked with --under, include hidden stack members (internal aggregate mode) --within=<path> media anywhere in the tree under this directory, at any depth; by time, with the undated after the dated when there is no date window. Inside an unlisted tree (staging) it lists what the library's searches leave out. --undated only media with no capture time, in the order it arrived. --missing=<string> only what lacks this attr, dotted for a nested one (duplicate.deferred); repeatable, each must be missing. --like=<path> rank by how much each picture looks like this photo or video (more like this), or like a label's tag directory (/archive/tags/ , by its model), instead of by words; the other filters still narrow it. --bbox=<string> region as north,south,east,west. --circle=<string> region as lat,lng,radiusMeters. --polygon=<string> region as "lat,lng;lat,lng;lat,lng". --sort=<string> score | time | -time | name (default: score with a query, name for timeless kinds, -time otherwise) --at=<string> start the page at this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01); needs a time sort. --facets answer with per-year, per-month, per-kind and per-label counts instead of results. --group-by=<string> answer with the groups holding the matches, counted and dated, instead of results: the nearest ancestors of these node types (album), or the subjects of these kinds the matches have (person: who is in them, and how many of them show someone nobody has named) --layout answer with one compact complete layout index for a container or a subject (JSON only) --cursor=<string> resume token from a previous page (a position, for --subject/--under) --above=<string> the page ending just above this resume token — walking up a time-ordered browse. --max-scan=<number> candidates to examine before giving up (default 5000); store-counted and materialized facets are exact regardless. --fields=<string> extra fields to include: description, channels (a text hit's rank in each channel that found it), derivatives (with --layout: whether each file has renditions yet) search segelbåt --kind photo search --subject person:anna-exempel --subject person:bo-exempel --kind photo -- sort - time search --subject-name 'person:anna' --kind video search --bbox=$(location-region Exempelstad --bbox-only) --from 2007 --to 2007 search --subject person:anna-exempel --group-by album search --under /archive/albums/Exempelalbum --group-by person search --like /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg --subject person:anna-exempel search --within /home/anna/staging/files -- sort time search --within /home/anna/staging/files --undated --facets search --within /home/anna/staging/files --missing duplicate.deferred With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : a page of matching media, each with its path, name and date; with --group-by the albums (or other containers) holding the matches, or the people in them, instead, counted and dated; with --facets per-year, per-kind and per-label counts.

Stream editor for filtering and transforming text. reads only sed [-n] [-e <string>] [-E] [-r] <SCRIPT> <FILE>... Argument What it is <SCRIPT> sed script (e.g. s/foo/bar/g); omit when using -e. <FILE>... files to process (reads from stdin if omitted) Option What it does -n suppress automatic printing of pattern space. -e <string> add the script to the commands to be executed (repeatable) -E use extended regular expressions (patterns are JS regex) -r alias for -E.

Print a sequence of numbers. reads only seq [-s <string>] [-w] <LAST> <FIRST LAST> <FIRST INCREMENT LAST> Argument What it is <LAST> print numbers from 1 to LAST. <FIRST LAST> print numbers from FIRST to LAST. <FIRST INCREMENT LAST> print numbers from FIRST to LAST with INCREMENT. Option What it does -s <string> use STRING to separate numbers (default: newline) -w equalize width by padding with leading zeroes.
Manage system services. service <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Add a service by linking to a service script directory. administrators only · changes things service-add <name> <path> Argument What it is <name> Service name. <path> Path to service script directory (must contain start.sh)
Disable a service. administrators only · changes things service-disable <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Enable a service. administrators only · changes things service-enable <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
List services, with how often each has restarted. reads only service-list [--detail] Option What it does --detail Also ask each running service for its own status line (its declared statusCommand)
Remove a service. administrators only · changes things service-remove <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Restart a service. administrators only · changes things service-restart <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Start a service. administrators only · changes things service-start <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Start all enabled services. administrators only · changes things service-start-all
Show service status. reads only service-status <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Stop a service. administrators only · changes things service-stop <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Stop all running services. administrators only · changes things service-stop-all

Remove session and tty nodes left behind by dead shells. administrators only · changes things session-reap [--path=<string>] [--max=<string>] [--stale=<string>] [--dry-run] Option What it does --path=<string> Sessions directory (default $SESSIONS_PATH) --max=<string> Stop after removing this many nodes (default 1000) --stale=<string> Age at which an unstamped session is collectable (default 24h) --dry-run Report what would be removed without removing it.
Show and set who has access to a node. share <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Show who has access to a node, and through what. reads only share-info [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links.

Make, list, change and turn off links that open a node without signing in. visitors too · reads only share-link [--expires=<string>] [--never] [--session] <subcommand> <target> Argument What it is <subcommand> create | list | set | remove | open | reap. <target> create and list: the node; set and remove: the link id; open: the token. Option What it does --expires=<string> create and set: when the link stops working, a date or epoch ms (default: 30 days) --never create and set: the link does not expire. --session open: act as the link in the whole session, not just this shell. share-link create /archive/albums/Exempelalbum share-link list /archive/albums/Exempelalbum share-link remove 0123456789abcdef With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : create: the link and how many nodes it reached (ShareLinkCreated); list: ShareLink[]; set: ShareLink; open: what it opens (ShareLinkOpened).

Set who has access to nodes and everything below them. changes things share-set [--mode=<string>] [--owner=<string>] [--group=<string>] [--default-owner] [--reference=<path>] [-m <string>] [-x <string>] [-b] [--drop-links] [--pin] [--unpin] [--pinned-below] [--no-recursive] [--strict] [-L] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... paths to nodes. Option What it does --mode=<string> mode to set, octal or symbolic (e.g. 0750 or g+rx) --owner=<string> user to own the node, by name or uid (administrator only) --group=<string> group for the node, by name or gid (one the caller is in, unless administrator) --default-owner give the node the configured default owner and group (CFG_DEFAULT_SHARE_OWNER, CFG_DEFAULT_SHARE_GROUP) --reference=<path> share the node as this one is: its group, mode and acl (the owner stays) -m <string> add or modify an entry (u: : or g: : ) -x <string> remove an entry (u: or g: ) -b remove the user and group entries before applying -m (share links stay) --drop-links remove the share links' entries too, so no link opens the nodes. --pin hold this node against access changes made further up. --unpin let access changes from further up reach this node again. --pinned-below change the nodes below each path that hold their own access (--pin), not the path itself. --no-recursive change only this node, not what is below it. --strict exit non-zero when any node below could not be changed. -L do not follow symbolic links.
Delay for a specified amount of time. reads only sleep <seconds> Argument What it is <seconds> number of seconds to sleep.

Sort lines of text. reads only sort [-r] [-n] [-u] [-k <string>] [-t <string>] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files whose lines are sorted together (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -r reverse the result of comparisons. -n compare according to string numerical value. -u output only unique lines. -k <string> sort by a key field (e.g., -k2) -t <string> use SEP as field separator.

Log in to another machine or run a command there (members of group ssh) changes things ssh [-p <number>] [-l <string>] [-i <path>] [-F <path>] [-o <string>] [-t] [-T] [-q] <destination> <command>... Argument What it is <destination> [user@]host, or a Host from ~/.ssh/config. <command>... command to run there instead of a shell. Option What it does -p <number> port (default 22) -l <string> remote user (default: your EiN user) -i <path> identity file (default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_ecdsa, id_rsa) -F <path> config file (default ~/.ssh/config; none: no file) -o <string> HostName, Port, User, IdentityFile, StrictHostKeyChecking, BatchMode, ConnectTimeout, ServerAliveInterval, PasswordAuthentication; the same keywords are read from ~/.ssh/config. -t allocate a terminal for a command (-tt: even without one here) -T never allocate a terminal. -q quiet. ssh anna@nas.local ssh -p 2222 backup.example.com ssh nas.local 'df -h' ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new anna@nas.local uptime With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the remote exit status; 255 when the connection fails.

Install your public key in another machine's authorized_keys (members of group ssh) changes things ssh-copy-id [-i <path>] [-p <number>] [-o <string>] [-f] [-n] <destination> Argument What it is <destination> [user@]host. Option What it does -i <path> public key file (default: first of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub, id_ecdsa.pub, id_rsa.pub) -p <number> port (default 22) -o <string> ssh option, e.g. StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new. -f add the key even if it is already there. -n only show what would be added. ssh-copy-id anna@nas.local ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub -p 2222 anna@backup.example.com With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; JSON mode: { ok, added }.

Make an SSH key pair in ~/.ssh, show a fingerprint (-l) or forget a host key (-R) changes things ssh-keygen [-t <string>] [-b <number>] [-f <path>] [-C <string>] [-N <string>] [-q] [-l] [-y] [-R <string>] Option What it does -t <string> key type: ed25519 (default), ecdsa, rsa. -b <number> bits: RSA 3072 (default) or more, ECDSA 256/384/521. -f <path> key file (default ~/.ssh/id_ ) -C <string> comment (default @ein) -N <string> passphrase; asked for when omitted at a terminal. -q quiet. -l show the key file's fingerprint instead. -y print the public key of a private key file. -R <string> remove a host ([host]:port off port 22) from known_hosts. ssh-keygen ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C "backup key" ssh-keygen -l -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ssh-keygen -R nas.local With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; with -l the key size, fingerprint, comment and type.
Start an SSH server. administrators only · changes things ssh-server [--port=<string>] Option What it does --port=<string> port to use.

Bookmark nodes as softlinks in $HOME/stars (star ..., star -d ..., star [list]) reads only star [-d] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... nodes to star/unstar, or "list". Option What it does -d remove the star.

Display file or node status. reads only stat [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links. stat /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the node's type, size, mode, owner and times.
Per-type archive growth: nodes and bytes added by year and month. reads only stats-overview
Which instance this is: host name, uptime, core's version and commit, the module API, each module's commit, and the PostgreSQL and Deno versions. reads only system-info

Output the last part of files, logs, or stdin (with -f to follow) reads only tail [-n <string>] [-c <string>] [-f] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] log/file/blob node to read (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -n <string> output the last NUM lines, or use +NUM for starting at line NUM (-NUM works too) -c <string> output the last NUM bytes, or use +NUM for starting at byte NUM. -f follow: keep the output live as the log/file grows.

Watch the system live: CPU graph, memory and event-loop lag, disks, pipeline work, running commands, sessions, services and recent problems. Keys: q quits, arrows scroll, s sorts, + and - change the interval, p pauses. reads only top [-d <number>] [-n <number>] Option What it does -d <number> Seconds between updates (default 2) -n <number> Write this many frames one after another and stop, as without a terminal. top top -d 5

Translate or delete characters. reads only tr [-d] [-s] [-c] <SET1> <SET2> Argument What it is <SET1> set of characters to translate from. <SET2> set of characters to translate to. Option What it does -d delete characters in SET1. -s squeeze repeated characters in last operand. -c use complement of SET1.

Move nodes into the reader's trash, alone or as one batch, list it, restore entries, or empty it. changes things trash [--batch=<string>] [--label=<string>] [--limit=<number>] [--older-than=<number>] [--all] <subcommand> <items>... Argument What it is <subcommand> put | list | restore | empty. <items>... put: paths to trash, at most 2000; restore and empty: entry ids, batch ids, or / for one entry of a batch. Option What it does --batch=<string> put: into one batch, the one with this id or, with no id, a new one (at most 2000 entries) --label=<string> put: what the batch is called in the trash. --limit=<number> restore: at most this many entries of each batch named. --older-than=<number> empty: only entries trashed more than this many days ago. --all empty: every user's trash (administrators) trash put /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg trash put --batch --label 'Copies of a sailboat' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0002.jpg /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0003.jpg trash list trash restore 01J9Z8Q4R7XKD3V5B2N6M0PA1C -- limit 500 trash empty --older-than 30 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : put: the entries made and their batch (TrashPutResult); list: TrashEntry[], a batch as one row; restore: where each went, and what is left of the batches named (TrashRestoreResult); empty: how many were removed.

Truncate an associated resource of a node if it has one. changes things truncate [-s <string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to truncate. Option What it does -s <string> size to truncate to (default: 0)

Bundle modules' pages into /var/cache/ui for the web UI to load, unless unchanged since the last build. changes things ui-build [--all] <module>... Argument What it is <module>... Module to build; repeatable. Option What it does --all Every installed module with pages, and forget the bundles of those gone.
Tabler icons by name, as SVG markup, for the web UI. reads only ui-icons <name>... Argument What it is <name>... Icon name: map-pin, heart-filled.
The web UI's sidebar, top bar and panels for the caller, from every module's entries and the administrator's, the caller's groups' and the user's changes. reads only ui-nav

Report or omit repeated lines. reads only uniq [-c] [-d] [-u] [-i] [<INPUT>] Argument What it is [<INPUT>] file to read (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -c prefix lines by the number of occurrences. -d only print duplicate lines. -u only print unique lines. -i ignore differences in case when comparing.
Unmount a filesystem. administrators only · changes things unmount [--save] <path> Argument What it is <path> mount point. Option What it does --save also remove the mount from /etc/fstab.
Remove a bidirectional relation (both sides) changes things unrelate <a> <b> <label> Argument What it is <a> relation link path, or first node. <b> second node (with label) <label> relation label.

Expand a zip archive into a directory, streaming each entry. Refuses an archive with an entry that would land outside the directory, or whose files would not leave a tenth of their size free. A file already there at its entry’s size is left as it is, so a run that stopped can be run again. changes things unzip [-d <path>] [-n] [-o] <archive> Argument What it is <archive> the zip to expand. Option What it does -d <path> the directory to expand into, made if missing (default: the current one) -n never write over an existing file (the default) -o write over an existing file. unzip -d /home/anna/staging/files/inbox /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/takeout-001.zip With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : in JSON mode, UnzipAnswer: the files, directories and bytes written, the files left as they were, and each entry not expanded with why. Exits non-zero when any entry was not expanded.
Manage users. user <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Create a user account and its home with its own group (an existing group of its name when that group's gid is free as a uid) and link it into its own and its other groups. administrators only · changes things user-create [--uid=<string>] [--title=<string>] [--email=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--groups=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> name of the user to create: lower-case letters, digits and . _ -, starting with a letter or _. Option What it does --uid=<string> numeric user ID. --title=<string> display title for the user. --email=<string> e-mail address, which signs in like the username; no other account may have it. --description=<string> description of the user. --groups=<string> comma-separated groups to add it to besides its own; empty for none (default CFG_DEFAULT_USER_GROUPS)

Delete a user account, its home, its own group, and its open sessions; what it owned goes to another user. administrators only · changes things user-delete [--to=<user>] [--force] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to delete. Option What it does --to=<user> user that takes over the nodes it owned (default admin) --force force deletion even if errors occur.
Disable a user account and end its open sessions. administrators only · changes things user-disable <username> Argument What it is <username> username to disable.

Make this sign-in an administrator's, for a member of the sudo group, after entering the password again. changes things user-elevate [--password=<string>] [--session] [--off] Option What it does --password=<string> your own password (prompts if not given); --password= for one starting with a dash. --session the session's sign-in, every page and terminal of it, not just this shell's. --off make the sign-in no longer an administrator's.
Enable a disabled user account. administrators only · changes things user-enable <username> Argument What it is <username> username to enable.
Check if a user account exists. reads only user-exists <username> Argument What it is <username> username to check.
List groups a user belongs to. reads only user-groups <user> Argument What it is <user> user to list groups for.
Print user and group IDs. reads only user-id [--uid=<string>] Option What it does --uid=<string> show identity for specified uid.
Display user account information. reads only user-info <username> Argument What it is <username> username to look up.

List the user accounts; as JSON with each one's primary group, e-mail address, description, person and built-in role, and for an administrator whether a password is set. reads only user-list [--inactive] [--active] Option What it does --inactive show only inactive users. --active show only active users.

Change user password. changes things user-passwd [--username=<user>] [--old-password=<string>] [--new-password=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to change password for. Option What it does --username=<user> username (alternative to positional) --old-password=<string> current password (required for non-admin) --new-password=<string> new password to set.
Resolve username to UID or vice versa. reads only user-resolve <uid_or_username> Argument What it is <uid_or_username> uid (numeric) or username to resolve.
Set a user's primary group. administrators only · changes things user-set-primary-group <user> <group> Argument What it is <user> user to change primary group for. <group> new primary group.

Update an account's display name, description and (an administrator only) e-mail address; anyone may update their own name and description. changes things user-update [--name=<string>] [--email=<string>] [--description=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to update. Option What it does --name=<string> set display name. --email=<string> set the e-mail address, which signs in like the username; empty to remove it. --description=<string> set description.
Print the current username. visitors too · reads only user-whoami
Generate a random UUID. reads only uuid

Print newline, word, and byte counts of files or stdin. reads only wc [-c] [-m] [-l] [-w] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to count, each on a line of its own and then a total (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -c print the byte counts. -m print the character counts. -l print the newline counts. -w print the word counts. wc -l /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/notes.txt With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the counts asked for, then the file name; a total line when there are several files.

List who is signed in: each SSH login, terminal and web UI connection, the address it connects from, its idle time and what it runs. Admin sees everyone's, anyone else their own. reads only who who With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One row per open session, oldest first.
Manage active web UI. reads only www <command> [<name>] Argument What it is <command> Command: list, active, set, reset. [<name>] UI name to set as default.

Run a command with the items read from stdin as its arguments, as GNU xargs does: as many per run as fit, or -n per run, or one input line per run with -L, or once per line with -I replacing a string in the command. Items are separated by blanks and newlines, with quotes and backslashes as GNU has them; -0 and -d split on one character instead. The command reads an empty stdin; with no command it is echo. Exits 123 when a run failed, 124 when one exited 255, 125 when one was killed, 126 or 127 when one could not run. reads only xargs [--null] [-0] [--delimiter=<string>] [-d <string>] [--max-args=<string>] [-n <string>] [--max-lines=<string>] [-L <string>] [--max-chars=<string>] [-s <string>] [--replace=<string>] [-I <string>] [--eof=<string>] [-E <string>] [--no-run-if-empty] [-r] [--verbose] [-t] [--arg-file=<path>] [-a <path>] <command>... Argument What it is <command>... the command to run and its first arguments; the items follow them (default: echo) Option What it does --null items end with a NUL character, as find -print0 writes them; quotes are not special. -0 items end with a NUL character, as find -print0 writes them; quotes are not special. --delimiter=<string> items end with this character, such as , or \n; quotes are not special. -d <string> items end with this character, such as , or \n; quotes are not special. --max-args=<string> at most this many items per run. -n <string> at most this many items per run. --max-lines=<string> at most this many input lines per run. -L <string> at most this many input lines per run. --max-chars=<string> at most this many characters per command line (default 131072) -s <string> at most this many characters per command line (default 131072) --replace=<string> run once per input line, with this string in the command replaced by the line, as -I {}. -I <string> run once per input line, with this string in the command replaced by the line, as -I {}. --eof=<string> an item equal to this ends the input. -E <string> an item equal to this ends the input. --no-run-if-empty run nothing when stdin is empty. -r run nothing when stdin is empty. --verbose write each command line to stderr before running it. -t write each command line to stderr before running it. --arg-file=<path> read the items from this file; the command then reads stdin. -a <path> read the items from this file; the command then reads stdin. find /home/anna/staging -name '*.tmp' -print0 | xargs -0 rm ls /archive/people | xargs -I {} info /archive/people/{} With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : what the commands it runs write; xargs itself writes text only.

Every setting of an EiN with all its modules: 81 of them, in the groups the Settings page shows. Configuration says where each value comes from and how to change it. Who it is for : everyone is a system setting, which only an administrator changes, on Settings → System or with config set ; each person is a preference everyone sets for themselves, on Profile → Preferences. Default : the value until someone changes it. A deployment can set another in .env , and a module can choose one. Restarts : the services a change restarts by itself. Work already running is picked up again when they are back.

Stack similarity . How alike two neighbouring photos in an album must look to be stacked as one burst. Higher stacks only near-identical shots. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.75 Kind number Restarts album-metadata From the module Archive

Stack time gap (seconds) . How far apart in capture time two neighbouring photos may be and still be stacked together. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 10 Kind number Restarts album-metadata From the module Archive

Header entrance . How the tiles of a page's header arrive when the page opens: drawn as if by pen and filled from the bottom up, falling into place, sliding in from the right, swept in from left to right, growing from the bottom edge, rippling out from the title, snapping in like puzzle pieces, or a wave of light across them. A device set to reduce motion never animates it. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default drawn Choices drawn , falling , sliding , sweep , growing , ripple , puzzle , wave Kind select

Header entrance time . How many milliseconds the header's entrance takes, from the first tile starting to the last one in place. 0 shows the header as it is, without an entrance. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default 450 Kind number

Header over a cover . How the tiles of a page's header meet its cover photo: split gives the left of the header to the tiles, dissolving hat by hat into the photo along a slanted edge, with their outlines running on over it; lines lays only their outlines over the photo, fading out from the left. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default split Choices split , lines Kind select

Answer length (tokens) . How many tokens the model may write in one call when thinking is not asked for. A thinking model writes its thought inside the same budget, so it may need more. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2048 Kind number From the module Assistant

Language model . The model name sent with each request. A llama.cpp server answers with whichever model it loaded, whatever this says. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default qwen3.5-4b Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model address . The base of an OpenAI-compatible chat API, without /v1: ours (a llama.cpp server) or a provider's, which is then named under Language model provider. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default http://127.0.0.1:8190 Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model key . The bearer key the provider expects, sent only to the language model address above. Unset when the server needs none. No shell sees it, and nothing shows it once it is set. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model provider . The provider's name when the language model is a service elsewhere (OpenAI, say). The chat names it and says that questions, and what the assistant reads in the archive to answer them, are sent there. Set by the host profile. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means ours, run on this host Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Think before answering . 1 asks the model to think before it answers, 0 asks it not to. Sent as llama.cpp's chat_template_kwargs, so only a server that reads them honours it. Empty sends nothing and the server decides. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the server decides Choices 1 , 0 Kind select From the module Assistant

Wait for the language model (seconds) . How long a question to the assistant waits for a language model that is not there, restarting or still loading its model, before the chat says the assistant is unavailable. The chat says it is waiting meanwhile. 0 gives up at once. The search box never waits; it reads the words without the model. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 180 Kind number From the module Assistant

Where our language model runs . card: on the graphics card, beside the share it leaves. cpu: on the processor. Set by the host profile; unused when a provider runs the model. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the host does not say Choices card , cpu Kind select Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Confidence to start a new person from a face . How sure the detector must be of a face that matches nobody before it starts a new, unnamed person. Less certain faces stay unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.7 Kind number From the module Archive

Face match threshold . How similar two faces must be before one is attached to a known person. Higher is stricter and produces fewer wrong matches but more unknown faces. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.55 Kind number From the module Archive

Face neighbour similarity . How similar a known face must be to count as a vote for its person. Faces less alike than this are ignored when deciding who an unknown face is. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.5 Kind number From the module Archive

Face neighbours compared . How many of the most similar known faces are compared with each unknown one. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 24 Kind number From the module Archive

Face winner margin . How far the leading person's votes must outweigh the runner-up's before a face is attached. 1.2 means 20% more; higher leaves close calls unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 1.2 Kind number From the module Archive

Maximum head turn (degrees) . How far a head may be turned away from the camera, estimated from the eyes, nose and mouth, and still be kept as a face. Full profiles beyond this match the wrong person far more often. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 80 Kind number From the module Archive

Minimum face confidence . How sure the detector must be before a box is kept as a face that takes part in recognition. Below 0.7 most detections are backs of heads, blur or things that are not faces, and they pull strangers toward the wrong person.
