Add GPU=1 to make run to give it an NVIDIA card; The graphics card has what the machine needs first. The service listens on port 8181 with the key let-me-in unless you set EMS_PORT and EMS_KEY . EiN looks for it at http://127.0.0.1:8181 , the default of CFG_EMS_URL . Give EiN the key with CFG_EMS_KEY , in the settings file you pass to make container-run as ENV_FILE : # ems.env, in the core checkout CFG_EMS_KEY =let-me-in For the assistant's model, clone llm and run bash run.sh in it. It fetches the model on its first start and answers at http://127.0.0.1:8190 , the default of CFG_LLM_URL , so EiN finds it without a setting. A hosted provider works as well; The language model explains both.

Run these in the core checkout before you send a change: Command What it does deno task test The fast tier: every test under src/ and modules/ , against an in-memory tree. Needs no database and no module; with module checkouts in modules/ , their tests run too. make test-pg The same tests, plus the PostgreSQL tier, against the database at POSTGRES_URL . Those tests keep their tables under a prefix of their own. make container-test Every module's end-to-end tests ( *.e2e.test.ts ) inside core's image, against the services the ENV_FILE points at. Build the image first. deno task test:one <file> One test file. deno task check Type-checks core, the module contract, the modules' commands and the web interface's pages. deno task lint deno lint over src/ and modules/ . deno fmt Formats the code as deno.jsonc says: 175 columns, two spaces, single quotes. deno fmt --check reports what it would change. The module contract is what modules may import from core: @ein/client , @ein/api , @ein/paths and the web interface's kit, @ein/ui/* . Its surface is kept as a snapshot in src/client/contract.snapshot , and a test fails when the surface changes. After a deliberate change, raise MODULE_API_VERSION in src/modules/types.ts and run deno task contract:snapshot to write the snapshot again. The commit history follows Conventional Commits, such as fix(shell): … or feat(archive): … . Write yours the same way.

Core's image holds Deno, core and its documentation, and nothing else: no module, no media tool and no model. Build it with: # on your machine, in the core checkout make container-build and run it with: # on your machine, in the core checkout deno task bundle-ui mkdir -p old make container-run ENV_FILE=ems.env make container-logs make container-run mounts the web interface from the checkout's src/builtin/ui/ui/ , so bundle it first, and the checkout's old/ at /old , so that folder must exist. It runs the container on the host's network, with these variables: Variable Default What it sets ENV_FILE none A file of KEY=value lines: every CFG_… setting beyond the ports. HTTP_PORT , SSH_PORT 8080 , 2222 The ports, passed in as CFG_HTTP_PORT and CFG_SSH_PORT . POSTGRES_URL postgres://ein:ein@localhost:5432/ein The database. FILE_ROOT_PATH , VOLATILE_FILE_ROOT_PATH , FILE_TMP_PATH ./files , ./files-volatile , ./files-tmp The host folders mounted at /files , /files-volatile and /files-tmp . MODULES_PATH ./modules The module checkouts, mounted read-only. MODULE_INSTALL_PATH ./modules-installed Where mod install puts modules, kept when the container is replaced. INSTALL_MODULES none Modules to install at boot when they are missing, such as 'archive assistant' . CONTAINER_MEMORY 6g The container's memory, with no swap. IMAGE_NAME , CONTAINER_NAME ein , ein The image and the container. LOG_LEVEL , LOG_MODULES none The log level, and levels per component such as ssh-server:DEBUG . DENO_ARGS none Extra flags for deno run , such as --inspect=127.0.0.1:9229 . The administrator's password is in make container-logs on the first start. make container-stop stops the container and make container-shell opens bash inside it.

p.h: Run your own build in an installation
p.x: An installation made with the installer runs what the organisation that --source names holds, https://github.com/einhq unless you give it, and keeps it in .env as EIN_SOURCE . To run your own changes there, push them to an organisation of your own on GitHub, Forgejo or Gitea that holds deploy , core and db (and ems and llm when you use those options), and install, or run setup.sh again, with --source and its address. Where the sources come from explains the option, and Updating how setup.sh fetches the newest commits and builds them. From https://github.com/einhq , setup.sh pulls the images ghcr.io/einhq/core:main , ghcr.io/einhq/db:main and ghcr.io/einhq/ems:main , which GitHub builds for every commit on the main of core, db and ems. From any other source it builds them itself, as localhost/ein-core from src/core/src/Containerfile , which also runs deno task bundle-ui , localhost/ein-db from src/db and localhost/ein-ems from src/ems . EiN installs modules from the places CFG_MODULE_SOURCES names; with a Forgejo or Gitea source, setup.sh sets it to the same organisation, while a GitHub source leaves it at https://github.com/einhq .

deno task dev stops at Connecting to database... . PostgreSQL is not answering at POSTGRES_URL . Check that the container runs with podman ps , and run bash ein-db/run.sh again; it reports postgres did not answer on port 5432 when the server does not come up. The browser shows a terminal instead of the web interface. The web interface was not bundled when EiN started. Run deno task bundle-ui and restart EiN. make container-run fails on a missing folder. Create old/ in the checkout, or set OLD_PATH to a folder that exists. A module's page shows the old version. Run ui-build <name> in EiN's terminal, then reload the page. A test fails in module-boundary.test.ts after you edited a manifest. The module's deno.jsonc no longer matches its mod.json . Run deno task sync:modules . With the Archive, files arrive but get no thumbnails. The media service is not reached, or sees other paths than EiN. The media service has the checks.

The Archive is the module that makes EiN a family archive: albums of photos, videos, recordings and documents, the people in them and the family tree, the places they were taken, and the devices that took them. This page is for anyone deciding whether to install it and for anyone starting to use it: what it needs, how to install it, what it adds to EiN, and where to begin. The pages in this section apply once the Archive is installed.

Part What it gives you Covered on Albums and media Albums that hold photos, videos, audio recordings and documents, the Media feed and the Year page, labels, and the viewer Albums , Media, Year and labels , Viewing photos, videos and recordings Staging A private place for each person, where uploads wait, get their dates and places read, and are grouped into suggested albums to file Getting your photos in , Sorting in staging People and the family People, the faces found in pictures, the family tree, events in their lives and the homes they lived in People and faces , Family tree, events and homes Locations and the map Named places with outlines on the map, and pictures placed by their GPS position Locations and the map Devices and GPS tracks The cameras, phones and trackers that took pictures or recorded routes, their owners and clocks Devices and GPS tracks Search Finding pictures by what they show, say and contain, and the albums, people, locations and devices they belong to Searching your pictures Home On this day, News and Events on the Home page, and the life-event charts on the Statistics page Memories, news and events on Home

The ems module. The Archive reaches the media service through it. EiN installs ems along with the Archive. The media service , a separate container beside EiN that reads dates and places, makes the previews, and finds faces, text and speech. Installing the module does not install it: the installer's --ems option does. Without it, the Archive installs and uploads arrive, but nothing gets thumbnails, dates, faces or searchable text, and uploads wait in staging as being prepared until the service is there. The media service covers it. Some of its models are for non-commercial use only; see Models and their licences . A language model is optional. With the assistant module's model, the search box also reads people and places out of a sentence; see Searching your pictures .

Installing takes an administrator. Any of these installs the Archive with the ems module: At the install , with the installer's --module archive , together with --ems for the media service: # on the machine that will run EiN curl -fsSL https://einhq.eu/install.sh | bash -s -- --ems --module archive On an EiN that is already installed, ~/ein/setup.sh --ems --module archive does the same. Without --ems , the installer's archive line says low and reminds you that the Archive needs the media service. In the web interface : open Settings → Modules , choose the Published modules button beside the filter, and choose Install beside archive . When it brings ems along, EiN says "Installed, with ems". In the terminal , as the administrator: # in EiN's terminal mod install archive Its pages appear in the sidebar without a reload. Modules covers installing, updating and removing modules, and Installing in detail the installer's options.

p.h: What it adds to the interface
p.x: In the sidebar: Section Entries (top) Media , and Staging when you are signed in Explore Year and Map , beside EiN's own Search Browse Albums , People , Locations and Devices In the top bar: The Create menu gets Import media (when you are signed in), Album , Person , Location and Device . The account menu gets Favourites . Random album , the button with two crossing arrows beside the search box, opens an album at random; Alt + R does the same. In EiN's own pages: Home : the Archive fills On this day , News and Events , and offers Import media under an empty News when you are signed in; see Memories, news and events on Home . Statistics : the Events section, with births, engagements, marriages and deaths by month. Search : the People , Locations , Years and Labels rows before you search, and, when you are signed in, the pictures that look like a label in a search for that one label; see Searching your pictures . Nodes : a Duplicates tab among the page's tools, for the folder that is open. The finder in the top bar finds albums, people, locations and devices by name, and offers Pictures of "…" to search the Media page. Finding your way around shows where each of these sits.

The Archive keeps its content in the tree: in folders under /archive that it makes when it is set up, and in a staging folder in each person's home: Path What is there /archive/albums Albums, and the photos, videos, recordings and documents in them /archive/people People, with their family, homes, events and devices /archive/locations Locations, each with its outline on the map /archive/devices Cameras, phones and GPS trackers, each with the route it recorded ~/staging In each person's home, such as /home/helen/staging : uploads waiting to be sorted, seen by nobody else Removing the module never removes the folders under /archive , since they hold the content. The tree describes them, and the labels in /archive/tags , which are EiN's own.

Upload. In the top bar, open Create (the plus) and choose Import media . Choose Inbox under Into which category? , click Choose files or Choose a folder , and click Upload . Keep the tab open until the Uploads button in the top bar says it is done. For more than about 10,000 files, copy them over SFTP instead. See Getting your photos in . Sort in staging. A few minutes after the files are prepared, open Staging in the sidebar, then the category, then Sort . Each group shows its proposal, such as New album “…” , which Enter accepts on a computer; or choose New album… in the group's ⋯ menu, check the Name and choose Create album . The pictures leave staging for the album, which is now under Albums . Every decision can be undone. See Sorting in staging . Share an album. Open the album and choose Share in its header. Under Who can see it , Default lets everyone with an account see it, and Private only its owner; for someone without an account, choose Create link under Share with a link . See Sharing . Then name the people in your pictures ( People and faces ), and find what you have ( Searching your pictures ). An administrator setting EiN up for a family finds the whole order of steps on First steps .

Getting your photos in : Import media, dropping files, SFTP, zips and Google Takeout. Sorting in staging : filing uploads into albums. Duplicates : copies, look-alikes and bursts, and removing them. Dates and places of pictures : when and where each picture was taken, and setting them right. Albums : making, editing and arranging albums. Viewing photos, videos and recordings : the viewer, its details panel and slideshow. Media, Year and labels : the Media feed, the Year page and labels. Searching your pictures : finding pictures and what they belong to. People and faces : people, and naming the faces found in pictures. Family tree, events and homes : how people are related, and their lives. Locations and the map : places, their outlines and the map. Devices and GPS tracks : cameras, phones and trackers, and their routes. Memories, news and events on Home : what the Archive shows on Home and Statistics. Supported files : the files the Archive reads. Processing pictures : the work done on every file, for administrators. Staging for administrators : staging areas, large imports and repairs. Archive commands : the Archive's commands in the terminal.

This page is for everyone in the family who brings photos, videos, recordings and letters into EiN. It shows every way in, where each one puts your files, and what happens to them until they are in an album.

Almost everything you bring in lands first in your staging area , a private place that only you can see. EiN reads each file there, checks whether you have it already and suggests albums for it. Nobody else sees the files, and they stay out of the shared library, until you file them into an album. The usual way past staging is to upload straight into an album that already exists. Way in Where the files go Folders kept Create → Import media the staging category you choose yes Dropping files on the Staging page the category you drop them on yes Upload , or dropping files, on the Media page your Inbox in staging yes Upload , or dropping files, on an album's page that album, in the library no Copying over SFTP or scp the folder you copy into, normally a staging category yes Your staging area is divided into categories . The Inbox is always there and takes everything you do not put elsewhere; you can add others, one per source: a Google Photos export, a box of scanned prints, an old phone. Each category is a folder, /home/<you>/staging/files/<name> . Sorting in staging covers categories in full. Until they are filed, staged files stay out of the library's own views: the Media page, the map, On this day, the newest pictures and search leave them out. You find them on the Staging page, in the sidebar below Media . EiN takes photos (camera RAW files too), videos, recordings, documents such as PDFs, and GPX tracks. Supported files lists the formats and what EiN works out from each. A GPX track you upload into staging is not a picture: it joins the track of the device that recorded it, or waits for you to say which device that was (see Devices and GPS tracks ). Note You need to be signed in to bring files in: visitors are not offered Import media or Staging .

Import media is the main way in. It puts files into one staging category, keeping the folders you choose. Open the Create menu (the plus in the top bar) and choose Import media . The same dialog opens from the Import media button on the Staging page, the Import button on a category's card, Import media… in a category's ⋮ menu and, while the Home page has no news yet, the Import media button there. Under Into which category? , pick a category. Each shows how many files it holds and its folder, for example "0 files · files/inbox". The Inbox is chosen unless you opened the dialog from a category. To keep this batch in a category of its own, choose New category instead ("For one source kept together: an export, a box of scans, a phone."). Pick What it holds , and type what the category is Called . The line under the name shows the folder it gets, for example "Folder files/box-3". Choose Choose files or Choose a folder . The line under the buttons counts what you picked, for example "212 files in 3 folders, 1.4 GB". Choose Upload 212 . The button counts your files. Import media: a category, the files, then Upload. The dialog closes, the category opens on its Files tab and the files upload in the background. If you made a new category, it is created first. What it holds starts on Google Photos export . Pick the kind closest to where the files come from: Google Photos export , Scans , Phone , Camera , Messaging , Screenshots or Other . The kind decides how the files are dated and grouped; a scan, for example, is never dated by the scanner's clock. The kinds of category explains each one. For an existing category, the dialog also says "Over about 10,000 files? Copy them over SFTP instead, folders and all, into" with the category's folder, a button that copies the path, and a How link. See Copy files in over SFTP .

While files upload, an Uploads button with a progress ring appears in the top bar. Its panel shows how far the whole upload is ("1,204 of 3,000" and the bytes), the progress of each place the files go (a category or an album), the files being sent, and the last failures with their reasons. Cancel stops the upload: the files being sent are stopped and the waiting ones dropped. Retry failed sends the failed files again. Clear forgets the finished files; the button goes away until the next upload. Four files are sent at a time. The upload goes on while you move around EiN, but it runs in this browser tab: closing or reloading the tab stops the files not sent yet. The files already sent stay. A name already taken in a folder is never replaced. The file is stored under a numbered name, such as IMG_0042 (2).jpg , and the panel says "N saved under a new name, theirs was taken".

p.h: Upload or drop files on a page
p.x: Four pages take files from a button in their header and from files dropped anywhere on them: Page Buttons When you drag files over it Where the files go Staging (the overview of your categories) Import media "Drop the files on where they go", with a tile for each category the category whose tile you drop them on A staging category, on any tab Upload , and Upload a folder under ⋮ "Drop files to upload", "Into Box 3, folders and all" (with the category's name) that category Media Upload , and Upload a folder under ⋮ "Drop files to upload", "Into staging, folders and all" your Inbox An album you may change Upload "Drop files to upload", "Into Sailing in the archipelago" (with the album's name) that album On the Staging overview, files dropped beside the tiles go nowhere. An upload into staging goes into a folder for the day inside the category, named upload-YYYY-MM-DD , and a folder you drop or choose keeps its structure below it: Trip/day 2/IMG_0001.jpg lands in upload-2026-10-25/Trip/day 2/ . Folder names help the grouping. In most kinds of category, a folder you named yourself, holding at least three pictures, becomes a suggested album of its own, named after the folder, such as "Cornwall, summer 1968". Names that cameras and exports give folders, such as DCIM , 100CANON , a bare year or date, or Takeout , are not used. On a phone the header's buttons fold into the ⋮ menu, and Upload offers your photos, videos, recordings and GPX files, and the camera. EiN on a phone has more. Files dropped on a terminal tab are uploaded into that tab's current folder, without their folders; see The terminal .

An album's page has Upload in its header, and files dropped anywhere on the page go into the album. This skips staging, and it differs from an upload into staging in these ways: The files are in the album at once, shared as the album is: everyone who can see the album sees them as soon as they are processed. EiN suggests nothing and does not check them against your other pictures for copies. Folders are not kept: every file goes straight into the album. A zip stays a zip; it is expanded only in staging. New files show a plain tile with a picture icon until their thumbnails are made, and take their place in date order once their dates have been read. Upload is offered only on an album you may change, and never on a suggested album (a staging group opened as an album page). Albums covers the album page.

Use staging ( Import media , the Media page or the Staging page) when: you bring in a batch: a phone's worth, an export, a box of scans or a folder from an old laptop; you want EiN to find the pictures you have already and suggest which albums the rest belong in; you want to look at the pictures before anyone else sees them. Upload straight into an album when you have a few pictures that belong in an album that already exists, you may change that album, and the people it is shared with may see them right away.

For tens of thousands of files, or a whole export, copy them over SFTP instead of through the browser. You need the host name, the SSH port (2222 unless your administrator changed it), and your EiN username and password. sftp , scp , FileZilla, Cyberduck and your file manager's "connect to server" all work; SSH and SFTP explains connecting. Open Staging in the web interface once. This sets up your staging area. Without that, EiN sets it up within the hour. For a big export or a box of scans, make its category first: on the Staging page, choose its kind on the New category card, type what it is Called and choose Create . Copy the files into the category's folder, /home/<you>/staging/files/<name>/ . The Staging page says "Tens of thousands of files? Copy them over SFTP into a category's folder:", and the Import media dialog shows the folder of the category you pick, with a button that copies the path. # on your own computer scp -P 2222 -r "From the old laptop" anna@ein.local:/home/anna/staging/files/inbox/ Mind the capital -P for the port in scp and sftp . Files copied over SFTP are taken in exactly as a browser upload is; on the Staging page they show as "being prepared" (the "arriving" stage counts uploads from your browser only).

p.h: Keep folder names for the grouping
p.x: A folder becomes a suggested album of its own, named after the folder, only when it lies two or more levels below the category. A browser upload does this for you, because it adds the folder for the day. Over SFTP, copy a folder that holds your event folders, not the event folders themselves: staging/files/inbox/ From the old laptop/ one level down: its name is not used Cornwall, summer 1968/ two levels down: suggested as "Cornwall, summer 1968" Christmas 1975/ two levels down: suggested as "Christmas 1975" Pictures in a folder only one level down are still grouped, by when and where they were taken; only the folder's name is not used. Put files in a category's folder, never in files/ itself: a folder copied directly into files/ becomes a category of its own, of the Other kind, and a file left there belongs to no category until EiN moves it into files/inbox/unsorted/ . It does that once an hour, for a file nothing has changed on for six hours, so a copy still being written is left alone. Warning A file you delete over SFTP is gone for good; it does not go to the trash. To get rid of staged files, use Discard… on the category's Files tab, which puts them in your trash with Undo.

You do not need to unpack a zip first. A zip uploaded or copied anywhere into a staging category is expanded once its upload has ended: what it holds goes into the folder the zip lies in, and the zip is removed. One zip is expanded at a time. The disk needs room for what the zip holds and a tenth more. A zip that does not fit, or that would put a file outside its folder, is left as it is. A file already there at the same size is skipped, so a zip whose expansion was cut off is finished on the next attempt. A file of the same name and another size is not written over: the rest of the zip is expanded, and the zip stays. When a zip stays, your administrator can see why on the pipeline's page; see Processing and pipelines . Outside staging, for example uploaded into an album, a zip stays a zip.

A Google Photos Takeout comes as one or more zips. Beside every photo and video, Google writes a JSON file with what it knows of it: when it was taken, where, its caption and whether it was a favourite. EiN reads these files, called sidecars, and gives what they say to the picture. On the Staging page, choose Google Photos export on the New category card. Call it, for example, "Google Photos"; its folder is files/google-photos . You can also choose New category in the Import media dialog, where Google Photos export is the first kind. Bring in the zips as they are: in Import media , choose the category, Choose files and the zips, then Upload . For a large export, copy them over SFTP instead: # on your own computer scp -P 2222 takeout-001.zip takeout-002.zip anna@ein.local:/home/anna/staging/files/google-photos/ Wait. Each zip is expanded and removed, and the parts of one export fill one tree of folders. About 30 seconds after a folder's files stop arriving, EiN pairs each JSON file with its photo or video. What a paired JSON file gives its picture: In the Takeout In EiN when the picture was taken its date where it was taken its place, when the file has no GPS position of its own its caption its description, when it has none marked as a favourite in your Favourites an album's folder and its title a suggested album under that title the people Google named in it not used: EiN finds the faces itself A paired JSON file moves under its picture and is no longer listed as a file of its own. A JSON file that matches no picture stays where it is and counts among the category's Other files . The pairing knows Google's ways of naming: IMG_0001.jpg.json and IMG_0001.jpg.supplemental-metadata.json , names cut short, the (1) of a second picture of the same name, edited copies, and the video of a Live Photo. A category of the Google Photos export kind is worth making for two reasons: it pairs sidecars, and its processing waits behind other work, so pictures you upload to the Inbox in the meantime are ready first. A Scans category waits behind other work in the same way. An XMP file that a photo editor or a scanning tool writes beside a picture ( IMG_0001.jpg.xmp or IMG_0001.xmp ) is paired the same way. Every kind of category pairs sidecars except Messaging and Screenshots .

p.h: If the export went into the Inbox
p.x: A folder that arrives in the Inbox is looked at to see where it came from. When it looks like an export, a blue box on the Staging page and on the Inbox's Files tab says so, for example "“Takeout” looks like Google Photos", with the two strongest signs. Make a Google Photos export category… makes the category and moves the folder into it. Move to Google Photos… (with your category's name) appears instead when you have a category of that kind already. The ✕ ("Keep it here, stop asking") leaves the folder where it is. Nothing moves by itself. The same box recognises scans, a phone's or a camera's pictures, pictures from a messenger and screenshots.

Files wait in your staging area until you decide; only filing can make them visible to others Each category's card on the Staging page, and the strip above a category's tabs, show where your newest files are. Each stage shows while it holds files: You see Its tooltip "N of M arriving" "Uploading from this browser" "N being prepared, about 12 min" "Their dates and places are being read; the groups they join may still change" "N being grouped" "Read, and waiting for the organizer to put them in a group" Arriving. The files are on their way from your browser. Files copied over SFTP skip this stage and show first as being prepared. Being prepared. EiN reads each file's date, place and camera. A file that is an exact copy of a picture you can open already is recognised here and goes no further: it is not processed, and shows its original's picture (see An exact copy shows its original ). The time estimate comes from how fast files left this stage while the page was open. Being grouped. The organizer sorts read files into groups within minutes of their arrival. On a category's page, Group now beside this stage asks it at once, and a message says "Grouping asked for: the new files are grouped within a few minutes". Suggested albums. The groups appear on the category's Sort tab, one after another, each in a lane: To sort , Everyday , Needs a date , Clutter or Later . Before the first is ready, the tab says "No groups yet" and "Groups appear as your files are prepared: N still to go." Filed. For each group you choose New album , New private album , Add to album… , Later or Discard . Filing moves the files into an album in the library, with everything EiN worked out about them; from then on whoever can see that album sees them. A discarded group goes to your trash. Filing and discarding can be undone on the category's Done tab. The card's bar shows the same files by how far along they are: Being prepared , To sort (read, with a date), Needs a date (read, but with no date) and Other files (files that are not pictures, videos or recordings). An exact copy that went no further, and an empty picture, video or recording, are in none of them. How to go through the groups is on Sorting in staging .

p.h: Why new pictures have no thumbnails yet
p.x: Reading a file's date and place is only the first step. The rest of the work runs side by side afterwards, and each part shows up in EiN when it is done. Each piece of work fills in its own part of EiN as it finishes. Work What it gives you Thumbnails, and a version of each video and recording your browser can play the picture in grids and in the viewer; until then a plain tile with a picture icon Faces the people in the picture, named or waiting for a name ( People and faces ) Picture vectors searching by what a picture shows Text in pictures and documents letters, signs, handwriting and the text of PDFs become searchable; read once a file is filed, not while it waits in staging Transcripts and voices what is said in videos and recordings becomes searchable, with who says it Fingerprints look-alikes, stacks of photos taken in a burst, and the same recording twice Address lookup the street address for a GPS position, from OpenStreetMap The media service does most of this work. It is the part of your EiN installation that holds the tools and models for pictures, video and sound. With a graphics card it is faster; without one it makes the same things, more slowly. A few new pictures take moments; an export of tens of thousands keeps it busy for a long while. While files are being prepared, their category's card on the Staging page estimates how long that stage has left, as in "about 12 min". If the media service is not running, nothing new is read: files stay "being prepared", while uploading and browsing go on working. Nothing is lost; the work waits and goes on once the media service answers. The media service is the administrator's page on it. Your administrator follows this work on the Dashboard , whose verdict reads Catching up while work is waiting and getting done. Only Stuck or Needs a person , for long, means something needs looking at; see Health and the dashboard . Anyone can ask the same question in the terminal with health , whose first line is the verdict: catching up: 1,500 jobs waiting, the slowest kind done in 4h00m

Upload stays greyed out in the dialog. Choose files first. With New category , the name must hold a letter or a digit; the line under it says "Needs a letter or digit" until it does. Some files failed. Open the Uploads button in the top bar: the failures are listed with their reasons. Choose Retry failed . The panel says files were "saved under a new name, theirs was taken". A file of that name was in the folder already. If it is the same picture uploaded twice, the second one is marked as an exact copy; remove it on the category's Duplicates tab ( Duplicates ). An album has no Upload button. You may not change that album, or it is a suggested album from staging. Filing from staging into an album also needs you to be able to change it, so ask whoever shares the album to let you edit it ( Sharing ), or file the pictures into an album of your own. Files stay "being prepared" for a long time. A large import can take hours. If the count does not go down at all, the media service may not be running; tell your administrator. The Sort tab says "No groups yet". The files are still being prepared, or the organizer has not grouped them yet. Wait a few minutes, or choose Group now on the category's page. A zip is still a zip. It was uploaded outside staging, the disk lacked room, or a file in it clashed with one already there. Your administrator can see the reason. A folder's name was not used for a group. The folder lies only one level below the category (see Keep folder names for the grouping ), holds fewer than three pictures, or has a name a camera or an export gives. New pictures are not on the Media page, the map or in search. That is how staging works: they appear there once you file them. Look for them on the Staging page. Over SFTP, /home/<you>/staging does not exist. Open Staging in the web interface once, then copy again. The dates are wrong, or scans have none. A scan is undated until you give it a date; see Dates and places of pictures .

Sorting in staging : categories, the suggested albums and filing them. Duplicates : exact copies, look-alikes and bursts. Supported files : what EiN takes in and what it works out from each file. SSH and SFTP : connecting from your own computer. Staging and importing for administrators : the background work, big imports and the staging command.

Everything you upload waits in your own staging area until you decide where it goes. This page is for family members sorting their uploads into albums. It covers the categories that hold your files, the albums EiN suggests, the keys and buttons that file, discard or regroup those suggestions, and how to undo any of it.

Pictures, videos and recordings you bring in do not go straight into the family's shared library. They land in your staging area , a private inbox that only you can see. The page says so under its title: "New media to sort before it joins the shared library. Only you can see it." How files get there ( Import media , dragging files onto a page, the Media page's upload, SFTP) is on Getting your photos in . While the files wait, EiN reads each one: its date, its place, the faces in it and its thumbnails. It also checks whether you already have a copy. Then the organizer sorts them into suggested albums , called groups on these pages: a birthday, a trip, a folder you named, a year of everyday pictures. You go through the groups and decide for each one: file it as a new album , or a new private album only you can open; file it into an album that is already in the library; put it aside for Later ; discard it to your trash. Only filing makes the files visible to anyone else. Every decision can be undone. A file's way through staging: nothing reaches the shared library until you file it Until a file is filed, the views of the whole library leave it out: the Media page and its counts, the map, On this day, search, and the number on a person's card on the People page. The faces and voices in it are found all the same, and count once the file is filed. Note Staging is only for people who are signed in. A visitor browsing without an account does not see it in the sidebar, and opening its address asks them to sign in.
Open Staging in the sidebar, under Media . While you have only the Inbox, staging opens the Inbox's page directly. Once you have more than one category, it opens on the overview of all of them.

The overview shows one card per category. The header has Import media and New category . Each card shows: the category's name, and under it what it holds and its folder, for example Scans · files/box-3 ; a gear, Category settings ; a bar of its files by how far along they are: Being prepared , To sort , Needs a date and Other files (files that are not pictures, videos or recordings), or "Nothing here yet."; how many files it holds and their size, followed by "filed into" and an album's name when its files go to that album by default; where the newest files are on their way in (below); Import , and Continue ( Open while the category is empty). While files are on their way in, a card and the top of a category's page show up to three stages. Hold the pointer over one to see what it means. Stage What it means N of M arriving Uploading from this browser N being prepared, about <time> Their dates and places are being read; the groups they join may still change N being grouped Read, and waiting for the organizer to put them in a group The organizer groups new files within a few minutes of their arrival. On a category's page, Group now beside "being grouped" asks it to start at once; the message "Grouping asked for: the new files are grouped within a few minutes" confirms it. Drag files or folders over the overview and a tile appears for each category. Drop them on one and they go into that category's folder for today, folders and all. When a folder that arrived in the Inbox looks like it came from one source, a blue box above the cards says so, for example "“Takeout” looks like Google Photos", with the two strongest clues. The same box shows on the Inbox's Files tab. Its button moves the folder into your category of that kind, for example Move to Google Photos export… . When you have no such category, the button makes one first: Make a Google Photos export category… opens the New category dialog, whose Create and move “Takeout” makes the category and moves the folder into it. The ✕ ("Keep it here, stop asking") leaves the folder where it is and stops asking. Nothing moves by itself. Below the cards, a yellow box titled Needs you appears when a GPS track waits for the device that recorded it; Choose device opens the Inbox's files, where you say which device it was (see Devices and GPS tracks ). Last comes the folder to copy into over SFTP, for tens of thousands of files; see SSH and SFTP and Staging and importing for administrators .

A category keeps one source together: a Google Photos export in one, a box of scanned prints in another, your phone in a third. Each category is a folder of your staging area, and what it holds decides how EiN treats its files: how they are grouped, which clocks may date them, and in which order they are processed. The Inbox is always there and cannot be removed. Uploads land in it unless you choose another category.

What it holds Use it for What it changes Inbox Anything; the default Grouped by time and place. A date in a file name, such as a phone's IMG_20190601_123456.jpg , counts when nothing better dates the picture. Google Photos export A Google Takeout Grouped by time and place. Google's JSON files are paired with their photos and give them their date, place and caption. An album folder's title names its group. Processed after other work, so what you upload to the Inbox meanwhile is ready first. Scans Scanned prints, negatives and slides Grouped by folder and by runs of file names; when a scan was made never groups it. No scanner clock, file name or upload time dates a scan, only a date a person gave it, so most count under Needs a date until you give them one. Processed after other work. Phone A phone's pictures Grouped by time and place. Dates in file names count. Camera A camera's memory card Grouped by time and place. File names are not read as dates. Messaging Pictures saved from a messenger A group per folder and month, all in the Everyday lane. Dates in file names count. Sidecar files are left as they are. Screenshots Screenshots Like Messaging. Other Anything else Grouped by time and place. File names are not read as dates. How these work for dates is explained further on Dates and places of pictures .

On the overview, choose a kind on the dashed New category card ("Keep one source together: a Google Photos export, a box of scanned prints, a phone."), or choose New category in the header. On a category's page, click its name and choose New category… . In the New category dialog, check What it holds . When you started from a kind's button, it is chosen already, and Called holds the kind's name. Fill in Called , the name the pages show, for example Box 3 . Leave Folder name empty to have it made from the name, or type one: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 48 characters. The folder name never changes. Choose Create . The new category's page opens. You can also make a category while importing. In Import media , choose New category under "Into which category?", then What it holds and Called ; the dialog shows the folder it makes ("Folder files/box-3"). The category is made when you choose Upload . Import media can make a category and fill it in one step

Open Category settings with the gear on the category's card, or from the ⋮ menu on its page. Field What it does Called The name the pages show. Its folder stays as it is. What it holds The kind, from the table above. The Inbox's kind cannot be changed. Files go to An album its files go to by default. Type in Find an album to choose one you may add to; None clears it. Without one: "No album by default: each group is filed where you choose." Choose Save to keep the changes. An album under Files go to becomes the proposal for most groups that no library album matches well, marked "· the category’s album" under the proposal, and it is the album B files into until you choose another. Warning Changing What it holds resets everything the kind decides to the new kind's way: how the files are grouped, which clocks date them, the order they are processed in and whether sidecars are paired. Only the name and Files go to are kept. The files are dated again at once, and the organizer groups them again within minutes. Some finer settings of a category, such as how readily a day becomes a group of its own, can only be changed from the shell; see Staging and importing for administrators . To remove a category, choose Remove category in its settings, then Remove (or Keep it ). Only an empty category can be removed: "Only an empty category can be removed: move or discard its files first." The Inbox cannot be removed.

The page's title is the category's name with a chevron. Click it to switch to another category, to All categories , or to New category… . The header has Upload , which adds files to the category's folder for today, and under ⋮: Upload a folder , Import media… , Category settings and, with more than one category, All categories . You can also drop files anywhere on the page, on any tab, and they go into the category on screen. Under the tab names, a thin bar shows the category's files and the stages of what is arriving, with Group now . The four tabs: Tab What it is for Its number Sort Deciding the suggested albums, one after another Groups Duplicates Exact copies and look-alikes, to resolve Exact copies Files The category's folders and files Files held Done What was decided here, with Undo Files filed and discarded The Duplicates tab has a page of its own: Duplicates .

p.h: Sort: the stream of suggested albums
p.x: The Sort tab lists the category's groups one after another, oldest first. Every picture, video and recording that has been read is in exactly one group. Until the first groups are made, the tab says No groups yet , with "Groups appear as your files are prepared: N still to go." or "Groups appear here once uploaded files have been prepared and organized, within minutes of their arrival." Show the files opens the Files tab.

The line above the stream has: the lanes, each with its number of groups, when more than one lane has groups; otherwise "N photos to decide in M groups"; "◌ N applying" while decisions you made are still being carried out; Select , to select every group of the lane at once (see Decide several groups at once ); Oldest first or Newest first . Groups without a date come last either way. One group is open . The others are closed to their name and two rows of their pictures. Click a closed group, or press J and K , to open the next or previous one. An open group shows its pictures in a grid per day. A group that spans more than 40 days, such as a year of everyday pictures, shows a grid per month instead, with the month's days as small buttons above it; click one to select that day's pictures. Pictures without a date come last, under No date . Below the open group, "Next:" and a name say which group follows. A group's header shows its name, then its dates, how many photos and how many days it holds, for example "Christmas Eve · 24 Dec 1975" over "24 Dec 1975 · 86 photos". Badges may follow: Badge Meaning Trip Two or more days away from home Still indexing "Some of these are still being indexed, so the group may still change" Later Put aside with L Yours "You edited this group, so the organizer leaves it as it is" ⧉ 4 in library · 2× 1 Some pictures are copies or look-alikes; its menu has Compare , Keep the library copies and Select these ( Duplicates ) A closed group says where it is proposed to go when that is a library album, for example "→ Sailing in the archipelago likely". The open group has its proposal as a button with Enter , or New album… with N when there is no proposal. Its ⋯ menu holds every action. Where you were is kept in the page's address, and per category in your browser, so a reload or a link brings you back to the same group. When a stream holds 30 groups or more, a time rail at its right edge brings the groups from a chosen date up.

The stream is divided into lanes. Each lane is a view of some of the category's groups. Lane What it holds To sort Events, trips, folders a person named, and runs of scans Everyday Each year's ordinary days, as one group per year, or per month in a busy year Needs a date Pictures with no date, or dated only to a year or a month Clutter Screenshots and images saved from messages Later Anything you put aside with L , whatever lane it came from Lanes keep the events to decide apart from the everyday pictures, the undated ones and the clutter Groups in the Everyday, Needs a date and Clutter lanes are named after what they hold: "Everyday · 2014", "Screenshots and saved images · 2019", "Undated · box-3", or "1987 · box-3" for pictures known only to a year. They are collections, not events, so they are not split, merged or called "not a group". To take some pictures out of one, make them a group of their own with New group on a day, or move them with < , > and G (see Change the groups ). Everyday. Each day of an Everyday group is compared with the library's albums. A day that matches one shows it in its header, for example "→ Christmas at the cottage 72%", with File , which files that day's pictures into the album. Select the day with [ or ] and Enter does the same. A closed Everyday group says how many of its days match an album, for example "→ 3 days match an album". Needs a date. Give the pictures a time with T ( Set the time… ): the Set time dialog takes one start time, and the pictures keep their spacing or follow a minute apart. A picture known only to a year or a month keeps that date unless you click its row to give it a time. Once dated, the organizer puts them with the events and days they belong to. The dialog is explained on Dates and places of pictures . Clutter. Its proposal is Discard .

Each group has a proposal : what Enter , or the button on the group, does with it. In the column beside the stream (on a wide screen) it comes with how sure it is: Dots Word Meaning ●●● sure EiN is confident ●●○ likely Probably right; have a look ●○○ unsure A starting point The button says what happens: Button When it is proposed Add to “…” A library album you may add to matches the group well (likely or sure), or it is the category's album under Files go to New album “…” No album fits: a new album under the group's name. A folder a person named is proposed as a new album under the folder's name, sure. Keep the library copies · N photos go Most of the group's photos are copies of photos already in the library; the copies go and the rest of the group stays to be sorted Discard Clutter File N matched days · M photos An Everyday group some of whose days match a library album you may add to; each matched day goes into its album and the rest stays "No proposal: N, A, B or X." Nothing to propose, for example an Everyday group with no matched days in a category with no album under Files go to Runs of scans and folders a person named go into an existing album only when the match is sure. Nothing is ever filed by a match on its own: you decide every time.

Open the group: click it, or press J or K until it is open. Look at the proposal on the group's button, or at the top of the column beside the stream. Press Enter or click the button. For an existing album, the photos are filed at once. For a new album, the New album dialog opens with the group's name under Name . Change it if you like, and choose Create album . The group leaves the stream and the next one opens in its place. A green message says, for example, "86 photos filed in “Christmas at the cottage”", with Undo . Instead of the proposal you can choose another way, each with its key: Choice Key What it does New album N A new album from the group, shared as your new albums are. New private album P A new album only you can open ("Only you see it"). Its name is still listed among the albums. Add to album… A The Add to an album dialog: type to find any album you may add to, or type a name and choose New album “…” with that name. Before you type, your recent albums are listed, and 1 to 8 pick one. The target B Files into the target album without asking. Shift + B chooses another target ("B now files into “Christmas at the cottage”"). A candidate 1 2 3 Files into one of the albums EiN found for the group (see Candidates and compare ). The target is the album you chose with Shift + B for this category, else the category's album under Files go to when you may add to it, else the album you filed into last. The target and your recent albums are remembered in your browser. Filing moves the files out of your staging into the album. Everything EiN has read about them goes along: dates, places, faces and thumbnails. Text in them, such as a letter or a sign, is read once they are filed. A new album is shared the way your new albums are, as the administrator set it up (see Sharing ); a private one only you can open. Filed into an existing album, the files are shared the way that album is. An album you may only look at is refused before anything moves: "You can't add to “Christmas 1975”."

You do not have to file a group whole. Press [ or ] to step to a day (or a month) of the open group, or select pictures the way you do in an album (see Albums ). With the arrow keys on a picture, Space selects it. Enter , N , P , A , B and X act on those pictures alone; the line at the foot of the stream says so, for example "New album of 12 pictures". The rest of the group stays where it is. With pictures selected, New group of N pictures under the open group makes them a group of their own instead.

On a computer, when the Sort tab is at least 1,100 pixels wide, a column stands beside the stream. It starts with "Put it in" and the group's name, then the proposal and its dots. Below them are up to three candidates : library albums the group may belong in, best first. Each shows its name, a percentage, its dates and size, and up to three reasons in words, such as "within 40 min of its photos for 12 of 12", "same places for 8 of 10 located photos", "2 of 3 people appear in it" or "looks alike". An album you may only look at is marked "view only" and cannot be chosen. When EiN compared the group with the library and found nothing, it says "No album in the library fits it well." One candidate is highlighted. Under the list, its pictures around the group's days are shown, headed with its name and "around these days", with the group's own days marked "· when the group was taken". Earlier and Later page through the album and Open album opens it. Compare side by side (C) widens the column to half the page; Narrow the column (C) puts it back. , and . move the highlight up and down. 1 , 2 and 3 , or a click, file the group into that candidate. Further down the column are New album , New private album , the target with "⇧B chooses another" (or Choose a target… ), up to four recent albums, Add to album… , the ways to change the group, Later and Discard ("To the trash, with Undo").

When a candidate is wrong, press R , or click the ✕ ("Not this album (R)") on the highlighted one. The message "“Christmas 1975” is no longer offered for “Christmas Eve · 24 Dec 1975”" confirms it. The album is not offered again for this group, or for any group made mostly of the same photos, until you undo it on the Done tab.

p.h: Put a group aside or discard it
p.x: Later ( L ) moves the group to the Later lane: "“Saturday evening” is in Later". No file moves, and the group stays in Later when the organizer regroups the category. In the Later lane the same key, Back to its lane , returns it. Discard ( X , or Discard the photos… in the ⋯ menu) moves the group's photos to your trash as one entry on the Trash page: "86 photos moved to the trash". A group of 200 photos or more asks first, in a Discard? dialog. Nothing in staging is deleted outright: Undo in the message, Z , the Done tab, or Restore on the Trash page brings the photos back (see Your profile, favourites and trash ).

On a computer you can select several groups and decide them together: tick the box in a group's header, or Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on a Mac) its name or a closed group's pictures; hold Shift to select everything from where the selection started; press Shift + J or Shift + K to select on to the next or previous group; choose Select → All in To sort (or whichever lane you are in), or Those with a sure proposal ; or draw a box around them from an empty part of the page (hold Shift to add, Alt to take away, Esc to stop). Then Enter accepts each group's proposal, after the Accept the proposals? dialog has asked which to take ( Every proposal , Likely and sure or Only sure ); N or P makes one album of everything selected, A and B file it into an album, X discards it after asking, and L puts the groups aside. Esc clears the selection. A message shows the progress, for example "Filing 1,840 of 9,830 photos · 37 of 214 groups", with Cancel ; when it is done, Undo all takes the whole run back. You can also drag selected pictures, or a group by the grip ⠿ in its header, onto a row of the column or onto another group's header. Each place says what the drop would do as you arrive.

On a computer, the line at the foot of the stream shows the keys for where you are, each also a button; hide folds it to a Keys chip. ? lists every key. Keys do nothing while you type in a field or a dialog is open, and there are none on a phone. All the app's shortcuts are on Keyboard shortcuts . On a group: Key What it does J / K Next group / previous group Enter The proposal N New album from the group P New private album A Add to album… B Into the target, or Choose a target… when there is none Shift + B Choose the target 1 2 3 Into that candidate , / . Highlight the candidate above / below R Not the highlighted candidate C Compare with the highlighted album, or narrow the column again X Discard L Later, or back to its lane Z Undo the last decision of this visit E Rename T Set the time of every picture M / Shift + M Merge into the group above / merge the group below in [ / ] Previous / next day or month of the group Arrow keys Step through the pictures O Open the first picture Shift + J / Shift + K Select on to the next / previous group On a picture (after an arrow key), a day or month (after [ or ] ), or selected pictures: Key What it does Space Select the picture, or the day's pictures O Open the picture S Split the group before them; in a lane, make them a new group < / > Move them to the group above / below G Move them to a group… Enter N P A B X Act on the day or the selected pictures only Esc Back to the group, or clear the selection With the arrow keys on a single picture and nothing selected, Enter , N , P , A , B and X still act on the whole group. < , > , [ and ] work on any keyboard layout, also where you type them with AltGr or Option.

The organizer's groups are suggestions. When one is wrong, change it. Every change but a rename says so in a message with Undo , and every change is listed on the Done tab, where Undo takes it back. To Do this What happens Split a group Split here on a day or month, or S on a picture, a day or a selection That picture and the ones after it become a group of their own: "“A week in London” split in two". You cannot split before the first picture. Move pictures to a neighbour Select them, then < or > They join the group above or below. Move pictures to any group Select them, then G The Move to a group dialog: the five groups on each side, Find a group by name , or New group ("A group of their own, named by their dates"). Make a new group New group of N pictures under the open group; in a lane, New group on a day or S The pictures become a group of their own, named by their dates. Merge two groups M ( Merge into “…” , the group above) or Shift + M ( Merge “…” in , the group below) One group. It keeps a name a person gave; otherwise a name that says what or where rather than bare dates; otherwise the larger group's. Break up a group Not a group… in the ⋯ menu or the column The Not a group? dialog: the photos go back to their lanes, Everyday and the like, and the organizer does not suggest them as a group again. No photo is removed. Rename E , Rename in the ⋯ menu, or double-click the open group's name Type the name and press Enter ; Esc keeps the old one. Keep a group exactly as it is ⋯ → Open as an album page , then ⋮ → Keep album as is The organizer leaves the group and its files alone. Let the organizer manage album hands it back; Sort in Staging returns to the group in the stream. You can also drag pictures, or a whole group by its grip ⠿, onto another group's header to move or merge them. In a Scans category, groups are runs of scans in their folders, not events: split or merge them instead of using Not a group… , which is refused there.

The organizer looks at a category again a couple of minutes after its files change, and when you choose Group now . Groups can change while files are still arriving and being read, which is what Still indexing warns of. The stream follows along: a group that changes is read again, and one that is removed disappears. What you decide is kept through every one of those runs: Your changes of the groups (splits, moves, new groups, merges, Not a group , names) are kept on every run until you undo them. On the Done tab all but a rename carry the badge kept : "The organizer keeps this change on every run until it is undone". A group whose pictures you changed by hand shows Yours , and the organizer leaves it as it is. Not this album keeps that album away from those photos until you undo it. A group put aside stays in Later until you bring it back. If the organizer changed a group while you were deciding on it, your decision is refused with "it changed while you were deciding; look again". The group comes back with Retry and Dismiss ; look at it again before you decide.

The Files tab shows the category one folder at a time. The line at the top leads back up to the category; subfolders are cards with the number of entries in each. Media shows every picture, video and recording in the folder and its subfolders, by day. Select pictures to use Add to album , Set time , and, when you may change them all, Set location and Label . Folder lists every entry in the folder itself, whatever its type (a PDF, a sidecar file), 200 at a time in name order, with Name , Kind and Size , a box to select each, and Show more . To move or discard a folder or files, use the ⋯ on a folder's card, the Actions button for the folder you are in, or Actions over a selection in Folder : Move to folder… moves it to another folder of the same category. Move to category… moves it into another category (offered when you have more than one). It first leaves the groups of its old category, and its files are dated again by the new category's rules. Discard… moves it to your trash. In the move dialog, choose the Category , step into a folder, and optionally type a name under Into a new folder here . The line under it says where it goes, for example "Into Scans › box-3. Links to them, in albums and suggested groups, follow them." Choose Move here . The Discard dialog says: "They go to your trash, kept together as one entry on the Trash page. Undo, here or on the Done tab, puts them back where they were." Choose Discard ; the message has Undo . An empty category says "Nothing in Box 3 yet" (with its own name) and offers Import media , and the folder to copy into over SFTP.

p.h: Done: what you decided, and Undo
p.x: The Done tab lists what was decided in the category, newest first, 50 at a time ( Show older for more). At the top: "N filed · M discarded". Everything shows every decision; Regrouping shows only the changes you made to the groups. Each row shows when it happened and what it was: "86 files → Christmas at the cottage" with the album as a link, "12 files discarded", "Split “A week in London”", "“Christmas Eve · 24 Dec 1975” is not for Christmas 1975", and so on, with the groups it touched. Badges: only you for a private album, kept for a change the organizer keeps, in part for a decision that stopped part-way. Each row has Undo , or "undone" and the time once it is undone. Undo puts things back: filed files move back into staging, and an album the decision made is removed once it is empty; discarded files come back from the trash, as long as they are still there; the groups get their pictures back, and a change of the groups stops applying; Not this album gives the group its candidates back. The message says "Undone:" and what was undone. A file that was moved after the decision stays where it is: "Undone in part: some files have moved since, and stay where they are". In the Sort tab, Z undoes the decisions of this visit, newest first; one still waiting to be carried out is cancelled instead. With nothing left, it says "Nothing to undo from this visit; the Done tab lists every decision." Later is not listed on Done ; bring a group back from the Later lane instead.

On a phone the Sort tab has no keys, no column beside the stream and no selecting of several groups. Tap a group to open it. Each closed group has its proposal (or New album… ) as a button under its pictures, and the ⋯ menu on each group has every action. More on EiN on a phone .

What you see What it means What to do No groups yet The files are still being read, or the organizer has not grouped them yet Wait a few minutes, or choose Group now under the tab names Still indexing on a group Some of its pictures are still being read Decide later, or go ahead; the group may still change "it changed while you were deciding; look again" The organizer changed the group after you opened it Look at the group, then Retry , or Dismiss "You can't add to “…”." The album is one you may only look at Choose another album, or ask whoever owns it "No proposal: N, A, B or X." EiN has nothing to suggest Choose yourself: a new album, any album, the target, or discard Remove category is greyed out The category still holds files Move or discard its files first "Undone in part: …" Some files were moved after the decision Look for them in the place they were moved to The commands behind these pages, for use in the terminal, are under staging in the Archive commands .

This page is for anyone sorting new pictures in staging. It covers how EiN tells exact copies, look-alikes and bursts apart, where it marks them, and how you remove the copies you do not want. The version you keep is filled in with anything the copies held that it lacks. Everything here happens in your own staging area, before pictures join the shared library. How pictures get there is on Getting your photos in , and the rest of staging is on Sorting in staging .

EiN sorts "the same picture twice" into three kinds and treats each one differently. An exact copy is kept once, a look-alike is yours to judge, and a burst is a stack, never a duplicate Kind What it is When EiN finds it What happens Exact copy The same file, byte for byte: the same photo uploaded twice, or a second copy of an export As the file is read on arrival One copy is kept. The others are not processed, and each one shows its original's picture Look-alike The same picture in other bytes: a smaller version a phone app or cloud service saved, a re-save in another format, a mild crop, a video or recording encoded again Once the file is prepared and its fingerprint is made Marked with how alike the files are, for example "97% alike". EiN suggests the better one, and you decide Burst Several shots taken a moment apart When the pictures are grouped Not a duplicate. The shots are folded into a stack, and nothing is removed EiN compares each new file with the library photos you can open and with the rest of your own staging area, across all your categories. A copy in someone else's staging area, or in a library album you cannot open, does not count. EiN does not take two shots for one picture when their times tell them apart. Two photos whose camera clocks (or GPS times) are a second or more apart are two shots. So are two photos from one camera, of one size and taken in the same second, when the camera recorded different fractions of that second. A picture that looks like thirty or more other files, such as a dark frame or a test chart, counts as alike to none of them.

p.h: An exact copy shows its original
p.x: When a file arrives that is an exact copy of one you can open, in the library or earlier in your staging area, EiN does not process it. It makes no previews, finds no faces and adds nothing to search. Taking in a second copy of a large export therefore costs a moment per file, not minutes. While it stays a copy: the Duplicates tab shows it with its original's picture and size, since the bytes are the same; it joins no suggested group in Sort ; the Media view of the Files tab leaves it out (the Folder view lists every file, copies too); it does not count among the files being prepared. Among identical files in your staging area, the one that arrived first is the original. When you file an original into the library, its copies still in staging become copies of the library photo. When a copy no longer has an original you can open, EiN processes it where it is, like any new file. If you discard the original in staging, this happens at once, and the copy is then grouped like any other file. If the original goes some other way, for example when someone deletes it from the library, it happens within the hour.

In the open group, a picture that copies or looks like another one carries a badge in its corner: Badge Tooltip Means ⧉ "In the library already: compare" It is a copy or look-alike of a photo in the library 2× "Another one here is the same picture: compare" It is a copy or look-alike of another staged photo Click a badge to open Compare for that picture. The open group's header also gets a chip with the totals, for example "⧉ 4 in library · 2× 1". Its menu has these items: Compare opens the first marked picture side by side with its matches. Keep the library copies removes the group's pictures the library already has. It removes only those that need no look: exact copies, and smaller versions of a library photo (see Remove all for what counts). Look-alikes that need a look stay in the group. Select these selects the marked pictures, so you can act on them together. It is offered on a computer. When at least four in five of the open group's pictures are copies or smaller versions of library photos, the group's proposal becomes Keep the library copies · N photos go , marked sure (●●●). Enter removes them, and the rest of the group stays to be sorted. The message says, for example, "12 photos of “Cornwall, summer 1968” removed", with Undo .

In the Media view of a category's Files tab, tiles carry the same ⧉ and 2× badges. A photo that is kept over copies left out of the list also gets 2× , so you can see that it has copies. Click the badge to compare.

When you open one of your own staged pictures in the viewer , its details panel says which sets it belongs to, with one of these lines: "A copy of a library photo" or "A copy of a photo in this import" "Looks like a library photo" or "Looks like a photo in this import" "Kept over 2 copies" or "Kept over 1 look-alike" Under the line are the set's other files as thumbnails, with the kept one marked Kept , and why it is kept. Compare opens the files side by side, and for look-alikes Not duplicates keeps them apart. If you remove the picture you are viewing, the viewer closes.

A burst is not a duplicate, so it has no set to remove. In a suggested group, consecutive photos that look alike and were taken within seconds of each other are folded behind one tile, which shows a stack icon and the number of shots. Each album makes its own stacks the same way once the pictures are filed. The files never move. You can choose the front photo or keep one out of a stack: see Albums . How alike and how close in time the shots must be are two settings an administrator can change, Stack similarity ( CFG_ALBUM_STACK_THRESHOLD , 0.75 by default) and Stack time gap (seconds) ( CFG_ALBUM_STACK_MAX_GAP_SECONDS , 10).

Open Staging , choose a category, and select the Duplicates tab, the second tab after Sort . The number on the tab counts the category's exact copies. Look-alikes are counted inside the tab. The tab reads what EiN already found while the files arrived, so it opens at once however large the category is. At the top, a switch shows four lists, each with its count: List What it holds When it is empty Copies of library photos Staged photos with the same bytes as a photo in the library "No photo of this category is a copy of one in the library." Copies within this import Staged photos with the same bytes as another staged one, which arrived first "No photo of this category is a copy of another one here." Like library photos Staged photos that are the same picture as a library photo, in other bytes "No photo of this category looks like one in the library." Alike within this import Staged photos that are the same picture as each other "No two photos of this category look like one picture." "This import" means your staging area: an original in another of your categories counts too. A category's tab lists the copies that lie in that category. The tab opens on the first list that has something in it. The lists hold videos and recordings as well as photos.

The tab shows one card per set : the file kept and the files it would replace. The card heading says what the set is, for example "2 copies of a library photo", "1 copy of a photo in this import", "1 photo like a library photo" or "2 photos alike in this import". Beside it, a set of look-alikes shows how alike they are ("97% alike"), and every set shows how much space removing the copies frees. Each file is a tile with a label in its corner: Label Means Keep · library The kept file is a library photo. The album holding it is named under the tile Keep The kept file is one of your staged photos Drop This file goes to your trash when you remove the set Elsewhere A file of the set that this removal leaves alone, for example a copy in another category (dimmed) Under each tile are its picture size, file size and the time it was taken. A copy that holds something the kept file lacks says so, for example "gives description, labels". Under the tiles, one line says why the kept file is kept and what it gains, for example "kept: it is in the library · the kept one gains: description, star". Yellow lines warn of anything to look out for. They are listed under When something looks wrong .

A library photo is always kept: nothing in staging removes or changes a library photo, except to fill it in. Between your staged files, EiN keeps these: In a set of exact copies, the file that arrived first ("kept: it came first"). In a set of look-alikes, the better picture, by the first of these rules that tells two apart: Rule What the line says More pixels "kept: it has more pixels (4032×3024 over 1600×1200)" A better format: RAW, then HEIC, then TIFF or PNG, then JPEG, then WebP, then GIF "kept: its format is better" A surer time: typed in by hand, then GPS, then the camera's clock, then a sidecar, then the file name "kept: its time is surer" The larger file "kept: it is the larger file" A name that is not a copy's, such as one without (2) , a trailing -1 or copy "kept: its name is not a copy’s" Otherwise, the one that arrived first "kept: it came first" When you pick another one yourself, the line says "kept: you chose it".

Removing a set merges the copies into the kept file before they go. The kept file is filled in, never overwritten . From the copies it takes a description, a time typed in by hand, a place or a sidecar when it has none, the labels and your star when it lacks them, and the copies' people, comments and albums. The line "the kept one gains: …" lists what it will get. The copies then leave your suggested groups. When the kept file is staged in the same category, it takes a copy's place in its group. The copies go to your trash together, as one entry.

p.h: Remove the copies of one set
p.x: Open Staging , choose the category, and select the Duplicates tab. Choose a list at the top. Look at a set. If you are not sure which file is better, click Compare . Click Remove 1 copy (for exact copies) or Remove 1 photo (for look-alikes). The button gives the number of files that go. The set leaves the list at once, and a message says how many files were removed, for example "2 removed", with Undo . While removals are still running, "◌ 2 applying" shows at the top. To keep a different staged file, click Keep this one under its tile. It is offered in sets within this import and in sets of look-alikes. EiN keeps that file and removes the other staged files of the set. A library photo stays whichever file you pick. On a computer you can work through the list with the keyboard: Key What it does J / K Mark the next or previous set Enter Remove the marked set's copies C Compare the marked set Z Undo the last removal of this visit Clicking a set marks it too. All keys are on Keyboard shortcuts .

Compare opens a set's files large, side by side. You can open it from the Duplicates tab, from a badge in Sort or on the Files tab, and from the viewer. The dialog is titled Copies or Look-alikes . Under the title, the set's likeness and why the kept file is kept appear, for example "97% alike · kept: it has more pixels (4032×3024 over 1600×1200)". Each file is labelled Keep · library , Keep , Drop , Library (a library photo that stays) or Stays . Under each are its picture size, file size, the time it was taken, the camera, and how alike it is. When a file has exact copies of its own, "and 2 byte copies" says so: they go with it when it is removed. Key What it does ← / → Move between the files K Keep the file in focus instead (staged files only) Enter Remove the others X Not duplicates (look-alikes only) Esc Close without changing anything The buttons at the bottom do the same: Not duplicates (for look-alikes), Cancel and Remove the others . On a phone, tap a file to focus it and use the buttons.

p.h: Say that two pictures are not duplicates
p.x: Look-alikes can be wrong: two photos of the same view, or two shots of one moment that the camera did not time apart. Click Not duplicates on the set, in Compare or in the viewer. The set leaves the list, and the message "Kept apart: not duplicates" has Undo . EiN remembers the choice on each staged file and never pairs those files again. This choice is not listed on the Done tab, so the message's Undo is the only way back in the web interface. Exact copies cannot be kept apart, since their bytes are the same.

p.h: Remove a whole list at once
p.x: Three lists have a button at the top that resolves every set needing no look: List Button What it removes Copies of library photos Remove all N copies… Every copy Copies within this import Remove all N copies… Every copy but the one kept Like library photos Remove all smaller versions… Only staged photos that are smaller versions of a library photo, at least 95% alike, and that cannot be two shots of a burst Alike within this import has no such button: those sets are for you to look at one by one. Choose the list and click its Remove all button. Read the dialog, for example Remove all copies of library photos? It explains that each copy goes to your trash once the kept file is filled in. It also says that a set whose kept file is gone, or that you cannot fill in, is left as it is. Click Remove 120 copies (or Remove them for smaller versions), or Cancel . A bar shows the progress, for example "Removing copies of library photos: 40 copies so far, 80 left". Stop ends the run once the batch being removed is done; the button reads Stopping… until then. When the run ends, one message says how many copies were removed and has Undo for the whole run. Each set is checked again right before it is removed, so a set that changed meanwhile is left alone.

Nothing is deleted outright. Every removal can be taken back: with Undo in the message that follows it; with Z on the Duplicates tab or in Sort , for removals made during this visit; from the Done tab, where each removal is one entry, for example "3 copies of 2 photos removed", with Undo . See Sorting in staging . Undo brings the copies back where they were, with their places in their groups, and they are listed as copies again. What the kept file gained stays, since it overwrote nothing. Each removal is also one entry on your Trash page, named for example "Duplicates from Phone: 3 copies". Undo is the better way back, because it also puts the copies back into their groups. The Trash page is described on Your profile, favourites and trash .

What you see What it means What to do "perhaps two shots of a burst: same size, same camera, same second" The files may be two shots rather than one picture twice Compare them. If they differ, click Not duplicates "a staged one has more pixels than the library’s" Your new file is larger than the library photo, but the library photo is still the one kept To keep both, click Not duplicates and file your photo like any other. You can then remove the smaller one from its album yourself, as Albums describes "files in other folders stay" A copy lies in another category Remove it from that category's Duplicates tab "its original is gone or changed: nothing is dropped" The kept file is no longer there with the same bytes. Remove is greyed out Nothing to do.
