A video shorter than 2 seconds gets none: its still already shows it all; makes the small pictures you see when you move along the timeline, and finds where one shot cuts to the next, which become its chapters ( Play a video ); finds the faces in it, and works out what it shows; writes down what is said in it and recognises who says it, so that search finds the words and the viewer can show subtitles; takes a fingerprint, which finds copies and look-alikes. The viewer plays the AV1 version, not the original. A browser or device that cannot play AV1 says so; the original can still be downloaded. If a video is too long or too heavy for the media service to convert within its limits, which can happen on a machine without a graphics card, it gets no playable version. Use Download to watch it on your own device.

EiN recognises M4A (what phone voice memos are), MP3, WAV, FLAC, Ogg and Opus, and AMR. M4B audiobooks count as recordings too. For each recording, EiN: reads its date, where the file has one; makes a version your browser plays: AAC at no more than 128 kbit/s and 44.1 kHz, in an .m4a file; draws a picture of the sound, its waveform, which is the recording's tile and what you see while it plays; writes down what is said in it and recognises who says it ( Listen to a recording ); takes a fingerprint of the sound, which finds the same recording twice. A recording shorter than about 2.5 seconds gets none. A recording's tile and player show a picture of its sound, and the transcript beside it is searchable.

EiN reads the text of PDF files and of plain text files, so that search finds a document by what it is about: a search for Christmas letter finds the family newsletter of 2019. See Search and the finder . PDF. EiN reads the text the PDF holds. A page with almost no text, such as a scanned letter, is read as a picture instead, handwriting included. At most 40 pages of one PDF are read this way; the pages after that keep only the text they hold. Plain text. Any file that is text, whatever its name: .txt , a Markdown note, an HTML page. An SVG drawing is text too, so EiN treats it as a document, not as a picture. Copied in over SFTP, a .md or .html file takes the type its name gives instead, and its text is not read. A document's text is read once the file is in an album or elsewhere in the library, not while it waits in staging. Files in folders whose name starts with a dot, such as the trash, are not read. Documents have no thumbnail: they show as a plain tile, and the viewer has no reader for them. Use Download to open one on your device. The Documents choice on the Media page also lists RTF files, but EiN does not read their text: search finds them by their file name only. An old Word ( .doc ) file is not recognised at all and is kept as one of the other files .

The media service can read the text of Word ( .docx ) and OpenDocument ( .odt ) files, but EiN recognises a file by its first bytes, and these formats begin like any zip file. A .docx or .odt file you upload is therefore kept as a zip file (one copied in over SFTP keeps its type, and its text is read): its text is not read, so search finds it by its name only; in a staging category, it is expanded like any other zip, into the parts it is made of, and the file itself is removed. To keep such a document whole and findable, save it as a PDF before you bring it in. To keep the Word file itself, upload it straight into an album rather than into staging ( Upload straight into the album ).

A sidecar is a small file beside a picture that says things about it: the JSON file Google Photos writes beside every photo and video of a Takeout, such as IMG_0001.jpg.supplemental-metadata.json ; the XMP file a photo editor or a scanning tool writes, IMG_0001.jpg.xmp or IMG_0001.xmp . A sidecar is not a picture or a document of its own. In staging, EiN pairs it with its picture and moves it under it, and the picture takes its date, its place where the file has no GPS position, and its caption. A Google Takeout export shows what each part of a Takeout becomes. A sidecar that matches no picture stays where it is, among the category's Other files .

A GPX file is a route recorded by a GPS tracker, a watch or a tracking app. In staging it is not a picture: EiN adds its points to the track of the device that recorded it, and the file goes. On a device's page you can upload GPX files to its track directly. See GPX files in staging and Upload a GPX file to a device's track .

A zip file that you upload or copy anywhere into a staging category is expanded once its upload has ended: what it holds goes into the folder the zip lies in, and the zip is removed. Outside staging, for example uploaded into an album, a zip stays a zip. Zips and Google Takeout exports has the details. Only zip files are expanded. A .tar , .7z or .rar archive is kept as it is.

Any other file is kept as it came, with its name and size, and nothing is made from it. In staging it counts among the category's Other files , and the Folder view of the Files tab lists it, where you can move or discard it ( Sorting in staging ). It does not appear on the Media page, in albums' grids or in search by content. You reach it over SFTP or in the terminal , and an administrator also on the Nodes page. Some media formats are among these, because EiN does not recognise them from their first bytes: Format Usual extension Windows Media video and audio .wmv , .wma AIFF audio .aif , .aiff AAC audio outside an M4A file .aac JPEG XL .jxl To have EiN work with such a file, convert it on your own computer first: a video to MP4, a sound to M4A, FLAC or WAV, a JPEG XL picture to JPEG or PNG.

p.h: Your originals stay as they are
p.x: EiN never changes the bytes of the file you uploaded. Thumbnails, playable versions, transcripts, read text and everything else it works out are kept beside the file. When you correct a date, turn a picture or write its text by hand, EiN changes what it keeps, not the file. Download in the viewer, and the file name at the top of its details panel, always give you the original.

p.h: When a file does not show up as expected
p.x: What you see Why What to do A new picture shows a plain tile with a picture icon Its thumbnails are not made yet. Wait. A large import keeps the media service busy for a long while. A file you uploaded into staging is counted under Other files EiN did not recognise it as a picture, video or recording: a document, a sidecar, or a format from the table above. Look at it in the Folder view of the Files tab. Convert an unrecognised media file and upload it again. A video or recording says "This file cannot be played" The file is damaged: nothing can read it. The reason is under the message. Download it and check it on your own device. A video says "This browser or device cannot play AV1, the format this video is in." The browser cannot play the format EiN makes playable videos in. Use a current browser, or Download the original. A document is not found by its words It is still in staging, it is a format whose text EiN does not read, or it is a .docx or .odt kept as a zip. File it into an album. Save Word and OpenDocument files as PDF. A .docx file in staging turned into a folder of XML files It was expanded as a zip. Discard the parts, and bring the document in as a PDF or upload it straight into an album. A RAW file is shown as an ordinary picture with no RAW detail Its sensor data could not be read, so it is shown from the preview inside it. Nothing is lost: the original is kept, and Download gives it to you. Viewing photos, videos and recordings covers the viewer's other messages.

mime shows the type EiN stored for a file, the type its name suggests, and the type its first bytes say, and whether it counts as camera RAW: # in EiN's terminal mime "/archive/albums/Christmas in Wellington/IMG_0412.HEIC" stored: image/heic ext: image/heic content: image/heic raw: no A file whose stored line says application/octet-stream was not recognised; one that says application/zip is kept as a zip. Two commands do a file's reading again, for a file you may change: Command What it does exif-extract -f <file> Reads a photo's, video's or recording's date, place and camera again. A file marked as unreadable is tried again. index-document -f <file> Reads a document's text again. Every command and its options are in the archive's command reference and the core command reference .

Getting your photos in : every way to bring files into EiN, and what happens next. Sorting in staging : where uploaded files wait until you file them. Viewing photos, videos and recordings : how each kind of file is shown and played. Search and the finder : finding files by what they show, say and contain. Duplicates : copies and look-alikes, and which format is kept. Files and storage : how EiN stores files and what it keeps beside them. The media service : the part of EiN that does the reading.

This page is for the administrator of an EiN with the Archive installed. It covers the work the Archive does on every photo, video, recording and document that arrives: its pipelines, the workers that run them, the settings that decide how much runs at once, and the commands that run the work again. The pipelines run in core's engine. Processing and pipelines covers the engine itself: watching the work on the Dashboard and in the terminal, failed work and how it is run again, the bulk lane, and the engine's own settings.

When a file arrives, the Archive's archive-bridge service turns the change into an event that a new file is there, media.file.discovered . That starts media-ingest , which reads the file's metadata; every other media pipeline waits on it, and starts once the metadata is read. Changes and pipelines follows one upload from start to finish. The Archive runs these services for its processing: Service What it does archive-bridge Turns changes into the events the media pipelines wait for cpu The worker for work done on this machine, such as reading metadata, making thumbnails and transcoding video models The worker for work done by a model in the media service , such as finding faces or transcribing speech models-second A second model worker beside models , when CFG_MODEL_SECOND_SLOTS is above 0 ; it is off by default media-heal Finds files that are missing something and announces them again (see Close gaps the pipelines missed ) Its other services, which keep albums, person covers, label suggestions and staging up to date, are listed in Services and logs . Most of the model work and much of the media work are calls into the media service: without it, those steps wait, and their kinds show waiting for EMS on the Dashboard .

Pipeline What it does Kind of work media-ingest Reads a photo's, video's or recording's metadata. Every other media pipeline waits on it. ingest media-reindex Reads the metadata again for a file whose bytes changed ingest media-stills A photo's display sizes and face crops, a video's poster frames, a recording's waveform stills media-transcode Video and audio the browser can play, a video's hover clip, storyboard and chapters transcode , stills , shots media-fingerprint The fingerprints that find duplicates and photo stacks fingerprint media-faces Finds the faces in a photo and crops each one faces media-video-faces Finds the faces in a video and when each is on screen faces media-face-assign Matches a found face to a person face-assign media-embed-picture A picture vector, for searching by what is in the picture embed-picture media-ocr Reads the text written in a picture ocr media-embed-text Text vectors of a file's stored texts embed-text media-transcribe A transcript of what is said in a video or recording transcribe media-voiceprint Who speaks when in a recording, with a voiceprint per voice diarize media-speaker-assign Decides which person each voice is speaker-assign media-speaker-faces Ties a video's voices to the faces seen speaking them, once its faces are found diarize , speaker-assign media-device Links a file to the camera or phone that took it run by the engine media-geocode Looks up the address of a file's GPS position run by the engine media-album An album's stacks, time span, missing cover and profile, when its members change run by the engine media-duplicates Decides again the duplicate findings of a staged file dedupe location-link-point Links a photo to the location that contains its GPS point run by the engine location-upkeep Redraws a location and relinks the photos inside it when it or its photos change run by the engine document-index Extracts the text of a document and makes it searchable run by the engine staging-unzip Expands a zip that lands in a staging category, then removes the zip unzip staging-sidecars Pairs Takeout and XMP sidecars with their files sidecars staging-organize Plans a staging category's suggested groups again organize staging-retime Dates staged files again by the rules of the category they were moved into retime track-stage Makes a GPX file dropped in staging into its device's route run by the engine

Every kind of work above that is not run by the engine goes as a job into the pool /var/pools/media , where the Archive's workers take it: cpu takes unzip , ingest , stills , face-assign , speaker-assign , fingerprint , dedupe , retime , organize , sidecars and transcode . models takes faces , embed-picture , ocr , embed-text , transcribe , diarize and shots , and models-second the same kinds in the reverse order. When a worker is stopped and no other takes its kinds, they show no worker on the Dashboard , and the work waits until it starts again; Work that nothing will run says what to do.

These settings are in the Processing category of Settings → System , or set with config set , and come with the Archive. Saving one restarts the worker that reads it, and work in progress is picked up again. Configuration explains how. Setting Default What it decides CFG_CPU_SLOTS 2 How much CPU work the cpu worker runs at once. A transcode takes two slots, other kinds one. CFG_CPU_NON_ENTRY_SLOTS 1 Slots kept first for work after ingest, so a long import does not hold back thumbnails and faces. Ingest borrows them when nothing else waits. CFG_CPU_WORKERS 4 The most CPU jobs in flight; the slots are the real limit CFG_MODEL_SLOTS 2 Requests the models worker keeps in flight against the media service. Size it to what the media service runs at once. CFG_MODEL_SECOND_SLOTS 0 Requests the models-second worker keeps in flight; 0 leaves it off. Size both workers' slots together against the media service. CFG_MODEL_KIND_QUANTUM_MS 3600000 How long the models worker stays on one kind before turning to the next, so faces do not starve the rest; models-second takes a change at its next start Tip More CFG_MODEL_SLOTS than the media service runs at once only moves the wait into its queue, and past its depth into waiting for EMS . With models-second on, the media service holds two families of models at once, and both must fit on its graphics card, or one runs on the processor. Performance and sizing says what to set on a small or a large machine, and Change how it works , on the media service's page, how many model requests the media service admits at once, EMS_LIMIT_MODELS .

You want to Run Run one pipeline on one file pipeline-start media-faces /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_2041.jpg Transcode a video again although it has renditions pipeline-start --var FORCE=-f media-transcode /archive/albums/christmas-2019/MVI_0412.mp4 Make the renditions again under a folder, without the pipelines regenerate --force /archive/albums/christmas-2019 Announce files the Archive never saw, or that are missing work media-scan /archive/albums Embed the stored texts and transcripts again, as they are media-reembed Encode the face crops again without finding the faces again regenerate-face-crops --limit 200 media-transcode , media-transcribe , media-embed-picture and media-ocr declare FORCE , which -f makes them redo work already done. pipeline-start is core's; the other commands are the Archive's, and Archive commands lists their options.

media-scan walks a folder and announces each file that was never taken in, or that lacks something a pipeline should have given it: a fingerprint, display sizes, faces, renditions, or a transcript made with other settings than the media service runs now. Each pipeline then skips what is already done. The media-heal service runs it for you, but only when nothing is waiting in the pools, so a scan never repeats what is already on its way. It looks every CFG_MEDIA_HEAL_INTERVAL seconds (900), and after a pass through the whole archive it rests for CFG_MEDIA_HEAL_REST seconds (21600, six hours). Run it by hand after installing the Archive on files that were already there, or to look at one folder: # in EiN's terminal media-scan -n /archive/albums/christmas-2019 # only report what it would announce media-scan /archive/albums/christmas-2019 A run examines up to 20000 files ( --scan-limit ) and announces up to 1000 ( --limit ), and remembers where it stopped, so the next run goes on from there; --restart starts from the top. It announces fewer as running media-ingest instances and waiting triggers add up, and nothing once they reach 500 ( --max-active ). CFG_MEDIA_TRANSCRIPTS_CURRENT set to off stops transcripts from being made again when the media service's speech settings change. On a large archive such a change otherwise means hours of background work.

p.h: Large imports and the bulk lane
p.x: Work on a staging category of the Google Photos export or Scans kind runs in core's bulk lane , below all other work, so what people upload in the meantime is processed first. Any category can be put in that lane with staging category <name> --lane bulk , which applies to work announced from then on. Staging for administrators covers categories.

This page is for the administrator who looks after the staging areas where everyone's uploads wait: how they are laid out, the background work that reads and groups what arrives, how to plan an import of tens of thousands of files, the finer settings of a category, and the staging command for checking and repairing a person's staging area. How family members upload and sort is on Getting your photos in and Sorting in staging .

Every account has its own staging area in its home, /home/<username>/staging . Files wait there, seen only by their owner, until the owner files them into an album or discards them. The Archive module provides staging; without the archive module there is none (see Modules ). /home/helen/staging/ files/<category>/… the staged files, in any folders below a category albums/<category>/<slug> the suggested albums (groups) for that category's files journal/<id> one entry per decision, with the plan that undoes it routes/ GPX files waiting for the device that recorded them Part What it is files/inbox The default category. It is always there and cannot be removed; uploads from the Media page go here. files/<category> Any other category, one folder each. Its name is its key and never changes. Its settings are kept on the folder. albums/<category>/ The groups the organizer suggests, as albums whose members are links to the staged files. It also holds the organizer's checkpoint, .organizer . journal/ Every decision: filing, discarding, removing copies, changing the groups and "not this album". Entries are never deleted; each is undone from the Done tab or with staging undo . routes/ GPX tracks that name no device EiN knows, until their owner says which device recorded them. Every directory of a staging area is mode 0700 and owned by the account, and staging/ is marked unlisted. Nobody else can open it, find it in a search or see it on the map, and the library's own views (the Media page, the map, On this day, search) leave it out even for its owner until the files are filed. The administrator passes every permission check, other people's staging included, as root does; Permissions in depth explains why the 0700 folder is enough. The background work runs with administrative access, so it reads and processes staged files like any others. EiN sets no limit on how much one person's staging area holds. Staged files take room on the same disk as the library; df in the terminal shows the free space.

p.h: When a staging area is set up
p.x: A new account has no staging area until one of these sets it up: the person opens Staging in the web interface, or drops files on a page that uploads into staging; the staging-organizer service, which sets up every account's staging area once an hour; you, with staging init . Someone who wants to copy files in over SFTP before opening Staging finds no /home/<username>/staging yet. Have them open Staging once, or set it up for them: # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator staging init --user ruby ruby: 7 created, 0 repaired, 0 adopted, 0 moved, 0 groups, 0 routes, 0 relinked staging init makes the directories with their modes and owner, marks staging/ unlisted and makes the Inbox. It also puts right what is out of place, moving each thing with every link to it following, so albums and suggestions keep pointing at it: Found What staging init does A folder directly under files/ Adopts it as a category of the generic kind ( Other in the web interface), named after it. A file directly in files/ Moves it into files/inbox/unsorted/ , or the folder --loose-batch names. A group directly in albums/ Moves it into albums/inbox/ . A GPX file waiting for a device Moves it into routes/ . A name already taken where something moves gets -2 , -3 . Run again, it finds nothing to do. Option What it does --user <name> Sets up that person's staging area. Without it, your own. --all Every account's. --loose-batch <name> The Inbox folder that loose files of files/ move into, instead of unsorted . --idle-minutes <n> Leaves a loose file of files/ where it is when it changed within the last n minutes, so a copy still being written is not moved. The service passes 360 . --layout-only Makes the directories and categories and moves nothing. The Staging page runs this. --dry-run Says what it would do and does none of it.

Nothing in staging needs you to start it. Each step below is a pipeline that starts on its own when files arrive or change, or a service that runs on a timer. All of them run in EiN's pipeline engine, which Processing and pipelines covers. Pipeline or service Starts when What it does staging-unzip A zip anywhere in a category has finished uploading Expands it into the folder it lies in ( unzip -n ), then removes it. One zip at a time. staging-sidecars A Google Takeout JSON or an XMP file lands in a category that pairs sidecars, about 30 seconds after the last one Pairs each sidecar with its photo or video ( media-sidecars ), which gives the picture its date, place and caption. One run at a time. media-ingest and the media work A file lands Reads its date, place and camera, and checks whether it is an exact copy; then the thumbnails, faces, fingerprints and the rest, through the media service . staging-retime Files move into a category with other time rules, about 10 seconds after the last one Dates them again by the rules of the category they are in now ( staging retime ). staging-organize A category's files arrive, leave, move or are read, or someone asks for a run; held two minutes Plans the category's groups again where its files changed, and writes what differs ( staging organize ). track-stage A .gpx file lands anywhere in staging Adds its points to the track of the device it names and removes the file; one that names no known device waits for its owner. staging-organizer (service) Every 15 minutes Asks for an organizer run of each category that something waits for, and matches the groups due a match against the library's albums. staging-organizer (service) Every hour Sets up every account's staging area and moves a file copied loose into files/ , once nothing has changed on it for six hours, into files/inbox/unsorted/ ( staging init --all --idle-minutes 360 ); and checks every duplicate finding against where its file is now ( staging duplicates --repair --all ). The organizer reads what changed since its last run and plans only that again. A run while another is going folds into one more run, so a large upload does not queue thousands of them. A category gets a full build on its first run, when its grouping settings change, and once a week. Text in pictures and documents is the one piece of work that waits: it is read when a file is filed, not while it is staged. To see the work, look at the Dashboard ( Health and the dashboard ), or in the terminal: # in EiN's terminal health pipeline-instances -s failed staging-unzip service-status staging-organizer

p.h: Look at a person's staging area
p.x: staging status reads a staging area without changing it: per category, its media, its other files (anything that is not a picture, video or recording), those still being read and those without a date. # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator staging status --user helen inbox: 1204 media, 37 other, 212 indexing, 18 undated google-photos: 48210 media, 1391 other, 30544 indexing, 66 undated 1 route(s) waiting for a device A staging area that was never set up answers helen: not initialized; run staging init . With JSON_OUTPUT=1 the answer also holds the bytes, each category's organizer summary, the exact copies by where their originals are, and how many files were filed and discarded. Other commands that only read: Command What it shows staging category <name> --user <name> One category: what it is called, its kind, its default album, whether it is in the bulk lane, its media. staging journal [<category>] --user <name> The decisions, newest first, 50 a page, with the totals filed and discarded. staging detect --user <name> What the newest folders in the Inbox look like: a Google export, scans, a phone and so on. staging duplicates --counts --user <name> How many copies and look-alikes the staging area holds, by where the originals are. staging check --user <name> What breaks the layout's rules (see Put a staging area right ).

A browser upload suits a few thousand files. For a whole Google Takeout, a scanned collection or years of a phone's pictures, copy the files in over SFTP and let EiN work through them. Check the disk. Run df . The files need their own size, and a zip needs room for what it holds and a tenth more while it is expanded. A zip that does not fit is left as it is. Make a category for the source , of the kind closest to it. On the Staging page this is the New category card; in the terminal, as the person or for them: # in EiN's terminal staging category google-photos --create --kind google-photos --user helen The Google Photos export and Scans kinds put their files in the bulk lane: their reading, thumbnails, faces and the rest wait behind all other work, so what anyone uploads to an Inbox meanwhile is ready first, and the import goes on whenever nothing else waits. Copy the files into the category's folder , never into files/ itself. Keep a folder above the event folders: a folder's name becomes a suggested album only when it lies two or more levels below the category. # on your own computer scp -P 2222 takeout-001.zip takeout-002.zip helen@ein.local:/home/helen/staging/files/google-photos/ Zips can go in as they are: each is expanded where it lands, and the parts of one Takeout fill one tree. Getting your photos in has the details the person copying needs, and SSH and SFTP the connection. Let it run. staging status --user helen shows how many files are still being read. The Dashboard reads Catching up while work waits and gets done. A file that is an exact copy of one its owner can already open is recorded as a copy and processed no further, so a second copy of an export costs little. Sort. The groups appear on the category's Sort tab as the files are read; its owner files them as Sorting in staging describes. Tip One category per source keeps an export's files together and lets its kind decide how they are dated and grouped. A source already copied into the Inbox can be moved into a category of its own afterwards, with Move to category… on the Files tab or staging move ; the files are dated again by the new category's rules. How fast the work goes depends on the machine and the graphics card; see Performance and sizing .

p.h: Change the finer settings of a category
p.x: The web interface changes a category's name, kind and default album. The rest of its settings are changed with staging category . A person may change their own categories; an administrator may change anyone's with --user . Option Values What it decides --kind <kind> inbox , google-photos , scans , phone , camera , messaging , screenshots , generic What it holds; only the Inbox is of the inbox kind. A new kind resets every other setting, the label too, to that kind's, but for the default album and what the same command sets. --label <text> The name the pages show. --destination <album> an album's path The library album its files are filed into by default. --no-destination clears it. --strategy <strategy> events , folders , none How its files are grouped: by time and place, by folder and runs of file names, or into monthly lanes only. --significance <level> fewer , normal , more How readily a day becomes a group of its own rather than part of an Everyday lane. --digitized on|off on , off On: the files are scans, and no clock recorded while digitizing them (the scanner, a GPS fix, the file name) dates them. --filename-dates on|off on , off On: a date the file name spells, such as IMG_20190601_123456.jpg , dates a file when nothing better does. --lane <lane> normal , bulk bulk runs the work on its files below all other work. It applies to work announced from then on, within a minute; work already queued keeps its place. --sidecars <mode> pair , ignore Whether Google Takeout JSON and XMP files arriving from then on are paired with their files. --create Makes the category. Its name is lowercase letters, digits and dashes. --remove Removes it. Only an empty category other than the Inbox can be removed. What each kind starts with: Kind Grouping digitized filename-dates Lane Sidecars inbox events off on normal pair google-photos events off off bulk pair scans folders on off bulk pair phone events off on normal pair camera events off off normal pair messaging none off on normal ignore screenshots none off on normal ignore generic events off off normal pair A change of --digitized or --filename-dates dates the category's files again before the command answers. A change of --strategy or --significance asks for an organizer run, which regroups the files within minutes. # in EiN's terminal staging category inbox --significance more --user helen staging category old-phone --lane bulk --user helen inbox: Inbox (inbox); 1204 media, changed group old-phone: Old phone (phone), bulk lane; 8730 media, changed lane Dates and places of pictures explains what the time rules mean for the person sorting.

staging check lists what breaks the layout's rules and changes nothing. It checks up to 20,000 of the groups' links. # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator staging check --user helen 0 problem(s); 3120 link(s) checked Each problem is a line <code>: <path>: <detail> : Code What it means missing A directory of the layout is not there. not-directory Something other than a directory stands where one should be. mode , owner A directory has another mode than 0700 , or another owner. not-unlisted staging/ is not marked unlisted, so the library's views would show it. loose-entry Something lies directly in files/ or albums/ . no-inbox The Inbox category is missing. orphan-albums A folder of groups has no category. cross-category A group links to a file outside its own category. dangling-link A group links to nothing. waiting-route A GPX file waits for its device outside routes/ . staging init --user <name> puts right all but the two kinds of link. A group's broken links are put right by the next full organizer run, which you can start at once: # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator staging organize inbox --user helen --full Other repairs, each for one person with --user or, where marked, everyone with --all : Command When to use it staging organize [<category>…] --full The groups look wrong or stale. Plans the whole category again instead of what changed. --dry-run says what it would do. --all for everyone. staging organize [<category>…] --queue Asks the pipeline for a run instead of running one here; this is the Group now button. staging retime [<category or folder>] Dates look wrong after files were moved or settings changed. Dates the files again by their category's rules. --dry-run counts and writes nothing. staging duplicates --repair Copies are marked against the wrong original after files were moved outside staging. The service does this every hour. --all for everyone. staging duplicates --refresh [<folder>] Files have no duplicate finding. Has each one checked again, 5,000 a call; --force checks every file, --dry-run counts them. media-sidecars <folder> Sidecars were not paired, for example in a category set to ignore that you have since set to pair . A second run finds nothing to do. media-scan /home/<name>/staging/files Files stay unread after a crash, with the media service answering and nothing waiting. Announces the files that miss work. Run it only when the engine is idle: while work waits, it announces again what is already on its way.

--user <name> makes any staging subcommand act on that person's staging area, which only an administrator may; a member of the sudo group must first elevate with Administer… in the account menu, or admin in the terminal ( Permissions in depth ). --all works only for init , organize , match and duplicates --repair ; any other subcommand answers, for example, staging status: --all is only for init, organize, match and duplicates --repair; name one user with --user . A decision you make in someone's staging area, such as staging discard or staging promote , goes into their journal and shows on their Done tab, where they can undo it, and so can you: # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator staging journal inbox --user helen -- limit 10 staging undo 01JA2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9J0K1M2N --user helen Removing copies is the owner's alone: the copies go to the trash of whoever runs it, so staging dedupe for someone else answers staging dedupe: staging dedupe moves copies to your own trash: run it as helen . Archive commands lists every subcommand and option.

A person's /home/<name>/staging does not exist. Their staging area is not set up yet. Run staging init --user <name> , or have them open Staging once. A zip is still a zip. Look at the failed staging-unzip runs with pipeline-instances -s failed staging-unzip and pipeline-status <id> . The step's error says why: not enough space: … when the disk lacks room for what it holds and a tenth more, refusing entry '…': it would land outside … for an unsafe archive, or a file of another size is there when a file of that name is in the folder already. Free space or move the clashing file, then expand it by hand: unzip -d <folder> <zip> goes on where the last run stopped, and -o writes over the files there. Files stay "being prepared" for hours. A large import takes hours, and a bulk-lane category waits behind all other work. If staging status shows the indexing count not going down at all, see whether the media service answers ( The media service ) and whether the Dashboard says Stuck . The Sort tab stays at "No groups yet" though the files are read. Ask for a run with staging organize <category> --user <name> --queue ; it answers helen/inbox: run asked for at … . If no groups come, run it here without --queue to see its answer or its error, and look at service-status staging-organizer . Scans have dates they should not have, or phone pictures lack them. The category has the wrong time rules for its files. Change them with --digitized or --filename-dates , which dates the files again at once. An export's sidecars were not paired. The category is of the Messaging or Screenshots kind, or set to --sidecars ignore . Set --sidecars pair and run media-sidecars on the folder. A person left with files in staging. Deleting an account deletes its home, staging included; see Accounts and groups . File or move what should be kept first.

This page is for power users and administrators who use the Archive from the terminal. Each table row gives a task, a command line that does it, and a link to that command's full entry. The commands come with the Archive and are there once it is installed; The Archive says what it adds, and Commands by task has core's commands and how to read the tables. EiN runs most of the analysis by itself after an upload; the commands here are for looking things up, changing them by hand, and doing one thing again. Albums , People and faces and the other guide pages show the same tasks in the web interface.

Manage albums (create, info, list, set, add files) reads only album [--name=<string>] [--share=<string>] [--create] [--description=<string>] [--cover=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--cursor=<string>] <subcommand> <path> <files>... Argument What it is <subcommand> create | info | list | set | add. <path> album path. <files>... add: the files to put in the album: linked, or moved there out of staging; info: more albums, up to 50 in all. Option What it does --name=<string> create, add --create: the album display name (defaults to the slug) --share=<string> create, add --create: who sees it (default, private, shared, everyone; default: as your new albums are) --create add: make the album first when it is not there. --description=<string> album description (create) --cover=<string> cover media path (create) --limit=<string> albums per list page (max 1000) --cursor=<string> list: the last name of the page before (pages are in the store's name order) album info /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album info /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /archive/albums/Sommar_2020 album create /archive/albums/Nytt_Exempelalbum --name 'Nytt exempelalbum' album set /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 spanStart 2019-05-30 album set /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 next /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2020 album create /archive/albums/Stugan --name 'Stugan' --share private album add /archive/albums/Sommar_2020 /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg --create --name 'Sommar 2020' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : for info , each album's list row with its id, cover, neighbours in a series and child count, a suggested album's parts and candidate albums, and the paths that name none (AlbumInfoAnswer); for list , the albums under a root, a suggested album's with what staging decides it by and its best match (AlbumListResult); for add , the files linked and moved and where each now files, whether it made the album, and the staging journal entries that undo the moves (AlbumAddResult); for create and set , nothing.

Give an album without a cover a random one of its own pictures (coverPhoto softlink) changes things album-cover [--all] [--stale] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every album in the tree but the staging suggestions. --stale only albums that have no cover yet (the default; accepted for symmetry with album-span) --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print each album as it is written. album-cover /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-cover --all --stale -- limit 50 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink is written for each album that had none.

Build the profile staging matches suggested groups against, beside each library album as its .profile: its members' times, days, places and people, and the pictures that stand for it. changes things album-profile [--all] [--stale] [--force] <album>... Argument What it is <album>... library albums to profile; anything else is passed over. Option What it does --all every library album, a page at a time. --stale with --all: only albums with no profile, or one not checked for a week. --force build again even when the members are as they were. album-profile /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-profile --all album-profile --all --stale With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many albums were looked at, how many profiles were written, already current and passed over, how long it took, and the albums that failed (AlbumProfileResult).
The path of one album somebody made, at random. reads only album-random

Write an album's time span (timeStart/timeEnd/mediaCount) onto the album node: its media's, widened to the days set by hand (spanStart/spanEnd) changes things album-span [--all] [--stale] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every album in the tree but the staging suggestions. --stale only albums that have no span yet. --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print each album as it is written. --dry-run answer each album's span and its media's without writing. album-span /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-span --all --stale album-span --dry-run /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many albums were scanned and updated, and each written album (each scanned one with --dry-run): its span, media count, first and last capture, and the hand-set ends still in force.

Reconcile album-local stacks of consecutive, perceptually similar photos. changes things album-stack [--all] [--dry-run] [--threshold=<number>] [--max-gap-seconds=<number>] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <action> <album> <file> Argument What it is <action> refresh, front, separate, allow, stack or unstack. <album> album path. <file> member path for front/separate/allow/unstack; two or more for stack. Option What it does --all refresh every album but the staging suggestions. --dry-run report without writing manifests or links. --threshold=<number> minimum cosine of adjacent photos' SSCD fingerprints (default 0.75) --max-gap-seconds=<number> maximum adjacent capture-time gap (default 10) --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print one line per album. album-stack refresh /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 --dry-run -v album-stack front /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : refresh: how many albums were scanned and changed, stacks and stacked photos, and per album its manifest; the others: the album and member acted on.

Derive media and location domain events from VFS mutations (long-running) changes things archive-bridge archive-bridge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; it runs until stopped, turning VFS mutations into media and location events.

Turn a written search into search filters (kinds, years, people and locations as subjects, an area, what the pictures show) reads only archive-parse [--rules] <query> Argument What it is <query> the search as written, a sentence or a few words. Option What it does --rules only the deterministic pass: years and kinds, no model and no name lookups. archive-parse 'Anna Andersson Göteborg 2019' archive-parse --rules 'filmer från 2010' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : text, kinds, from, to, people (with slug when one person), locations (a location node or an area), region, unresolved, source (llm or rules) and a one-line explain.

Match an image's detected faces to existing people, creating unnamed people for the rest. changes things assign-faces [--vote-threshold=<string>] [--attach-threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-create-confidence=<string>] [--min-create-size=<string>] [--no-create] [--reassign] [--allow-duplicate-person] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to the image file. Option What it does --vote-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --attach-threshold=<string> min winning vote weight to attach to a person (default 0.55) --margin=<string> winner must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) -k <string> neighbours to consider per face (default 24) --min-create-confidence=<string> min detection confidence to seed a new person (default 0.7) --min-create-size=<string> min face box side in px to seed a new person (default 48) --no-create attach only; never create an unnamed person. --reassign also re-decide faces a previous automatic run assigned. --allow-duplicate-person permit one person on two faces of the same image. --dry-run report without writing. --verbose print each face. assign-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg assign-faces --dry-run --no-create /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each detected face with the person it was matched to, the score, and whether a new unnamed person was created.

Match a recording's voices to existing people, creating unnamed people for the rest. changes things assign-speakers [--vote-threshold=<string>] [--attach-threshold=<string>] [--person-threshold=<string>] [--asd-person-threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-create-seconds=<string>] [--asd-vote-weight=<string>] [--asd-min-score=<string>] [--no-create] [--reassign] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to the audio or video file. Option What it does --vote-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --attach-threshold=<string> min winning vote weight to attach to a person (default 0.55) --person-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity to the mean of the winner's voices (default 0.7) --asd-person-threshold=<string> the same, for the person a confident lip-sync match names (default 0.5) --margin=<string> winner must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) -k <string> neighbours to consider per voice (default 24) --min-create-seconds=<string> min seconds a voice spoke in all to seed a new person (default 10) --asd-vote-weight=<string> weight of a lip-sync match, as a similarity (default 0.9) --asd-min-score=<string> ignore a lip-sync match weaker than this (default 0.6) --no-create attach only; never create an unnamed person. --reassign also re-decide voices a previous automatic run assigned. --dry-run report without writing. --verbose print each voice. assign-speakers /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV assign-speakers --dry-run /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each voice with the person it was matched to and the score.

Weigh media against the library albums they may belong in, as staging weighs its suggested groups, and write nothing. reads only auto-album-assign [--per=<string>] [--root=<path>] [--top=<string>] [--holdout] [--evidence] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... files, albums, suggested groups or directories to match. Option What it does --per=<string> what one subject is: each path (group, the default), each media file (file), or all of it (set) --root=<path> only albums under this directory (default /archive/albums) --top=<string> candidates per subject (default 3) --holdout weigh the albums holding the subjects' media as if those media were not in them. --evidence each candidate's evidence, beside its reasons. auto-album-assign /home/anna/staging/albums/inbox/2019-06-14 --evidence auto-album-assign /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0002.jpg --per set --top 5 auto-album-assign /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg --per file --holdout With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each subject's media, how many are dated, its candidate albums best first with how likely and why, how likely a new album is, the margin and how sure (AlbumMatchReport).

Show how the staging organizer would group the media at and under some paths (directories, albums or files) into suggested albums, writing nothing. reads only auto-album-cluster [--user=<string>] [--strategy=<string>] [--significance=<string>] [--home=<string>] [--members] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... directories (everything within), albums (their members) or files. Option What it does --user=<string> whose home and household count (default the staging area's owner, else you) --strategy=<string> how to group (events, folders, none; default the category's, else events) --significance=<string> how readily a day is a group of its own (fewer, normal, more; default the category's, else normal) --home=<string> home for every year, as lat,lng or a location path (default the residence each year, else the densest cell) --members list each group's member paths. auto-album-cluster /home/anna/staging/files/inbox auto-album-cluster /archive/albums/2019-lake --members --significance more With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutoAlbumClusterReport: the media read, the home each year, and the groups proposed, by kind.

Recognize untagged faces as existing people (label propagation) + optionally create unnamed people for leftover clusters. changes things cluster-faces [--threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [--min-votes=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-cluster=<string>] [--cluster-threshold=<string>] [--max-cluster=<string>] [--max-people=<string>] [--create-people] [--mutual] [--no-mutual] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --margin=<string> winning person must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) --min-votes=<string> min winning vote weight to assign (default 0.5) -k <string> nearest neighbours per face (default 8) --min-cluster=<string> min faces in a new-person cluster (default 3) --cluster-threshold=<string> stricter min similarity to group two untagged faces (default 0.6) --max-cluster=<string> skip clusters larger than this as likely chained (default 60) --max-people=<string> max unnamed people to create per run (default 500) --create-people create an unnamed person per leftover cluster (off by default) --mutual keep only mutual nearest-neighbour edges (on with --create-people) --no-mutual disable the mutual-neighbour filter. --dry-run report recognitions without writing personId. --verbose print each recognition. cluster-faces --create-people --min-cluster 4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many faces were recognised as existing people and how many clusters became new unnamed people.

Recognize untagged speech turns as existing people (label propagation) + optionally create unnamed people for leftover clusters. changes things cluster-voices [--threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [--min-votes=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-cluster=<string>] [--cluster-threshold=<string>] [--max-cluster=<string>] [--max-people=<string>] [--create-people] [--mutual] [--no-mutual] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --margin=<string> winning person must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) --min-votes=<string> min winning vote weight to assign (default 0.5) -k <string> nearest neighbours per turn (default 8) --min-cluster=<string> min turns in a new-speaker cluster (default 3) --cluster-threshold=<string> stricter min similarity to group two untagged turns (default 0.6) --max-cluster=<string> skip clusters larger than this as likely chained (default 60) --max-people=<string> max unnamed people to create per run (default 500) --create-people create an unnamed person per leftover cluster (off by default) --mutual keep only mutual nearest-neighbour edges (on with --create-people) --no-mutual disable the mutual-neighbour filter. --dry-run report recognitions without writing personId. --verbose print each recognition. cluster-voices --create-people --min-cluster 4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many speech turns were recognised and how many clusters became new unnamed people.

Compute the fingerprints that find copies of a media file: SSCD for pictures and video keyframes, chromaprint for sound. changes things compute-fingerprint [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force recompute even if already fingerprinted. compute-fingerprint /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the fingerprints are written under the file, and fingerprintedAt on it, and the duplicate findings they change are decided.

List media taken on a given day (MM-DD, default today) in past years. reads only dayinhistory [--years=<number>] [--per-year=<number>] <day> Argument What it is <day> day as MM-DD (default today) Option What it does --years=<number> years with media to collect, newest first (default 8) --per-year=<number> media kept per year, earliest first (default 4) dayinhistory dayinhistory 06-21 --years 20 --per-year 1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : monthDay, and the years that have media taken on that day, newest first, each with its first media.

Find a video's cuts and write them as its chapters (metadata/chapters) changes things detect-chapters [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a video file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Look again even if the chapters are found. detect-chapters /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_1978/files/sommarfilm.avi With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the chapters are written as WebVTT under the file, with the cuts on the node.

Detect faces in an image or a video and keep the usable ones as face regions. changes things detect-faces [-c <string>] [-f] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to an image or video file. Option What it does -c <string> Minimum confidence (default: CFG_FACE_MIN_CONFIDENCE, 0.7) -f Re-detect: drop previous face-* regions first (manual-* boxes are kept) -v Verbose output. detect-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg detect-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0012.MP4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each face found, with its box and the crop written under the file; on a video, one per person told apart, with when it is on screen.
Camera and recording device management. device <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand: create, info, update, list, match, scan, relink, set-owner, remove-owner, correct-time.

Give a device without a cover of its own its newest picture, or its newest video with thumbnails (coverPhoto softlink) changes things device-cover [--all] [--media] [--verbose] <device> Argument What it is <device> device path, or with --media a media file (repeatable) Option What it does --all every device. --media the paths are media files: cover the device each is linked to. --verbose print each device as its cover is written. device-cover /archive/devices/Canon_EOS_5D device-cover --all device-cover --media /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/clip.mp4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink to its newest picture (or video) is written for each device without a cover somebody chose.

Create a device node. changes things device-create [--name=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--serial=<string>] [--timezone=<string>] [--digitizer] [--quicktime-utc] [--description=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the device node (default: /archive/devices/ ) Option What it does --name=<string> display name (required) --make=<string> manufacturer, as exif writes it. --model=<string> model, as exif writes it. --serial=<string> serial number (the strong match key) --timezone=<string> IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Stockholm. --digitizer scanner whose device dates are digitisation times, not capture times. --quicktime-utc keeps its videos' QuickTime CreateDate in UTC (phones), not local time. --description=<string> free-text note.
Show device details and owners. reads only device-info <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to device node.

Link a file to its capture device using extracted exif, or to a device named by hand. changes things device-link [--device=<path>] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file; with --device, files or directories (repeatable) Option What it does --device=<path> link to this device instead of matching the exif (directories link the files directly in them) -v Verbose output.
List all devices. reads only device-list <root> Argument What it is <root> Device directory (default: /archive/devices)

Match a device by serial number or make/model. reads only device-match [--serial=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--root=<string>] Option What it does --serial=<string> Device serial number. --make=<string> Camera manufacturer. --model=<string> Camera model. --root=<string> Device directory (default: /archive/devices)

Link existing media to a registered device by its fingerprint. changes things device-relink [--all] [--force] [--dry-run] [--reapply] <device> Argument What it is <device> VFS path to device node (omit with --all) Option What it does --all sweep every registered device that has a fingerprint. --force relink files already claimed by another device. --dry-run report what would change without writing. --reapply link nothing; only re-date the files already linked (after a clock setting changed)

Unlink a person from a device (removes both halves) changes things device-remove-owner <device> <person> Argument What it is <device> VFS path to device node. <person> VFS path to person node, or the owner link name.
Propose devices seen in media but not registered. reads only device-scan [--limit=<string>] Option What it does --limit=<string> max proposals to report (default 100)

Link a person as owner of a device (dated relation pair) changes things device-set-owner [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--update] <device> <person> Argument What it is <device> VFS path to device node. <person> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --from=<string> ownership start date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --to=<string> ownership end date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --update rewrite the dates of an existing owner; an omitted date is cleared.

One device's history as a chronological feed: owners getting and giving it up, its events and the albums with photos it took. reads only device-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to device node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost. device-timeline /archive/devices/canon-eos With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the device's history in order: owners getting and giving it up, its events and the albums with photos it took.

Change a device's settings. changes things device-update [--name=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--serial=<string>] [--timezone=<string>] [--digitizer] [--quicktime-utc] [--description=<string>] [--clear=<string>] <device> Argument What it is <device> VFS path to device node. Option What it does --name=<string> display name. --make=<string> manufacturer, as exif writes it. --model=<string> model, as exif writes it. --serial=<string> serial number (the strong match key) --timezone=<string> IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Stockholm. --digitizer mark as a scanner and suppress its device dates on linked media. --quicktime-utc read its videos' QuickTime CreateDate as UTC (phones), not local time. --description=<string> free-text note. --clear=<string> remove a field (repeatable)

Find duplicate files by checksum (exact) or by fingerprint, copies with other bytes (--fuzzy); record the staged exact copies of files (--record), or look checksums up before an upload (--checksum) reads only duplicates [--fuzzy] [-t <string>] [-n <string>] [--min-count=<string>] [--min-size=<string>] [--against=<string>] [--record] [--checksum] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... file, subtree, or omit for the whole library; --record takes files and directories, --checksum checksums. Option What it does --fuzzy match fingerprints (resized, cropped, edited or rescanned copies) instead of checksums. -t <string> fuzzy similarity threshold (default 0.75 image / 0.80 video / 0.70 audio) -n <string> fuzzy: max results for a single file (default 20) --min-count=<string> exact: minimum copies to report a group (default 2) --min-size=<string> exact: ignore files smaller than this many bytes. --against=<string> exact: require copies in both the scoped subtree and this second root. --record decide again the duplicate findings of these staged files, of the staged copies of these library files, and of the files within these directories. --checksum the media originals you can read in the library or your own staging inbox that carry these checksums (at most 1000) duplicates /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 duplicates /home/anna/staging/files --against /archive/albums duplicates --fuzzy --min-count 2 /archive/albums duplicates --record /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg duplicates --checksum 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : groups of files that share a checksum, or with --fuzzy a fingerprint; --record: DuplicatesRecorded; --checksum: ChecksumMatches.

Embed a photo or a video's keyframes for search by what is in the picture. changes things embed-picture [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a photo or video file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Embed again even if already embedded. embed-picture /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the picture vectors are written under the file's metadata/picture.

Birthdays, memorials and wedding anniversaries around a date, as events entries (core events gathers them) reads only events-anniversaries [--days-ahead=<number>] [--days-past=<number>] [--limit=<number>] [--today=<string>] [--people=<path>] Option What it does --days-ahead=<number> how far forward to look (default 30) --days-past=<number> how far back to look (default 7) --limit=<number> anniversaries returned; milestones survive the cut (default 16) --today=<string> the date to look around, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, UTC) --people=<path> people root to read (default /archive/people) events-anniversaries events-anniversaries --days-ahead 0 --days-past 0 events-anniversaries --today 2026-12-24 --days-ahead 7 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each birthday, milestone memorial and wedding anniversary in the window as an events entry, in date order: the day, the sentence, whether it is a milestone, the person, and the route that draws it.

Extract EXIF metadata from file and create exif/position nodes; the file's paired sidecar ( /sidecar) dates and places it too, a staged file is dated by its category's time rules, and its exact copies among its inbox's files are recorded with it. A staged exact copy of a file its owner can read is recorded and not indexed (duplicate.deferred) unless forced. changes things exif-extract [-f] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to file. Option What it does -f Re-extract even when metadata/exif already exists, and index a staged exact copy. -v Verbose output. exif-extract /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; exif and position nodes are written under the file, and its duplicate finding on a staged file; for a deferred copy only that finding.

Extract metadata from a file, as exiftool reads it (through the media service) reads only exiftool [-n] <filename> Argument What it is <filename> VFS path to file. Option What it does -n Numeric values (always the case now; accepted for compatibility) exiftool /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the file's metadata exactly as exiftool reads it.

Add a human-drawn face box to an image or a video frame as a new unidentified person. changes things face-add [--box=<string>] [--at=<string>] [--no-crop] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to an image or a video file. Option What it does --box=<string> display-frame fractions: x,y,width,height. --at=<string> on a video, required: the second of the frame the box is drawn on. --no-crop create the crop node without rendering it. face-add --box 0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg face-add --box 0.4,0.1,0.2,0.3 --at 12.5 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0012.mp4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the new face and the unidentified person created for it.

Confirm that regions show the person they are assigned to. changes things face-confirm [--dry-run] <region>... Argument What it is <region>... region paths, /regions/ . Option What it does --dry-run check the regions without changing them. face-confirm /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the regions confirmed.

Question whether regions show the person they are assigned to. changes things face-doubt [--clear] [--dry-run] <region>... Argument What it is <region>... region paths, /regions/ . Option What it does --clear withdraw the doubt instead, leaving the person as it is. --dry-run check the regions without changing them. face-doubt /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 face-doubt --clear /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the regions marked, or with --clear the regions cleared.

Remove a face and its person when it was the person's only unidentified face. changes things face-remove <face> Argument What it is <face> VFS path to a region. face-remove /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the face is removed.

Undo automatic face→person assignments by provenance, leaving manual ones intact. changes things face-reset [--source=<string>] [--delete-unnamed] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --source=<string> auto | cluster | transfer | all (required) --delete-unnamed also delete every unnamed person. --dry-run report without changing anything. --verbose print each face. face-reset -- source cluster-faces --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many automatic assignments would be undone, by provenance.

Change a region's box and regenerate its preview crop; a moved face stops voting in recognition. changes things face-set-box [--box=<string>] [--no-crop] <face> Argument What it is <face> VFS path to a region. Option What it does --box=<string> display-frame fractions: x,y,width,height. --no-crop leave the crop bytes for regeneration. face-set-box --box 0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the box is changed and its crop regenerated.

Set a file's hand-written description. changes things file-set-description [--text=<string>] [--text-base64=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --text=<string> the description; empty clears it. --text-base64=<string> the description, base64-encoded (for multi-line text) file-set-description --text 'Ett exempel' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0042.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the description is written.

Rotate or mirror a file for good: writes angle/angleManual/mirror, remaps face boxes and regenerates renditions (a video re-encodes on the media pool) changes things file-set-orientation [--rotate=<string>] [--angle=<string>] [--mirror] [--toggle-mirror] [--no-regenerate] [-v] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --rotate=<string> relative turn: cw | ccw | 180. --angle=<string> absolute angle: 0 | 90 | 180 | 270. --mirror set the horizontal flip (--no-mirror clears it) --toggle-mirror flip the horizontal flip. --no-regenerate leave the still renditions and face crops stale (a video is still re-encoded on the media pool) -v verbose output. file-set-orientation --rotate 90 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the file is rotated for good and its renditions regenerated.

Link the person who took a file (photographer softlink) changes things file-set-photographer <file> <person> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. <person> VFS path to person node. file-set-photographer /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the photographer link is written.

Set a manual location override (positionManual + child position node) on a file, or clear its location. changes things file-set-position [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--clear] <file>... <lat> <lng> Argument What it is <file>... VFS paths to file nodes (several with --lat/--lng) <lat> latitude (positional; use --lat= if negative) <lng> longitude (positional; use --lng= if negative) Option What it does --lat=<string> latitude, as --lat= — required form for a negative coordinate. --lng=<string> longitude, as --lng= — required form for a negative coordinate. --clear take away the position and the location link instead of setting one. file-set-position /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg 59.0000 18.0000 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a manual location is written onto the file, or its location is taken away.

Write the text in a picture by hand, in place of what was read from it. changes things file-set-text [--text=<string>] [--text-base64=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a picture. Option What it does --text=<string> the text; empty removes it. --text-base64=<string> the text, base64-encoded (for multi-line text) file-set-text /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg --text 'Kära Anna' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the text is written and the picture is not read again.

Set the language the text in a picture is written in (or auto), and read the picture again in it. changes things file-set-text-language <file> <language> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a picture. <language> ISO 639-1 code (sv, en, de, …), or auto to tell it from the text. file-set-text-language /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg en file-set-text-language /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg auto With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the language is set and the picture read again on the media pool.

Set, annotate or clear a hand-typed capture time (whenManual) on one or more files. changes things file-set-time [--note=<string>] [--clear] <file> <when> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. <when> Capture time, YYYY[-MM[-DD[THH:MM[:SS]]]] (repeatable as file/time pairs) Option What it does --note=<string> Why this time is what it is — shown beside the date. --clear Remove the manual time and note, letting the exif-derived date win again. file-set-time /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg 2019-06-01T12:00 file-set-time --clear /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : FileSetTimeAnswer: each file with the capture time it now resolves to and its source.

Write what is said in a video or a recording by hand, in place of the transcript. changes things file-set-transcript [--vtt-base64=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a video or a recording. Option What it does --vtt-base64=<string> the transcript as WebVTT, base64-encoded; without it, WebVTT is read from stdin. cat /home/admin/rattad.vtt | file-set-transcript /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the transcript is written, searchable, and not transcribed again.

Find positions inside a geographic bounding box: media points and locations. reads only find-within [--north=<string>] [--south=<string>] [--east=<string>] [--west=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--cursor=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--cell=<string>] [--include-hits] [--covers] [--facets] [--dir=<string>] [--person=<string>] [--location=<string>] [--tag=<string>] [-q <string>] [--under=<path>] Option What it does --north=<string> north edge latitude. --south=<string> south edge latitude. --east=<string> east edge longitude. --west=<string> west edge longitude. --limit=<string> page size (default: 100; with --cell, max points scanned, default 200000) --cursor=<string> resume after this row, from a previous answer's cursor. --from=<string> taken at/after this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01) --to=<string> taken before this date, exclusive (--to 2000 includes all of 2000) --cell=<string> cluster media into a grid of this many degrees and report counts. --include-hits with --cell, include members when the filtered answer has at most 500 media. --covers with --cell, give each cell of several pictures one of them as its cover. --facets answer with per-day, per-month and per-year counts instead of contents. --dir=<string> which way to page from the cursor: desc, asc (default desc, back in time) --person=<string> only media this person is tagged in (slug or path) --location=<string> only media linked to this location (slug or path) --tag=<string> only media carrying this label. -q <string> only media matching this text, searched inside the box. --under=<path> only media in this album or folder, as members lists it.

Generate web derivatives (still pictures, transcoded renditions) for a media file. changes things generate-derivatives [-v] [-f] [--only=<string>] [--size=<string>] [--prune] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force regenerate even if derivatives exist. --only=<string> Generate one class only: still | transcode | storyboard. --size=<string> Generate only these sizes (comma-separated): thumb | grid | small | medium | large | face | preview | 1080p | storyboard | standard. --prune Delete renditions under thumbnails/ that are no longer targets. generate-derivatives /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg generate-derivatives --only still /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the thumbnail, display and transcode renditions are written.

Batch reverse geocode the position nodes of the files under a directory. changes things geocode-files [-r] [-f] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS directory path. Option What it does -r Recurse into subdirectories. -f Force re-geocode even if cached. -v Verbose output. geocode-files -r /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many position nodes were geocoded.

Resolve a location's written address to coordinates (Nominatim forward geocoding) changes things geocode-location [--force] [--dry-run] [--radius=<string>] [--countrycodes=<string>] [--query=<string>] [--verbose] [--accept=<number>] [--drawn] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a location (e.g. /archive/locations/ ) Option What it does --force Re-geocode even if already placed or attempted. --dry-run Report the query without calling the geocoder. --radius=<string> Radius in meters for the resulting circle (default 50) --countrycodes=<string> Restrict to these ISO country codes (default: se; empty to disable) --query=<string> Override the address text to look up. --verbose Print skipped locations too. --accept=<number> Take the geocoder's suggestion with this index (from the location's geocodeCandidates) instead of looking up; --radius sizes it. --drawn Record that the location's shape was drawn by hand, answering any pending review. geocode-location /archive/locations/Exempelstad geocode-location /archive/locations/Exempelstad --accept 0 --radius 150 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the coordinates the location's address resolved to.

Reverse geocode a file's position node using Nominatim (OSM) changes things geocode-position [-f] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a position node, /position. Option What it does -f Force re-geocode even if cached. -v Verbose output. geocode-position /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/position With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the address the coordinates resolved to.
Say hello (example TypeScript module command) reads only hello <name> Argument What it is <name> name to greet.

Extract text content and generate embedding for a document file. changes things index-document [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to document file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force reindex even if already indexed.

Learn labels from their pictures, so search --like /archive/tags/ can suggest where else they belong. reads only label-model [--all] [-v] [--if-stale] <subcommand> <label> <paths>... Argument What it is <subcommand> train | show | list | reject | unreject. <label> the label (train takes several) <paths>... reject, unreject: files or albums that are not the label. Option What it does --all train: every label in use, and every word of the vocabulary in the archive's language. -v train: report how long each phase took. --if-stale train: only labels whose members or rejections changed since they were trained, or that were trained more than a week ago. label-model train exempeletikett label-model train --all --if-stale label-model reject exempeletikett /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg search --like /archive/tags/exempeletikett --kind photo,video With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : for train , each label's LabelTrainResult; for show , the LabelModelSummary; for list , every kept model's LabelModelSummary; for reject and unreject , how many the label has rejected.

List the most recently captured media, newest first. reads only latest <count> Argument What it is <count> number of results (default 10, max 500) latest latest 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the most recently captured media, newest first, with capture time and dimensions.

Link geotagged media files to the location whose shape contains them ( /location softlink) changes things location-link-media [--location=<path>] [--point=<path>] [--root=<string>] [--dry-run] [--force] [--verbose] Option What it does --location=<path> only the files inside this location's shape, and those it no longer covers. --point=<path> only the file owning this /position node. --root=<string> media root to scan (default: /archive/albums) --dry-run report without creating or removing links. --force replace links made by hand or by the import too. --verbose print each link. location-link-media location-link-media --location /archive/locations/Exempelparken With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files were linked, unlinked, skipped and left outside every location.

List locations with their saved coordinates. reads only location-list [--without-coordinates] <root> Argument What it is <root> Location directory (default: /archive/locations) Option What it does --without-coordinates skip the position-registry scan.

Give a location coordinates from its linked media, falling back to geocoding its address. changes things location-locate [--all] [--root=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--min-points=<string>] [--max-spread=<string>] [--radius=<string>] [--no-geocode] [--force] [--refresh] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a location (e.g. /archive/locations/ ); omit with --all. Option What it does --all Process every location under --root. --root=<string> Locations root (default: /archive/locations) --limit=<string> Stop after this many locations. --min-points=<string> Fewest geotagged files a centroid may rest on (default 2) --max-spread=<string> Reject a centroid whose media spread wider than this, in meters (default 25000) --radius=<string> Fixed radius in meters, instead of one derived from the media spread. --no-geocode Centroid only — never fall back to the address geocoder. --force Re-locate locations that already have a shape. --refresh Re-derive a placed location too, writing only what moved; never touches coordinates set by hand. --dry-run Report what would be applied without writing anything. --verbose Print each location.
