Turn a location name (a city, a country, an area) into the region search --bbox filters on. reads only location-region [--countrycodes=<string>] [--bbox-only] <name>... Argument What it is <name>... the location as the user named it, in any language. Option What it does --countrycodes=<string> limit the match to these countries, comma-separated ISO codes (se,no) --bbox-only print only the box, for search --bbox=$(…) location-region Exempelstad search --bbox=$(location-region Exempelstad --bbox-only) --group-by album With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the location's full name and its bounding box as north,south,east,west — the form search --bbox= takes.

What happened at one location as a chronological feed: residents moving in and out, its events and the albums with photos from it. reads only location-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to location node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost. location-timeline /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the location's history in order: moves in and out, its events and the albums with photos taken there.

Change a location's name, address, description, city or country. changes things location-update [--name=<string>] [--address=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--city=<string>] [--country=<string>] [--clear=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to location node. Option What it does --name=<string> what the location is called. --address=<string> the written address; a change is geocoded again by location-upkeep. --description=<string> free text about the location. --city=<string> city. --country=<string> country. --clear=<string> remove a field (repeatable): address, description, city or country. location-update /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen --address 'Ekbacksvägen 4, 123 45 Exempelby' location-update /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen --clear description With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which fields changed.

Read description, time, location, location, device with owners, albums, tagged people (with age) and comments for a media file. reads only media-details [--album=<path>] [--fields=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --album=<path> album context for stack membership and exclusion details. --fields=<string> extra fields to include: raw (the full exiftool dump) media-details /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the file's description, when and where it was taken, its albums, and the people in it with their ages.

Embed the extracted texts, transcripts and hand-written descriptions already stored into the current text space, from the stored text alone. changes things media-reembed [-l <number>] [-f] [-v] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... files to embed the texts of (default: every text the archive holds) Option What it does -l <number> stop after this many texts or transcripts (default: all); a run resumes where the last stopped. -f embed again even what the current embedder already made. -v name each transcript as it is done. media-reembed media-reembed -l 5000 media-reembed /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0001.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many texts, transcripts and descriptions were embedded, skipped and failed; pass complete once nothing is left.

Re-resolve media originals' capture times from their stored exif and manual sources. changes things media-resolve-time [--dry-run] [--under=<path>] [--device=<path>] [-v] Option What it does --dry-run report what would change, write nothing. --under=<path> only the files in the tree under this directory or album, or this one file. --device=<path> only files linked to this device (its devicePath) -v print every file that changes. media-resolve-time --dry-run media-resolve-time --under /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 media-resolve-time --device /archive/devices/Exempelkamera --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files had their capture time re-resolved, and from which source.

Emit media events for files the bridge never saw (backfill / gap recovery) changes things media-scan [--limit=<number>] [--max-active=<number>] [--depth=<number>] [--scan-limit=<number>] [--restart] [--no-gaps] [--only=<string>] [-n] [-v] <root> Argument What it is <root> Subtree to scan (default /archive/albums) Option What it does --limit=<number> Maximum events to emit per run (default 1000) --max-active=<number> Cap running media-ingest instances plus queued triggers (default 500) --depth=<number> Maximum directory depth (default 12) --scan-limit=<number> Maximum files examined per run; 0 walks the whole subtree (default 20000) --restart Ignore the stored resume point and start the pass at the top. --no-gaps Only discover unindexed files; skip half-indexed ones. --only=<string> Emit only these fact types, comma-separated (e.g. media.picture.stale); the cursor still moves, so follow with a --restart pass for the rest. -n Dry run — report what would be emitted. -v Verbose output. media-scan /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 media-scan -- limit 500 /archive/albums media-scan --only media.picture.stale --scan-limit 0 /archive/albums With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files were announced to the media pipeline.

Pair the Google Photos Takeout JSON and XMP sidecars in a folder with their files, as /sidecar, and carry over their dates, places, captions and favourites. changes things media-sidecars [--dry-run] <folder> Argument What it is <folder> the folder whose sidecars are paired, at any depth; the working directory when none is given. Option What it does --dry-run count what would be paired and carried over, changing nothing. media-sidecars /home/anna/staging/files/google-photos/upload-2026-10-18 media-sidecars '/home/anna/staging/files/google-photos/Takeout/Google Photos/Sommar i Exempelstad' --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : MediaSidecarsAnswer: the sidecars found, paired, shared and unmatched, and what the files were given.

List an album's media by the album's own rules: an imported album's files/ folder, links followed, the cover left out, stacks of similar photos folded. reads only members-album [--include-stacked] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path. Option What it does --include-stacked text output: also list the photos folded under a stack. members-album /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 members-album /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 --include-stacked With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every member, stacked ones included: its path, node id, the link it is a member through, and for a stacked photo the front that stands for it and the stack size.

Keep one file of a set of duplicates, fill it in from the others, and move them to the trash as one batch. changes things merge-duplicates [--batch=<string>] [--label=<string>] [--dry-run] <keep> <drop>... Argument What it is <keep> the file kept. <drop>... the duplicates dropped into the trash. Option What it does --batch=<string> trash into this batch (an id from trash put --batch), or with no id a new one. --label=<string> what the batch is called in the trash. --dry-run say what would be filled in and trashed, changing nothing. merge-duplicates /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/IMG_0001.jpg merge-duplicates --label 'Copies of a sailboat' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0002.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/IMG_0002.jpg --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : MergeDuplicatesResult: the fields filled in, how many were trashed, and the batch that trash restore takes back.

Recently created albums, newest first, with who made them, as news entries (core news gathers them) reads only news-albums [--limit=<number>] [--preview=<number>] [--albums=<path>] Option What it does --limit=<number> albums returned (default 8) --preview=<number> pictures kept per album (default 5) --albums=<path> album root to read (default /archive/albums) news-albums news-albums -- limit 20 --preview 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the newest albums by creation time as news entries: when, who made it, a title, the album, and the route that draws it with the member count and a few pictures.

The years with pictures taken on a day (MM-DD, default today), as onthisday entries (core onthisday gathers them) reads only onthisday-media [--limit=<number>] <day> Argument What it is <day> day as MM-DD (default today, UTC) Option What it does --limit=<number> years returned, newest first (default 8) onthisday-media onthisday-media 06-21 -- limit 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : one onthisday entry per year with pictures taken on that day, newest year first: the year, a title, the year's first picture, and the route that draws it as a ring.

Score the search parse (archive-parse) against the filters each question means. reads only parse-eval [--questions=<path>] [--limit=<number>] Option What it does --questions=<path> a JSON array of {text, people, locations, from, to}. --limit=<number> stop after this many questions. parse-eval --questions /tmp/parse-questions.json With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : per question: people, locations and years right of those asked for, names made up, and the time; totals and p50/p90.

People and family tree management. person <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand: list, create, name, merge, detach, discard, unknown, faces, set-parent, set-partner, remove, add-event, info, children, family-tree, graph, timeline, how-related, check, fixup. person info /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person create /archive/people/Cecilia_Exempel --name 'Cecilia Exempel' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : whatever the subcommand answers with; 'person' alone lists the subcommands.

Add an event (blob) to a person, album, location or device. changes things person-add-event [--type=<string>] [--date=<string>] [--body=<string>] [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--writer=<path>] <target> <name> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to the person, album, location or device. <name> optional event name (e.g. birth, wedding); without one, it is made from the type and date. Option What it does --type=<string> event type: birth, death, marriage, engagement, generic; a dated birth/death also sets born/died. --date=<string> event date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --body=<string> event body text (markdown) --lat=<string> latitude for the event position node. --lng=<string> longitude for the event position node. --writer=<path> the person who wrote the text, linked as the event's writer ; without it, whoever adds the event. person-add-event -- date 1998-06 --body 'Flyttade till Lund' /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-add-event -- type marriage -- date 1972-05-20 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel wedding person-add-event -- date 2019-07-14 --body 'A day on the water' --writer /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the event path; the event is written, and for a dated birth/death the born/died attr.

Check family-tree integrity (dangling links, reciprocity, cycles, dates, birth/death events not on born/died) reads only person-check [--json=<string>] <root> Argument What it is <root> people root (default /people) Option What it does --json=<string> JSON output. person-check /archive/people With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every dangling link, missing reciprocal, cycle, impossible date and birth/death event not mirrored onto born/died it found.

List a person's children (children/ dir) reads only person-children <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. person-children /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each child's name and slug.

Give a named person without a cover the crop of one of their own faces (coverPhoto softlink) changes things person-cover [--all] [--file=<path>] [--repick] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every named person. --file=<path> the people whose faces are in this image. --repick choose again over a cover this command picked earlier; never over one somebody set. --limit=<number> stop after this many people. --verbose print each person as it is written. person-cover /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-cover --file /archive/media/2019/IMG_0001.jpg person-cover --all -- limit 50 person-cover --all --repick With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink to a face crop is written for each named person that had no usable cover.

Create a person node. changes things person-create [--name=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] [--allergies=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the person node. Option What it does --name=<string> , -n Display name. --fullname=<string> , -f Full name. --gender=<string> , -g Gender: male, female, other, unknown. --born=<string> , -b Birth date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --died=<string> , -d Death date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --allergies=<string> , -a Allergy notes. person-create /archive/people/Disa_Exempel --name 'Disa Exempel' --born 2019-01-01 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the person node is created.

Take faces off a person: to a new unnamed person, to an existing one, or off identity entirely. changes things person-detach [--to=<string>] [--to-new-person] [--rematch] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <facePath...> Argument What it is <facePath...> regions or voices, e.g. /albums/x.jpg/regions/face-0. Option What it does --to=<string> move the faces to this person (path or bare unknown id) --to-new-person mint one unnamed person and move the faces there. --rematch not this person: let recognition place each face again, never back on the person it left. --dry-run report what would move without changing anything. --verbose print each face. person-detach --rematch /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 person-detach --to-new-person /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which faces moved, and to whom, and the unnamed people left empty and removed.

Say unidentified people are not a person at all: unassign and lock everything they hold, and remove them. changes things person-discard [--dry-run] <person...> Argument What it is <person...> unnamed people, by path or bare unknown id. Option What it does --dry-run report what would go without changing anything. person-discard /archive/people/unknown/01J0EXAMPLE person-discard --dry-run 01J0EXAMPLE 01J0EXAMPLF With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the people removed, with how many regions and voices each let go, and the ones refused.

Every face and tag assigned to a person, with the photo each came from. reads only person-faces [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--doubtful] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path, or a bare id under /people/unknown. Option What it does --limit=<string> max faces to return (default: all as text, 500 as JSON) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --sort=<string> 'confidence' (default), 'file', chronological 'date', or 'doubt' (the ones a person asked about, then the clearest) --doubtful only the faces in question: questioned by somebody, or found looking like somebody else. person-faces /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-faces -- limit 20 -- sort date /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-faces --doubtful -- sort doubt /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the faces assigned to the person, with the photo each came from; JSON pages, and nextOffset starts the next page.

Display ancestors and descendants of a person. reads only person-family-tree [--up=<number>] [--down=<number>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --up=<number> ancestor generations (default 3) --down=<number> descendant generations (default 2) person-family-tree --up 2 --down 2 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's ancestors and descendants to the given depth.

Repair family-tree links (recreate missing reciprocals, rewrite stale reciprocal paths, drop dangling) changes things person-fixup [--dry-run=<string>] [--delete-orphans] <root> Argument What it is <root> people root (default /people) Option What it does --dry-run=<string> report without changing. --delete-orphans delete unnamed people left with no faces. person-fixup --dry-run /archive/people With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which family links would be recreated, rewritten or dropped; exits 1 when a person could not be repaired.

Family graph around a person as nodes and edges, for drawing a tree. reads only person-graph [--up=<number>] [--down=<number>] [--only=<path>] [--to=<path>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --up=<number> ancestor generations (default 2, max 8) --down=<number> descendant generations (default 2, max 8) --only=<path> draw only the person and these people, no walk (repeatable) --to=<path> draw the line of relations from the person to this one: how the two are related (repeatable) person-graph --up 2 --down 2 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-graph /archive/people/Anna_Exempel --only /archive/people/Bo_Exempel --only /archive/people/Cecilia_Exempel person-graph /archive/people/Anna_Exempel --to /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the family graph around the person as nodes and edges, for drawing.

Compute the kinship term between two persons (English/Swedish) reads only person-how-related [--lang=<string>] [--json] <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> first person. <b> second person. Option What it does --lang=<string> en|sv (default $CFG_LANGUAGE or en) --json JSON output. person-how-related /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/people/Bo_Exempel person-how-related --lang sv /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the kinship term in English and Swedish, as a sentence to repeat as it comes.

Show person details, relationships, and events. reads only person-info <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. person-info /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's name, birth and death dates, their parents, partners and children, and their events.

List the named people, with how many faces and voice turns each has. reads only person-list [--sort=<string>] [--limit=<number>] [--min=<number>] Option What it does --sort=<string> name (default; placeholder names last) or count (most pictured first) --limit=<number> at most this many people. --min=<number> only people with at least this many faces and voice turns. With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the named people with their face and voice counts, as JSON (PersonListEntry[]).

Merge people into another (faces, events, relations and links to them move; the sources are removed) changes things person-merge [--dry-run] [--force] [--verbose] <src...> <dst> Argument What it is <src...> people to merge away. <dst> person to keep. Option What it does --dry-run report what would move without changing anything. --force merge even if a source has children this cannot move. --verbose print detail. person-merge /archive/people/unnamed-1 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : what moved; with --dry-run, what would move.

Name an unidentified person and move them into /people. changes things person-name [--name=<string>] [--slug=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--birthname=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> path (or bare id) of an unnamed person. Option What it does --name=<string> display name (required) --slug=<string> path segment (default: derived from the name) --fullname=<string> full name. --birthname=<string> name at birth. --gender=<string> male, female, other, unknown. --born=<string> birth date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --died=<string> death date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) person-name --name 'Anna Exempel' --born 1970-01-01 /archive/people/unnamed-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the named person and their new path under /archive/people.

Who a kin phrase reaches from a person through the family tree: 'moster', 'mammas syster', 'barn', 'my father's brother'. reads only person-relatives [--relation=<string>] [--age=<number>] <person> Argument What it is <person> the person to start from: a VFS path, or a slug under the people root. Option What it does --relation=<string> kin word or chain in Swedish or English, as the user said it. --age=<number> also give the capture-date span in which each relative was this many years old. person-relatives /archive/people/Anna_Exempel --relation moster person-relatives Anna_Exempel --relation 'mammas syster' person-relatives Anna_Exempel --relation dotter --age 6 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each relative the phrase reaches, with their path, name, birth and death dates and what they are to the person in Swedish and English; with --age, the capture-date span to search in.

Remove a relationship between two persons (both sides) changes things person-remove <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> first person. <b> second person. person-remove /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the relation is removed from both sides.

Remove a person↔location residence relation (both halves) changes things person-remove-home <person> <location> Argument What it is <person> VFS path to person node. <location> VFS path to a location. person-remove-home /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/locations/Exempelstad With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the residence relation is removed from both sides.

Record where a person lived, and when (dated relation pair) changes things person-set-home [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--update] <person> <location> Argument What it is <person> VFS path to person node. <location> VFS path to a location. Option What it does --from=<string> moved in (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --to=<string> moved out (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --update rewrite the span of a residence that already exists; the flags given are the new span. person-set-home --from 2001-01 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/locations/Exempelstad With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the residence relation is written on both sides.

Add a parent relationship (parents/ ↔ children/) changes things person-set-parent [--kind=<string>] <child> <parent> Argument What it is <child> VFS path of the child person. <parent> VFS path of the parent person. Option What it does --kind=<string> blood (default) | adoptive | step | foster. person-set-parent /archive/people/Cecilia_Exempel /archive/people/Anna_Exempel person-set-parent --kind adoptive /archive/people/Disa_Exempel /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the link is written.

Add or update a partner relationship (partners/, both directions) changes things person-set-partner [--kind=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> VFS path of first person. <b> VFS path of second person. Option What it does --kind=<string> partner (default) | married. --from=<string> partnership start date. --to=<string> partnership end date. person-set-partner --kind married --from 2001-01-01 /archive/people/Anna_Exempel /archive/people/Bo_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the link is written in both directions.

Count births, engagements, marriages and deaths by calendar month across all years. reads only person-stats person-stats With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : months (twelve rows of counts per kind), totals, and withoutMonth for dates known only to the year.

One person's life as a chronological feed: events, homes, partnerships, children and albums. reads only person-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost — the life itself in a few round trips. person-timeline /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's life in order: events, homes, partnerships, children and the albums they appear in.

List auto-created people nobody has named yet, with face counts and crops. reads only person-unknown [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--faces=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--min-faces=<string>] [--person=<string>] Option What it does --limit=<string> max people to return (default 200) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --faces=<string> crops per person (default 4) --sort=<string> 'faces' (default) or 'created'. --min-faces=<string> only people with at least this many faces and recordings together. --person=<string> return one person by node id or path. person-unknown -- limit 20 -- sort faces person-unknown -- sort created --min-faces 5 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : auto-created people nobody has named, with their face counts and crops; JSON pages, and nextOffset starts the next page.

Change a person's profile: names, birth and death dates, gender, allergies, description, contact details. An empty value clears the field. changes things person-update [--name=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--birthname=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--allergies=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--contact=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> the person. Option What it does --name=<string> the name shown everywhere (cannot be empty) --fullname=<string> full name. --birthname=<string> name at birth. --born=<string> birth date, YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. --died=<string> death date, YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. --gender=<string> male, female, other or unknown. --allergies=<string> allergy notes. --description=<string> a few words about the person. --contact=<string> contact details as a JSON list of { "type", "data" }. person-update /archive/people/Anna_Andersson --born=1970-01-01 --died= '' person-update /archive/people/Anna_Andersson --contact '[{"type":"email","data":"anna@example.com"}]' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the fields given are written, empty ones cleared.

Every recording a person is heard in, with how long they speak and a moment to hear them. reads only person-voices [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--sort=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path, or a bare id under /people/unknown. Option What it does --limit=<string> max voices to return (default: all) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --sort=<string> 'duration' (most spoken first, default), 'file', or chronological 'date'. person-voices /archive/people/Anna_Exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every recording voice assigned to the person, with its talk time and the moment to play.

Copy width/height/duration from a file's exif node onto the file node. changes things promote-exif-attrs [-v] [-n] [--angle] [--codec] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a media file or a directory to walk. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -n Dry run — report what would be set, write nothing. --angle Also promote a video's container rotation to angle (never a still's, never over angleManual) --codec Also promote a video's picture codec to codec (the hint EMS skips its VRAM stage on) promote-exif-attrs /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; width, height and duration are copied from the exif node onto the file.

Detect RAW image files and report (or --sort) the non-RAW file(s) they are related to. reads only raw [--sort] [-n <string>] [--unmatched] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> file, subtree, or omit for the whole library. Option What it does --sort move each RAW under its partner’s versions/ dir (frozen version); RAW with no partner is left as is. -n <string> max partner candidates per file (default 5) --unmatched scan: list only RAW files with no partner found. -v verbose output. raw /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/DSC_0001.NEF With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the non-RAW files the RAW is related to.

Read the text written in a picture and keep it for search. changes things read-text [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a picture. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Read again even if already read.

Regenerate web derivatives for media files under a path. changes things regenerate [--force] [--prune] [--size=<string>] [--mime=<string>] [--verbose] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to file or directory. Option What it does --force , -f Force regenerate even if derivatives exist. --prune Delete renditions that are no longer part of the target set. --size=<string> , -s Generate only these size classes, comma-separated (e.g. small,medium) --mime=<string> Only files whose mimetype matches this glob (e.g. 'video/*') --verbose , -v Verbose output. regenerate /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 regenerate --force --size thumbnail /archive/albums With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files had their derivatives regenerated.

Re-encode a bounded, resumable batch of existing face crops without re-detecting faces. changes things regenerate-face-crops [--limit=<string>] [--after=<string>] [--file=<path>] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --limit=<string> maximum face nodes to scan (default 100) --after=<string> resume after the node id returned as nextAfter. --file=<path> restrict the batch to one source image. --dry-run report existing crops without rewriting them. --verbose print each crop considered. regenerate-face-crops -- limit 200 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many face crops were re-encoded, and where to resume.

Search albums by name, description and what their pictures show. reads only search-album [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--root=<string>] [--like=<path>] [--not-within=<path>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results per channel (default 10) --root=<string> Albums root (default: /archive/albums) --like=<path> albums whose pictures look like the label of this tag directory, by its model (label-model) --not-within=<path> leave the pictures under this directory out of what albums are scored by; may be given more than once (how search leaves out staging) search-album 'kalas' -l 10 search-album --like /archive/tags/exempeletikett -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching albums, one row per channel that found it (name, description, members), best first within each channel.

Search devices by name, make, model or serial number. reads only search-device [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--root=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results per channel (default 10) --root=<string> Devices root (default: /archive/devices) search-device 'exempelkamera' -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching devices, one row per channel that found it (name, description), best first within each.

Search documents (PDF, Word, text) by what their text is about, using semantic similarity. reads only search-document [--kinds] [--within=<path>] [--not-within=<path>] [-l <number>] <query> Argument What it is <query> what the documents should be about. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. --within=<path> rank only among the documents in this JSON array of file ids (what search writes) --not-within=<path> leave out the documents under this directory; may be given more than once (how search leaves out staging) -l <number> Max results (default 10) search-document 'ett protokoll från styrelsemötet' -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching documents, best first, each with its path and score.

Search locations by name. reads only search-location [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--root=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results (default 10) --root=<string> Locations root directory (default: /locations) search-location 'Exempelstad' -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching locations, best first.

Search media files by what they show, the text in them, what is said in them, their written descriptions and their names, or by likeness to a picture or a label. reads only search-media [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--within=<path>] [--not-within=<path>] [--like=<path>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text or keywords (none with --like) Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results per channel (default 10) --within=<path> rank only these files: a JSON array of file ids (how search narrows text to a person, location or album) --not-within=<path> leave out what lies under this directory; may be given more than once (how search leaves out the unlisted trees, such as staging) --like=<path> answer the picture channel only, by likeness to this photo or video: its stored picture vectors, or for a file without them (one put in /tmp) the embedder asked now; or to a label's tag directory, by its model (label-model), without what carries the label. search-media 'segelbåt' -l 10 search-media --like /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg -l 10 search-media --like /archive/tags/exempeletikett -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching media, one row per channel that found it, best first within each channel, with its path, channel and score on that channel's scale.

Search people by partial name; every query word must match the same person. reads only search-people [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--root=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results (default 10) --root=<string> People root directory (default: /people) search-people 'Anna Exempel' search-people -l 5 Anna With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching people, best first, each with a name, a slug and a score.

Search tracks by the name of the device that recorded them, or their description. reads only search-track [--kinds] [-l <number>] [--root=<string>] <query> Argument What it is <query> Search query text. Option What it does --kinds print the content kinds this provider can return, and exit. -l <number> Max results per channel (default 10) --root=<string> Devices root (default: /archive/devices) search-track 'exempeltur' -l 10 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : matching tracks, one row per channel that found it (name, description), best first within each.

Tie a video's voices to the faces seen speaking them, the video's own face regions first. changes things see-speakers [-v] <video> Argument What it is <video> VFS path to a voiceprinted video. Option What it does -v Verbose output. see-speakers /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; each voice's asdRegionId, asdPersonId and asdScore are written.

Manage a user's private staging area: its categories and which one a newly arrived folder looks like it belongs in, their suggested groups and the organizer that makes them, the edits that change them, and the decisions that file them into the library or discard them, each journaled and undoable. reads only staging [--user=<string>] [--all] [--stale] [--since=<string>] [--full] [--queue] [--if-pending] [--at=<path>] [--new] [--to=<string>] [--name=<string>] [--into=<path>] [--share=<string>] [--except=<path>] [--expect=<string>] [--confidence=<string>] [--action=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--cursor=<string>] [--refresh] [--force] [--repair] [--counts] [--where=<string>] [--keep=<string>] [--apply] [--off] [--exact] [--near] [--loose-batch=<string>] [--layout-only] [--idle-minutes=<string>] [--dry-run] [--create] [--remove] [--kind=<string>] [--label=<string>] [--destination=<path>] [--no-destination] [--strategy=<string>] [--significance=<string>] [--digitized=<string>] [--filename-dates=<string>] [--lane=<string>] [--sidecars=<string>] <subcommand> <path>... Argument What it is <subcommand> One of init , status , check , detect , category , retime , organize , promote , discard , accept , later , undo , journal , move , split , regroup , merge , delete , rename , pin , reject , match , dedupe , duplicates , separate . <path>... a category's name, or suggested groups by path or slug in the default category of --user, as required; detect takes at most 20 folders, of staging or not (by default the folders newly arrived in the default category); organize takes the categories to organize (every one by default); retime takes a category, or a folder or file of one (every category by default); discard also takes staged files and folders; accept takes at most 20 groups (50 with --dry-run), later 100; undo takes at most 20 journal entries; move takes what to move, then the folder; regroup takes the group, then the staged files to move into it (at most 2000), or with --new the files alone; merge takes the group to keep, then the groups to fold into it; rename takes the new name after it; reject takes the group, then the library album it does not go into; match takes groups (every group of the user's by default); duplicates takes a category, a folder of staged files (all of them by default), a suggested group, or staged files (at most 200) for the sets they belong to; dedupe takes the sets to resolve (exact: or near: ), with a category, a folder in one or a suggested group to drop their files from (the default category by default); separate takes a staged file, then the files it is no duplicate of. Option What it does --user=<string> act on this user (defaults to the current user) --all init, organize, match, duplicates --repair: act on every user (administrator only) --stale match: only the groups due a match: none for their members as they are, by another model, or older than a candidate profile. --since=<string> match: only the groups around the days of the library albums whose profile changed after this time. --full organize: plan the whole category again, not only what changed since the last run. --queue organize: ask for a run rather than run one; the organizer's pipeline runs it within minutes. A user may ask for their own categories. --if-pending organize --queue: only for a category something waits for: changes since its last run, edits, a first run, or a week since its last full build (administrator only) --at=<path> split: the first file of the new group. --new regroup: the files make a new group of their own. --to=<string> promote: the directory a new album is made in (default /archive/albums) --name=<string> promote: the new album's title, its path made from it (default the first group's name); split, regroup --new: the new group's name; merge: the kept group's new name. --into=<path> promote: file into this library album instead of a new one. --share=<string> promote: 'private' makes the new album yours alone; 'default' shares it as your new albums are. --except=<path> promote, discard: leave this member in its group, which is then pinned (repeatable) --expect=<string> promote, discard, accept, split, regroup, merge, delete: the member key each group must still have, in group order (repeatable) --confidence=<string> accept: the least sure proposal to apply (high, medium, low; default medium) --action=<string> journal: only decisions of this kind (promote, file, discard, dedupe, edit, reject) --limit=<string> journal: entries per page (default 50, at most 200); duplicates: sets per page (default 50, at most 200); duplicates --refresh: files announced per call (default 5000); dedupe --apply: copies dropped per call. --cursor=<string> journal, duplicates, duplicates --refresh, dedupe --apply: go on after this one's cursor. --refresh duplicates: announce each staged media file whose duplicate finding is missing, from another inbox or for other bytes, for media-duplicates to record; takes a folder of the user's staging files (default all of them) --force duplicates --refresh: announce every staged media file. --repair duplicates: check each duplicate finding against where its file is now, and fix it (with --all, every user's) --counts duplicates: how many staged copies the scope holds, by where their originals lie. --where=<string> duplicates, dedupe --apply: only copies or look-alikes of library photos (library), or of files within the inbox (inbox); both, in that order, by default. --keep=<string> dedupe: keep this staged file (its id) of the one set named, instead of the one the rules keep. --apply dedupe: resolve every set of the scope that resolves unasked, at most 500 sets and --limit copies (default and most 2000) a call. --off pin: unpin, so the organizer manages the group again; later: bring back into its lane; separate: no longer keep the files apart. --exact duplicates, dedupe --apply: only byte copies. --near duplicates, dedupe --apply: only look-alikes: the same picture in other bytes. --loose-batch=<string> init: the default category's folder that loose entries of files/ move into (default unsorted) --layout-only init: make the directories and categories only; move nothing. --idle-minutes=<string> init: leave the loose files of files/ changed within this many minutes, which may still be being copied. --dry-run init, organize, promote, discard, accept, dedupe, duplicates, retime --refresh: say what would be done, and do none of it. --create category: make it, with its directory of groups. --remove category: remove it, which only an empty one other than the default can be. --kind=<string> category: what it holds, which resets its other settings to the kind's (inbox, google-photos, scans, phone, camera, messaging, screenshots, generic) --label=<string> category: what a page calls it. --destination=<path> category: the library album its files are filed into by default. --no-destination category: no default album. --strategy=<string> category: how its files are grouped (events, folders, none): by time and place, by folder and file-name run, or into monthly lanes. --significance=<string> category: how readily a day becomes a group of its own rather than part of an Everyday lane (fewer, normal, more) --digitized=<string> category: on, its files are digitized copies (scans), and no clock recorded while digitizing them (device, GPS, file name) dates them;
