LGPL-3.0; BSD-2-Clause Dates, places, cameras: metadata ExifTool The same terms as Perl: Artistic or GPL Camera RAW files rawpy with LibRaw MIT; LGPL-2.1 or CDDL-1.0 Pictures for the models, HEIC included Pillow and pillow-heif MIT-CMU; BSD-3-Clause pillow-heif's binary wheels are GPL-2.0, as they bundle x265 Text of PDF files PyMuPDF AGPL-3.0 Text of Word and OpenDocument files python-docx and odfpy MIT; GPL-2.0 or later, or Apache-2.0 In the licence column, code comes before weights where a model has both; — means the media service runs the weights with no code of the model's own, through the libraries the models run on. These are under permissive licences: PyTorch under a BSD-style licence, ONNX Runtime and CTranslate2 under MIT, and transformers , sentence-transformers and OpenCV under Apache-2.0.

Four features rest on models whose terms allow no commercial use: Faces , in pictures and in videos, and with them the face seen speaking, since LR-ASD reads the faces InsightFace finds: InsightFace's models are for non-commercial research only. Who is speaking when : Sortformer's weights are under CC BY-NC 4.0. Finding text by meaning , in transcripts, read text and documents, and the assistant's command search: jina-embeddings-v5-text-small is under CC BY-NC 4.0. English handwriting : TrOCR large handwritten states no licence, and it is trained on the IAM database, whose terms allow non-commercial research only. The National Archives of Finland's transcriber, under Apache-2.0, is fine-tuned from it. No setting turns one of these features off, in EiN or in the media service: with the media service there, the Archive asks it for all of them. The one way to go without them is to go without the media service, with ./setup.sh --no-ems , and so without everything in What the media service does . The assistant's command search alone can leave the text vectors out: with CFG_TEXT_EMBEDDER empty, it matches words instead. Other licences in the table ask for attribution (CC BY 4.0) or set conditions on passing the software and its source on (GPL, LGPL, AGPL). Check each licence for what it asks of your installation.

The installer adds it with --ems , at the first install or any time after: On the machine EiN runs on, run: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein ./setup.sh --ems With the Archive not installed yet, add it in the same run: ./setup.sh --ems --module archive installs the media service, and the Archive with the ems module at EiN's start. Wait for the download. The first time, setup.sh prints == Getting the images (the media service the first time: about 30 GB) : the image carries every model, and downloading it takes a while and about 30 GB of disk. Installed from your own source, it is built on the machine instead, which takes about an hour more. Install EiN lists what the machine needs with the media service. setup.sh starts the containers and prints EiN is up at http://…:8080/ once EiN answers. Open Dashboard under System in the sidebar, and choose the Media service tab. For the first minutes the media service loads its models; the tab then shows the healthy badge. --ems writes EIN_EMS=1 to ~/ein/.env , so a later ./setup.sh keeps it. When setup.sh found an NVIDIA card with its CDI spec at the first install ( EIN_GPU=1 ), the media service gets the card; The graphics card explains how. To leave the media service out again, run ./setup.sh --no-ems . Its container stops and is removed; your files and everything already made from them stay.

In the standard install, both containers run on the same machine and only EiN talks to the media service, on the compose network. Nothing outside the machine reaches it. Three things connect them, all set up by setup.sh : What Where it is set Value The address CFG_EMS_URL for EiN, in compose.yaml http://ems:8181 The key EMS_KEY in .env , made at the install; EiN gets it as CFG_EMS_KEY 48 random hexadecimal characters The folders The same four folders under the data folder, mounted at the same paths in both containers see below Path in both containers What it holds The media service may /files your originals read /old older originals read /files-volatile the renditions read and write /files-tmp scratch space read and write Because a path means the same file on both sides, nothing is ever copied between them, and the media service can never change an original. It refuses any path outside these four. The key is a secret: no shell in EiN sees it, and the settings page never shows it once it is set. The media service accepts a request only with that key. Leave CFG_EMS_URL , EMS_KEY , EMS_PORT and EMS_ROOTS as setup.sh and the compose files set them; Configuration explains how a value set in the deployment relates to the settings page.

Open Dashboard under System and choose the Media service tab. It asks the media service how it is, again and again, while the tab is open. Media service : a badge, healthy , degraded or model worker down , and the facts: version , commit , api , uptime , batch worker and query worker ( up , or down , with × and the number of restarts), card , driver and url . Graphics card mode , when there is a card: who has the card now (see The graphics card below). An orange box for each degradation, such as gpu degraded , and a yellow one for each warning. Graphics card memory : the card's memory split by process, the media service's workers and everything outside EMS , and what is free; GPU load , Batch worker RAM and Query worker RAM . Models : every model the media service can load, loaded or not, with Status (for example GPU loaded or CPU loading ), Loaded , Last used , Size and Activity . Hover a model's name for what it does. The heading counts them: for example 3 of 15 loaded · 2 on the GPU . Executing : the requests running or waiting now, and the three lanes they go through, models , tools and encodes , each with how many run at once. When the media service does not answer, the tab shows only The media service is not answering , with the address it tried. The Overview tab shows GPU and VRAM tiles beside the computer's own CPU and memory when the media service has a card. With no card, or no media service, they are not there. The GPU and VRAM tiles are the media service's card; they show only when it has one About EiN in the account menu also has a Media service tile: its version, the API it speaks, its commit, how long it has been up and the card it runs on, or Not answering .

The dashboard's verdict and the health command read these checks about the media service: Check State When ems ok It answers: EMS <commit> answering, up <time> ems warn It does not answer: <address> is not answering; work that needs it waits ems worker warn the model worker is down; EMS starts it again ems gpu fail The card is meant to be there and is not, or the card stopped working ems card ok Who has the card, busy or quiet , and which search models are on it Only ems gpu fails, and a failed check turns the verdict to Needs a person . The others are warnings: while the media service restarts or loads its models, the work that needs it waits.

ems-status prints the whole answer the dashboard draws, and its options shorten it: # in EiN's terminal ems-status # everything: version, models, requests, card, memory ems-status --brief # one line, degradations first ems-status --checks # the checks above ems-gpu # the card now, with the last six hours ok ems EMS 3f9a2c1 answering, up 2.4h ok ems card quiet, search on it: text-query, siglip-text service-list --detail shows the same one line as ems-status --brief beside the ems-link service. When the media service does not answer, ems-status says ems-status: http://ems:8181 is not answering and exits with 1.

The media service is the ems service of compose: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose ps ems # or docker compose podman compose logs -f ems # what it says, as it says it podman compose restart ems Compose checks it every 30 seconds, and gives it 120 seconds to start before a failed check counts.

The media service uses an NVIDIA card when it has one, and the CPU otherwise. Without a card every model and every encoder still runs, only more slowly. Where each model runs is the media service's own decision, made each time it loads one; it changes how fast an answer comes, never what it is. A model that does not fit on the card runs on the CPU, except transcription and the handwriting readers, which wait for room on the card. With a card, the media service hands the card between indexing and search, and Graphics card mode on the Media service tab shows which has it: Mode What it means busy Indexing has the graphics card and search runs on the CPU, until no indexing work has come for a while. quiet No indexing work, so its models are unloaded and search runs on the graphics card, as far as it fits. switching Handing the graphics card over between indexing and search. off No graphics card to share: every model runs where its setting says. When the mode is off, which EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER=0 makes it too, the tab leaves Graphics card mode out. It turns quiet after 600 seconds without indexing work ( EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER ). A search never waits for the card: a separate model process answers searches on the CPU throughout. The graphics card covers preparing the machine, checking that every model really runs on the card, sharing the card with the language model and being told when the card goes missing .

The media service is configured by its environment alone. ~/ein/.env is that environment, so an EMS_ line there reaches it: Add or change the line in ~/ein/.env : # in ~/ein/.env EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES =sv,en Apply it: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose up -d Under podman-compose, a container that podman compose up -d makes again has no swap limit, so the media service's idle models may go to swap and a search waits for them; ./setup.sh makes the containers again with the limit. Any change restarts the media service, and EiN with it, since both read .env . Requests in flight fail and are retried; see When the media service restarts . These are the settings an administrator is most likely to need: Setting Default What it does EMS_MEMORY 16g The most memory the container may use. Compose reads it, not the media service. EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES empty The languages spoken in your recordings, as codes separated by commas, the most common first. Detection is biased towards them; empty lets detection alone decide. EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGE empty One language every recording is transcribed as; detection never runs. Right only when every recording is in that language. EMS_EXPECT_GPU empty 1 : the machine is meant to have a card, and the ems gpu check fails when none is visible. EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB 0 The most of the card the media service holds, in MB, for a card shared with the language model; 0 is all of it. EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER 600 Seconds without indexing work before search gets the card; 0 keeps search on the CPU. EMS_MODEL_IDLE_EVICT 21600 Seconds a model may sit unused before it is unloaded. EMS_MODEL_PINNED text-query Models loaded at start and never unloaded, separated by commas. The search models, text-query and siglip-text , are pinned in the query worker whatever this says. EMS_MODEL_MAX_RSS 0.6 of the container's memory The batch worker's memory ceiling, such as 10g . At the ceiling the worker finishes its requests and starts again; 0 turns the ceiling off. EMS_LIMIT_MODELS 8 Model requests admitted at once. EMS_LIMIT_TOOLS 4 Tool requests at once: metadata, thumbnails, fingerprints, document text. Each tool uses one core, so this is a number of cores. EMS_LIMIT_ENCODES 2 Transcodes and other whole-file decodes at once. EMS_QUEUE_DEPTH 64 Requests that may wait before a new one is answered busy . EMS_INTERACTIVE_RESERVE 1 Slots more for a request a person is waiting on, so a person never waits behind indexing. EMS_VIDEO_ENCODER empty The video encoder: empty picks av1_nvenc on a card that offers it and libsvtav1 otherwise. EMS_CPU_ENCODE_MAX_MB 4000 Memory one video decode on the CPU may grow to. A long video is encoded in pieces within it; one that cannot be is refused. 0 turns the CPU encode off. EMS_TOOL_STALL 900 Seconds a tool may go without using the CPU or moving a byte before it is stopped as stuck. Not a limit on how long it may take. Warning Leave EMS_WHISPER_MODEL as it is ( large-v3 ). It must match the model built into the image; another name makes the first transcription download one, or fail without a network. A change to the transcription settings changes what EMS reports as its transcript settings. With Keep transcripts current ( CFG_MEDIA_TRANSCRIPTS_CURRENT ) left on, the Archive then transcribes every video and recording again in the background, behind new media. On a large archive that is hours of work.

EiN's own settings for the media service are in the Media service and Transcription groups of Settings → System , with CFG_MODEL_SLOTS , the Archive's, in Processing . All can be set with config set : Setting Default What it does CFG_EMS_URL http://127.0.0.1:8181 ; the install sets http://ems:8181 Where the media service answers CFG_EMS_KEY none; the install sets it The key the media service expects CFG_EMS_CONNECT_RETRY 90 Seconds a background request keeps retrying while the media service refuses connections CFG_EMS_LINK_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 How often ems-link asks whether the media service answers CFG_WHISPER_LANGUAGE empty A language sent with every transcription; empty lets the media service decide CFG_WHISPER_VAD_MIN_SILENCE_MS empty The pause that ends a stretch of speech CFG_WHISPER_WORD_TIMESTAMPS empty 1 for the time of every word, 0 for timings per segment CFG_MODEL_SLOTS 2 Model requests the Archive keeps in flight against the media service at once For the languages of a family archive, prefer EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES in .env to CFG_WHISPER_LANGUAGE : the first biases detection, so a holiday clip in English is still transcribed as English; the second forces one language on everything. Processing pictures explains CFG_MODEL_SLOTS and the other slots.

A restart takes tens of seconds, longer when models load. Meanwhile: A background request that finds the connection refused tries again for up to CFG_EMS_CONNECT_RETRY seconds (90) before the step gives up for now. A step that cannot reach the media service, finds it busy , or finds a model still loading waits without using up an attempt, and runs again later. A request a person is waiting on, such as a search, does not wait: it fails at once. The ems-link service writes each change to its log, such as ems-link: down — not answering and ems-link: up — … . When the media service comes back with a different build, ems-link runs every failed pipeline instance again at once, since a new build is the likeliest fix for what failed under the old one. It logs ems-link: EMS <old> -> <new>; failed work runs again: … . Services and logs shows how to read that log.

./setup.sh without options downloads the newest images of EiN and of each service it runs, the media service included, and starts them again. Only the layers that changed are downloaded. Updating has the whole procedure.

The Media service tab says The media service is not answering. Look at the container: podman compose ps ems . If it is not running, podman compose logs ems says why; start it with podman compose up -d . If .env has EIN_EMS=0 , the media service is not installed: run ./setup.sh --ems . It answers, but the badge says model worker down. The model process stopped; the media service starts it again by itself. If it keeps stopping, the count after × beside batch worker climbs: podman compose logs ems says why. When it ran out of memory, give the container more with EMS_MEMORY in .env . gpu degraded and the verdict is Needs a person. The card the machine should have is not visible to the media service, or its context was lost. A reboot that renumbers the cards is the usual cause; The graphics card has the fix. A warning no keys configured: authentication is off . The media service got no key. Check that EMS_KEY is in ~/ein/.env , and run podman compose up -d . A warning no roots configured: every file request will be refused . EMS_ROOTS is empty. It is set in compose.ems.yaml ; undo a change to that file with git -C ~/ein checkout compose.ems.yaml and run podman compose up -d . Uploads stay being prepared for a long time. Look at Executing on the Media service tab. Requests waiting in the lanes mean the media service is busy: after a large import, the Dashboard reads Catching up until the work is done. With a card, a model shown as CPU loaded is several times slower than on the card; see Performance and sizing . The first transcription or face search after a quiet spell is slow. Models are unloaded after EMS_MODEL_IDLE_EVICT seconds unused, and loading one again takes tens of seconds. The Models table shows it as loading. The download or the build fails, or the disk fills. The media service's image is about 30 GB, and podman downloads or builds it in a folder beside its own storage, not in /tmp . Free space there and run ./setup.sh again. Troubleshooting covers problems that are not the media service's own.

This page is for whoever runs the media service or the assistant's language model on their own machine and wants them to use an NVIDIA graphics card: what the card speeds up, what the machine needs before EiN can reach it, how EiN is given the card, how to check that it uses it, and how the two share one card. It applies once the media service or the Assistant 's own language model is installed: it is the media service's page for the card, and also the one for the language model's use of it. Nothing in EiN needs a card; without one everything runs on the processor, more slowly.

p.h: What the card is used for
p.x: Two of EiN's optional services use the card. EiN itself and its database never do. Service What runs on the card The media service ( ems , the --ems option) The models for faces, voices, transcripts, text in pictures and handwriting, picture and text vectors; AV1 video encoding The language model ( llm , the --llm option) As many of the model's layers as fit in the part of the card left to it A card changes how fast the work is done, not what comes out of it, with one exception. Each model family is placed when the media service loads it: on the card when there is room, otherwise on the processor with the same weights. Transcripts are the exception: on a machine with a card, whisper always runs on the card and a transcription waits for room there rather than move to the processor; on a machine without one it runs on the processor, at about twice the length of the recording. The two give slightly different words, so a transcript never depends on what else happened to be on the card. The handwriting readers also wait for room on the card rather than move, since on the processor they are about ten times slower. Card Transcripts Everything else Language model 16 GB on the card on the card on the card 12 GB on the card on the card when there is room, or the processor partly on the card 8 GB on the card on the card when there is room, or the processor on the processor none on the processor, about 2x the recording on the processor on the processor A smaller card only makes the work slower: every output is made on any card or none. Video renditions are AV1. The media service encodes them on the card when the card and its build offer the av1_nvenc encoder, and on the processor otherwise; on a card without an AV1 encoder the attempt on the card fails and the processor encodes the video instead. EMS_VIDEO_ENCODER=libsvtav1 in ~/ein/.env keeps video encoding on the processor. Search uses the card too, when the media service has no indexing work: after 10 minutes without any, it unloads its indexing models and moves the search models onto the card, as far as they fit, and gives the card back to indexing as soon as work arrives. The Media service tab on the dashboard shows which of the two has it, under Check that EiN uses the card .

NVIDIA only. EiN uses no other make of card. Driver 610 or newer. The media service's ffmpeg needs it to encode video on the card. 16 GB of card memory is recommended : room for the media models and the language model side by side. Cards of 8 and 12 GB work, as the table above shows. A transcription needs about 4 GB of the card free. One card. When the machine has several, EiN hands all of them to both services; it is built and tried with one. The installer checks the card when you install with --ems or --llm . It reports the card with the most memory, and every graphics line is at most low , never missing : without a usable card the install goes on and the services run on the processor. graphics ok NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, 12282 MB, driver 610.31 card memory low 12282 MB: works; 16 GB is recommended, room for the media models and the assistant side by side container GPU ok nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.1, CDI spec in /var/run/cdi To run only the checks, without installing anything: # on the machine that will run EiN curl -fsSL https://einhq.eu/install.sh | EIN_CHECK=1 bash -s -- --ems --llm

The containers reach the card through CDI, the Container Device Interface: a file that describes the card's devices and libraries, which the container engine reads when a container asks for nvidia.com/gpu=all . These steps need root, once per machine and again after reinstalling its operating system. Install NVIDIA's driver, 610 or newer, from your distribution or from NVIDIA. Check it: # on the machine EiN runs on nvidia-smi It lists the card, its memory and the driver version. When it says it cannot reach the driver, fix that first: nothing below works without it. Install nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18 or newer, from NVIDIA's package repository. 1.18 is the first that ships nvidia-cdi-refresh.service , which writes the CDI file /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml from the devices the machine actually has, at every boot and whenever the driver or the toolkit changes. Check the version: # on the machine EiN runs on nvidia-ctk --version Turn the refresh on, and check that it wrote the file: # on the machine EiN runs on sudo systemctl enable --now nvidia-cdi-refresh.service ls -l /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml Remove any CDI file made by hand. Do not run nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/… yourself: such a file names the card numbers of the moment it was made, and podman falls back to it after a reboot has renumbered them. The installer warns about it with with a hand-made spec in /etc/cdi . Check your container engine: Engine What it needs podman podman 5 reads the CDI file as it is. Versions before 5, such as 4.9.3 in Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22, need the fix in the next section. Docker Docker Engine 28.2 or newer, where CDI is on by default. The installer checks both, and reports a podman before 5 that would reject the file, or a Docker before 28.2, as low on its container GPU line. Check that a container sees the card: # on the machine EiN runs on, as the user EiN runs as podman run -- rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all docker.io/library/debian:trixie-slim nvidia-smi -L With Docker, write docker run --rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all instead. It prints one line per card. When it fails with unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all , the engine cannot read the CDI file: see the next section.

p.h: Fix the CDI file for podman before 5
p.x: podman before 5, such as 4.9.3, rejects the CDI file as nvidia-ctk 1.17 and newer writes it, with unknown field "additionalGids" , and a container asking for nvidia.com/gpu=all then finds no card. The media service's repository has a script that makes every regeneration of the file readable to it, once per machine: Make sure the machine has Python's YAML library, which the fix uses. On Ubuntu and Mint: # on the machine EiN runs on sudo apt install python3-yaml Run the installer for the fix. After an install with --ems , the media service's sources are in ~/ein/src/ems : # on the machine EiN runs on sudo bash ~/ein/src/ems/deploy/install-cdi-refresh.sh Without the media service, fetch its repository first with git clone https://github.com/einhq/ems.git and run deploy/install-cdi-refresh.sh from there. The script copies the fix to /usr/local/sbin/ems-fix-cdi , adds it to nvidia-cdi-refresh.service as a step that runs after every regeneration, removes /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml if there is one, and regenerates the file at once. It ends with the service's status and a count of the cdiVersion , additionalGids and /dev/dri/card lines in /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml : after the fix, cdiVersion: 0.6.0 and no additionalGids . It keeps working across reboots and toolkit upgrades, and running it again does no harm. Then try the check in step 6 again.

The first setup.sh , the one the installer runs, looks for a card. When nvidia-smi works and a CDI file exists in /var/run/cdi or /etc/cdi , it writes EIN_GPU=1 into ~/ein/.env ; otherwise EIN_GPU=0 . From then on, every run of setup.sh gives the card to the media service and the language model, whichever of them you installed, by writing it into ~/ein/compose.override.yaml . Under podman, with both installed, the file reads: # Written by setup.sh from the options in .env and the container engine; edit those and run # setup.sh again. services: db: restart: always ein: environment: CFG_LLM_CARD: card restart: always ems: extends: { file: compose.ems.yaml , service: ems } devices: [ nvidia.com/gpu=all ] restart: always llm: extends: { file: compose.llm.yaml , service: llm } devices: [ nvidia.com/gpu=all ] restart: always Under Docker the restart: always lines are left out. CFG_LLM_CARD tells EiN where its own language model runs, card or cpu , so the chat and the health checks can say so ( setting ). setup.sh looks for the card only when it first writes .env . When you add a card, or prepare the machine, after EiN is installed, turn it on yourself: Open ~/ein/.env and set: # in ~/ein/.env EIN_GPU = 1 Run setup.sh , which writes compose.override.yaml again and starts the services with the card: # on the machine EiN runs on ~/ein/setup.sh It also downloads the newest images, as on any update ( Updating ). EIN_GPU=0 and ~/ein/setup.sh take the card away again. Do not edit compose.override.yaml by hand: setup.sh writes it again from .env every time it runs.

p.h: Check that EiN uses the card
p.x: Open Dashboard under System in the sidebar. The Overview tab has a GPU tile, with the card's use and temperature, and a VRAM tile, with the memory in use on it, each with the last six hours. Both are missing when the media service sees no card: no tile means no card, not an idle one. The GPU and VRAM tiles appear only when the media service sees a card The Media service tab shows more: Media service , at the top, names the card and its driver . Graphics card mode says who has the card now: busy while indexing has it and search runs on the processor, quiet when there is no indexing work and search runs on the card as far as it fits, switching while it is handed over. With no card to share, or with EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER=0 , the mode is off and the tab leaves this out. Graphics card memory splits the card's memory by process: the media service's batch, query and card workers, its other processes such as transcodes, and outside EMS , which is the language model when it shares the card. The list of models gives each copy its place, GPU or CPU , and whether it is loaded. The same is in EiN's terminal. ems-status shows every model and the device it is on, ems-status --checks the checks health reads, and ems-gpu the card's use and memory now: # in EiN's terminal ems-status --checks ems-gpu llm-status llm-status says whose the language model is and where it runs, such as http://llm:8190: ours, on the card ( reference ). It repeats what CFG_LLM_CARD says; how many layers the model really holds on the card is in its log ( podman compose logs llm ). To prove that every model really computes on the card, run the media service's self-test inside its container. It loads each model in turn and prints the device it bound to, ending with all GPU checks passed or a list of failures. It needs most of the card, so run it while the archive is not busy: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose exec ems python3 scripts/gpu_selftest.py --only with part of a check's name runs only the checks that match.

p.h: Share one card with the language model
p.x: With both --ems and --llm on one card, the two services split it by one number, set on both sides in ~/ein/.env : Variable Read by Default What it sets EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB the media service 0 The most of the card, in MB, the media service's processes hold. A model that would take it past this runs on the processor, even while the rest of the card is free. 0 is the whole card. LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB the language model 8800 How much of the card the language model leaves free when it starts. It takes as many layers as fit in the rest, and runs the others on the processor. Set the language model's reserve 400 MB above the media service's share: the language model counts the card as nvidia-smi does, and some 400 MB of that are never usable by the media service. The media service then never loads into the language model's part. The language model fits its layers when it starts, into what is free then less its reserve, so it gets all of them when it starts beside a media service that holds little, as when both start together; started again while the media service holds models, it gets fewer until its next start. setup.sh sets neither, so the media service may use the whole card while the language model leaves it 8800 MB; set both when the two share a card. On a 16 GB card, the pair EiN's own test machine runs with leaves the media service 9.7 GB, more than the 7.3 GB its busiest work has needed, and the language model the 6.2 GB that hold all of its layers: # in ~/ein/.env EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB = 9700 LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB = 10100 Apply it: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose up -d On a smaller card the language model gets fewer layers and answers more slowly; on an 8 GB card it runs on the processor. A language model at a hosted provider has no part of the card, so leave EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB at 0 and the media service uses all of it. The language model covers the model itself and the hosted alternative, and Performance and sizing how memory and processor are shared.

p.h: Be told when the card goes missing
p.x: After a reboot or a driver upgrade, a card can be lost to the containers: the media service then still runs, on the processor, and the work only gets slower. To have this show as a failure instead, tell the media service that the machine has a card: # in ~/ein/.env EMS_EXPECT_GPU = 1 Apply it with podman compose up -d . While the media service sees no card, the dashboard's health badge reads Needs a person , and health and ems-status --checks list: fail ems gpu this host is meant to have a card, and none is visible The same check fails, with the error, when the card's CUDA context is lost while the media service runs. Health and the dashboard explains the badge and the checks.

Without a card, or with EIN_GPU=0 , the media service and the language model run on the processor. Nothing else changes: every output is made, the same models are used, and transcripts are made on the processor at about twice the length of the recording. The media service then needs the processor and memory the installer asks for with --ems : 4 cores, 6 or more recommended, and 16 GB of memory, 32 GB recommended ( Install EiN ).

The commands are written for podman. With Docker, write docker compose where they say podman compose . What you see What to do The installer says no NVIDIA card: everything runs on the processor, more slowly The machine has no NVIDIA card, or the system does not list one. EiN works without it. The installer says an NVIDIA card is present but nvidia-smi cannot reach its driver The driver is missing or not loaded. Run nvidia-smi to see why; a reboot after installing the driver is often needed. The installer says 610 or newer is needed to encode video on the card Install a newer driver. Until then the models still use the card where they can; video is encoded on the processor. The installer says install nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18 or newer , or 1.18 or newer is needed Install or upgrade the toolkit ( Prepare the machine , step 2). The installer says but no CDI spec: sudo systemctl enable --now nvidia-cdi-refresh.service Run that command, then check that /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml exists. The installer says podman 4.9.3 rejects the CDI spec nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.1 writes (cdiVersion 0.7.0), so the containers find no card: … Apply the fix with the command the line ends with, or upgrade podman to 5 or newer. The installer says Docker 27.5.1 passes the card through its CDI spec from 28.2 on: update Docker Upgrade Docker Engine to 28.2 or newer. Starting fails with unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all The engine cannot read the CDI file. On podman before 5, apply the fix ; otherwise check that /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml exists. With Docker, check that it is Engine 28.2 or newer. The card is there but the dashboard has no GPU tile EIN_GPU in ~/ein/.env is 0 , most likely because the card or the toolkit came after the install. Give the card to EiN . After a reboot the media service does not start, or starts without the card A container keeps the device paths it was made with, and a reboot can renumber them. Make the containers again from the current CDI file: podman compose up -d --force-recreate . Models show CPU on the Media service tab while the card has room The card may be full at that moment, or held by the language model. Look at Graphics card memory , and set the share when the two use one card. The chat answers slowly on a machine with a card The language model got only some of its layers, or none. Its log, podman compose logs llm , says how many went to the card. Raise the part of the card it gets by lowering LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB and EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB together. A transcription waits for a long time On a machine with a card, whisper waits for about 4 GB of the card to be free rather than move to the processor. It goes on once other models are unloaded. Troubleshooting has more. The media service covers the media service beyond its card, and The language model the model beyond its card.

The commands the media service module adds. They are there once the module is installed. 4 of them, by name. Every command also says this with --help ; Commands explains how to read an entry. ems-gpu · ems-gpu-sample · ems-status · ems-text-embed

The media service's GPU now, with the last six hours of utilization and VRAM. reads only ems-gpu [--gauge] Option What it does --gauge The GPU and VRAM gauges top draws beside the host (the gpu-sampler service declares it) ems-gpu ems-gpu --gauge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : utilPct, memUsedMb, memTotalMb, tempC, vramPercent and the utilization and VRAM series, or null when there is no reading.

One reading of the media service's GPU: utilization, VRAM and temperature. reads only ems-gpu-sample ems-gpu-sample With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : utilPct, memUsedMb, memTotalMb and tempC, or null when there is no reading.

Show media service health: version, every model and its state, what is executing, degradation, worker memory and queues. reads only ems-status [--brief] [--checks] [--card] Option What it does --brief One line, degradation first (used by service-list --detail) --checks The checks health reads: answering, model worker, degradations, card. --card The card's mode alone: quiet, busy, switching or off; fails when EMS cannot say.

Texts as vectors, by EMS's current text model, to compare by meaning. reads only ems-text-embed [--role=<string>] [--timeout=<number>] [--model] <text>... Argument What it is <text>... the texts, one vector each. Option What it does --role=<string> query for what is searched with, document (the default) for what is searched. --timeout=<number> seconds to wait for EMS. --model the current text model alone, no vectors. ems-text-embed --role query 'restart a service' ems-text-embed --model With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : model, the model that made them, and vectors, one per text in order.
